#422. Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

📅 10 Nov 2026

Why Websites Show the Wrong Server Location When You Use a VPN

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/why-websites-show-wrong-server-location-when-you-use-vpn?utm_medium=RSS

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are many reasons why someone might use a vpn, but most often, it’s to conceal your real geographic location or prevent websites from tracking your online activity. It can also be a way to get around location-based restrictions that stop you from accessing certain websites or platforms.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you connect to a vpn server in the united states, websites are supposed to detect that your online traffic is originating from the u. S. traffic or circumvent regional censorship when travelling outside the U. S. S. That way, you can access online platforms that use IP filters to block non-U. But if you connect to a VPN server in the United States while you’re vacationing in Mexico, and a website thinks your IP address is from Brazil, that might not solve your problem and may even add unnecessary complications.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you’ve encountered something similar with your vpn provider, there are several fixes you can try. Depending on why your IP location is being misinterpreted, one of these should help you access the internet from the server location of your choice.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ip geolocation isn’t infallible. Websites rely on third-party IP databases to look up your location based on your current IP address. Maxmind, which has one of the largest such databases in existence, claims that its GeoIP products have a 99. 8% accuracy. Lesser-known providers with smaller IP databases may be far less accurate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, websites can also use more than just your ip address to estimate your location. For example, they can send WebRTC requests to your browser or directly query your device’s GPS. Moreover, VPN providers often have physical servers in one country while their IP addresses are registered to another country, and this discrepancy can also create issues. Let’s take a closer look at each of these problems individually, so you can find the fix that works best for you.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, webrtc is an open-source technology that lets your browser reduce latency when engaged in high-bandwidth tasks like streaming or video calls. Based on the IETF standard RFC 8828, it lets a website choose between your VPN server and your real IP address so it can establish the quickest path to transmit large amounts of data and reduce wait times or buffering.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the catch with webrtc is that it exposes both your vpn server and isp-assigned addresses to websites, which can reveal your real ip location and cause websites to reject your vpn server country. Firefox now comes with built-in protections to prevent WebRTC leaks, while Chrome and Edge support third-party extensions like WebRTC Control that you can use to eliminate these issues. To check if your browser is leaking your real IP address during WebRTC requests, you can use a free tool like BrowserLeaks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even when a browser isn’t leaking your real ip address, dns resolvers may fetch inaccurate location information if their nearest servers are too far from your current location. For example, a user in São Paulo may be geolocated to Chile when using Google Public DNS because that’s where Google’s nearest resolvers are located.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you toggle on dns leak protection in your vpn app, this will force websites to use your vpn’s resolver to perform dns lookups. That often solves the problem, but, again, you can confirm the fix worked through a service like BrowserLeaks or IPLeaks.

Sebagaimana diketahui, websites rely on ip databases like maxmind, ip2location, ipinfo, etc. to look up your exact location, but these databases get outdated quickly and need constant updating. Most of these databases also correct errors on request, but that takes some time. Also, each website has its own rules for how often it queries IP databases for updates.

Diungkapkan bahwa even when locations are updated in the actual database, a website may be sitting with outdated information unless it actively has refreshed it recently. MaxMind recommends doing this at least twice a week, but that’s ultimately up to the specific website.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, vpn providers often rely on virtual servers that use ip addresses registered in a different region than the server’s physical location. For example, ExpressVPN notes that it serves IP addresses in Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela through servers located physically in Brazil.

Diungkapkan bahwa while this is usually to help with the lack of local infrastructure or strict surveillance laws in the region, many databases and analytics tools will flag the discrepancy for websites, leading to confusion and inconsistency regarding your actual server location. In these cases, your best bet is to switch your VPN server or use a dedicated IP address by signing up for a paid add-on for your VPN.

Berdasarkan laporan, before investing in a specific solution, it’s better to do a thorough lookup to make sure why your ip address is pointing to the wrong location and whether a webrtc or dns issue, virtual servers, or something else is the cause. Here’s how I’d go about it, step by step:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’ll start by recording your baseline ip address, country, city, and asn. If you prefer using Terminal instead of your browser, you can also run curl ifconfig. With your VPN disconnected, navigate to IPConfig. co on your browser to grab your default IP details. I like this tool because it’s free and uses echoip to pull your location data straight from Maxmind. co/json to grab these details in plain text format.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, now connect your vpn server. Then visit IPConfig. co again to note down the changed details.

Berdasarkan laporan, make sure the country and timezone fields match your current vpn server location. Also make sure the ASN (organization) field does not list your home ISP.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in case these details do not match your vpn server, run a webrtc leak test and a dns leak test using browserleaks. If either of these tests doesn’t return your VPN server’s IP address, you’ve found your culprit.

If both the leak tests come back clean but a specific site still gets your location wrong, the issue is likely originating from an outdated database or virtual server.

Berdasarkan laporan, there’s no surefire way to solve ip location mismatches for good. But if it happens often enough to disrupt your internet use, you can consider switching to a different VPN server and getting a browser add-on that prevents WebRTC leaks. If that doesn’t work, I’d consider buying a dedicated IP address that isn’t based on a virtual server. While many IP databases like MaxMind or IP2Location also have ways to request a location correction, that takes a while to go through and isn’t worth the effort unless it’s a permanent IP address registered through your ISP.

#423. Apple to investigate accident that killed three workers at iPhone parts factory in India

📅 10 Nov 2026

Apple to investigate accident that killed three workers at iPhone parts factory in India

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/10/apple-to-investigate-accident-that-killed-three-workers-at-iphone-parts-factory-in-india/

Sebagaimana diketahui, reuters reports that three contract workers died after inhaling gas during an inspection at a tata electronics factory that produces iphone components in india. Here are the details.

As frequent 9to5Mac readers probably know, Apple’s supply chain in India relies heavily on Tata, which manufactures iPhone components and accounts for a significant share of the country’s iPhone assembly operations.

Since Apple began diversifying its manufacturing operations away from China, India has emerged as a major production hub, with roughly a quarter of the world’s iPhones now manufactured in the country.

Earlier this year, Apple found itself linked to an environmental controversy in India, after the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board investigated allegations that wastewater from a Tata facility had contaminated nearby farmland water.

A few weeks later, however, Tata said the regulator had dropped further action against the facility after the company addressed the concerns raised.

At the time, Tata said it had ordered separate testing related to the facility and that the results supported its position that the plant was operating within the rules.

However, the matter was apparently not fully resolved, as just three days later, Reuters reported that local health officials were still investigating complaints from nearby farmers.

And while there had been no major developments reported about the wastewater investigation since then, Reuters reported today that three contract workers died in an accident at the same Tata facility.

The three contract workers died during maintenance work on an effluent treatment ​plant operated by Nalco Water at the Tata facility, which is located in Hosur in Tamil Nadu, ​district official Dinesh Kumar said, adding that the deaths occurred when the workers inhaled gas while inspecting an external nano-filtration tank.

Reuters added that “Apple’s team is visiting ​the plant to assist in ​the ongoing investigation,” though the company did not respond when reached for comment.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the report added that tata and tamil nadu authorities are also investigating the fatal accident, and noted that “production was not affected as the facility was closed for the hindu festival of deepavali this week. ”.

To read Reuters’ full report, follow this link.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the holiday movie season is almost here, and there’s plenty to look forward to if you’re planning a trip to the theater. November and December 2026 are bringing some huge releases to the big screen, including the return of the Avengers in “Doomsday,” another trip to Arrakis in “Dune” and a new chapter in the “Hunger Games” franchise.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there’s also a festive horror sequel, a new adventure that brings a beloved video game to life outside its console, and a chilling medieval werewolf horror from “the witch” director robert eggers. Clearly, the coming weeks have plenty to offer. I’ve rounded up seven of the biggest movies hitting theaters this holiday season, so you can start planning your next cinema trip. Here’s what deserves a spot on your watchlist.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the hunger games: sunrise on the reaping” is easily one of the biggest movie releases to look forward to this month, thanks to the franchise’s huge fanbase and enduring popularity. Lionsgate moved quickly to bring Suzanne Collins’ latest novel to the big screen, announcing the film adaptation alongside the book in 2024. It marks the fifth film directed by Francis Lawrence in the dystopian series, bringing him back together with the creative team behind its distinctive cinematic style. The novel went on to become a major bestseller.

Sebagaimana diketahui, set 24 years before the events of the original film, “the hunger games: sunrise on the reaping” follows 16-year-old haymitch abernathy (joseph zada) as he prepares for the 50th annual hunger games. This year’s competition, known as the Second Quarter Quell, doubles the number of tributes sent into the arena. Living in District 12, Haymitch’s life changes when his name is selected during the Reaping, forcing him to leave behind his family and girlfriend, Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak). Alongside fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), Haymitch must fight to survive.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the hunger games: sunrise on the reaping" hits theaters on nov. 20.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the further mis-adventures of cliff booth” is an intriguing follow-up for fans of “once upon a time in hollywood,” with quentin tarantino returning to write the story and david fincher taking over directing duties. This time, the setting shifts away from the sun-soaked nostalgia of 1960s Hollywood towards a much darker 1970s crime backdrop. Fincher’s visual style should give the film a distinctly different feel with a much grittier atmosphere. It’s also a notable release for Netflix, which is giving the movie an IMAX-first theatrical run before it arrives on the streaming service over the holidays.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, set eight years after the events of “once upon a time “in hollywood,” the film follows former stuntman cliff booth (brad pitt). Having stepped away from stunt work, Cliff now earns a living as a bartender, using his unconventional skills to handle problems for the entertainment industry’s biggest names. When talent agent Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki) approaches him on behalf of television star Charlie Peters (Scott Caan), Cliff becomes involved in a complicated situation involving Charlie’s wife Toni (Carla Gugino) and two mysterious gangster brothers causing trouble across the city.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the further mis-adventures of cliff booth" hits theaters on nov. 25.

Diungkapkan bahwa for something with a much bloodier take on christmas, “violent night 2” should be on your radar next month. David Harbour returns as the hard-hitting Santa Claus, with Kristen Bell joining the cast for a new round of festive action. The sequel comes from the production company behind “Nobody 2” and “The Fall Guy,” so there’s good reason to expect plenty of inventive stuntwork and over-the-top fight scenes. Its reported influences include classic Spaghetti Westerns and traditional holiday movies, which sounds like an entertaining combination.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, santa claus (david harbour) returns for another christmas showdown when a ruthless gangster (jared harris) and his armed henchmen take over the silver bell mall. Diungkapkan bahwa “avengers: doomsday” is undoubtedly one of the biggest and most anticipated movies of the year, and i’m very curious to see what marvel has planned. ” As the 39th film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, there’s a lot riding on this one, particularly with Doctor Doom stepping into the spotlight as a major threat. I’m incredibly excited to see how it all unfolds, but also a little nervous about just how brutal Doom could be.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the avengers face their biggest challenge yet when a powerful new enemy threatens multiple universes. Led by Victor von Doom (Robert Downey Jr. As their worlds are set on a collision course, the unlikely allies must confront a threat capable of changing the fate of the multiverse. ), the looming crisis brings together heroes from across the Marvel universe, including the Avengers, Fantastic Four, X-Men and Wakandans. With familiar faces including Thor (Chris Hemsworth), Steve Rogers (Chris Evans), Shuri (Letitia Wright) and Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal), the heroes must find a way to stop Doom before it’s too late.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, another huge film releasing next month and competing on the same day with “doomsday” is “dune 3. ” Rather than simply serving as a traditional trilogy finale, Villeneuve has described the film as more of an epilogue to Paul Atreides’ story, bringing his journey to a close while taking the franchise in a new direction. ” Denis Villeneuve returns to direct what is expected to be the final chapter of his Arrakis saga, adapting Frank Herbert’s 1969 novel “Dune Messiah. With the previous two movies proving such huge cinematic events, this is easily one of the biggest releases over the holiday season.

Set several years after the events of part 2, the film follows Paul as he rules as Emperor, while facing growing opposition to his reign and the consequences of the religious movement that has spread across the universe in his name. Berdasarkan laporan, “jumanji: open world” brings the modern rebooted franchise to a close, reuniting audiences with its familiar mix of action, comedy and adventure. That means wild animals, chaotic stampedes and other game hazards spilling into everyday suburban and urban settings. The latest instalment looks set to shake up the formula by bringing the game’s dangers into the real world, rather than transporting its characters into a virtual jungle. It’s an interesting twist on the series’ familiar setup, and a promising way to wrap up this latest chapter of the “Jumanji” franchise.

Berdasarkan laporan, the group are reunited for another adventure when the jumanji video game unexpectedly escapes its console and spills into the real world. Smolder Bravestone (Dwayne Johnson), Ruby Roundhouse (Karen Gillan), Mouse Finbar (Kevin Hart) and Professor Shelly Oberon (Jack Black), find themselves roaming the streets in demo mode. As wild animals and dangerous creatures wreak havoc, the game’s familiar avatars, Dr. With the game threatening to turn everyday life upside down, the group must return to Jumanji and find a way to stop the chaos.

Diungkapkan bahwa "jumanji: open world" hits theaters on dec. 25.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of my most anticipated films of 2026 in general is “werwulf,” the period gothic folk-horror feature directed by robert eggers. It also reunites several familiar faces from his previous film, including Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Lily-Rose Depp, Willem Dafoe and Ralph Ineson. Following “Nosferatu,” the director is taking on another creature-focused story, this time set in a period setting with a folk-horror twist. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, set in 13th-century england, “werwulf” follows a mute medieval farmer (aaron taylor-johnson) who lives quietly with his family while hiding a terrifying secret: he transforms into a murderous werewolf whenever the full moon rises. When a hunting party arrives under the king’s orders to eliminate the wolves roaming the countryside, the farmer is forced to join them, putting his secret at risk. As the hunters search for the creature responsible for a series of attacks, he struggles to conceal his identity while protecting his wife and children from the growing danger.

#425. These are the 20 best books of 2026, according to Amazon editors

Diungkapkan bahwa amazon just dropped its best books of 2026 list. Earlier this year, the editors over at Amazon rounded up the best books of the year so far, but now that the year is nearly wrapped, the definitive list is here.

Berdasarkan laporan, "we saw people reach for sweeping family sagas, genre-bending fiction, gripping narrative nonfiction, and horror," says amazon editor al woodworth. The end-of-year list is packed with books across genres, and this year, the editors at Amazon even added two new best-of lists on horror and buzzworthy books.

Berdasarkan laporan, picking the top 20 books of the year is a big task. "At the end of the year, we look back at everything we've read and debate which books belong on the final list. Woodworth says that Amazon Editors are reading thousands of books every year, then championing the titles they can't stop thinking about. Every reader is different, so we recommend books from the widest possible selection," says Woodworth.

There are common themes across the top books of the year, including non-fiction that reads like fiction, stories of sacrificing for those they love, characters facing hard choices, and books the internet can't stop talking about.

But the best book of the year? Well, read on to find out which novel Woodworth and fellow Amazon Editors declared the best of the year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, earlier this year, amazon editor annabel gutterman spoke on night objects, saying: “this mesmerizing suspense novel about a teenager’s desperate search for belonging at her elite boarding school — where secrets swirl, and danger looms large — lived in my head for days. Eli Raphael introduces herself as a writer you don’t want to miss. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fans of alison bechdel's fun home will love the 2026 release the nightingales by emil wilson. This graphic novel is a touching picture of unlikely friendship between a 17-year-old girl and the dying stranger who moves into her family home. It's visually and emotionally striking, a graphic novel that's full of hope.

Diungkapkan bahwa the disappearers came out with a bang as the new york times declared it "the novel of the decade, if not the century. " It's a propulsive crime story that manages to be both harrowing and hilarious as it captures the gay experience in 1980s Jamaica.

Berdasarkan laporan, from gutterman: “when a tradwife influencer wakes up to discover it’s somehow the 19th century, her journey back to reality makes for a brilliant, biting novel about motherhood, fame, and faith. A reading experience like no other, this is the book I want to talk about with literally everyone I've ever met. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, from the author of shuggie bain, douglas stuart, comes a new novel, john of john. When John-Calum 'Cal' Macleod returns to his home on the Isle of Harris, it is not the place that has changed, but him. Sebagaimana diketahui, earlier this year, sarah gelman, amazon editorial director, said: "strangers is a divorce memoir, but it’s also a forensic examination of a love and a marriage gone wrong, seemingly without any warning. Burden puts words to many of our worst fears — that one day the person we love and trust the most will become an utter stranger to us. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa as a romance reader, there's one book i haven't stopped hearing about. But don't take it from me. Bad Words by Rioghnach Robinson is a will-they-won't-they romance of a novelist and the critic who panned his debut book. Emily Henry calls this novel a "once-in-a-lifetime read. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, as if releasing the hit film, teenage sex and death at camp miasma wasn't enough, director jane schoenbrun also released the novel public access afterworld. The debut is being heralded as one of the top books of the year as it delves into the surreal broadcasts of Public Access Afterworld, a pirate TV network with the potential to change lives.

Berdasarkan laporan, luna, phoenix, queen is an intricate novel, unraveling the relationship between two college professors and their resilient dog, luna. Julie Orringer's latest novel is a web of artistic and marital betrayal, and of all those tangled in that story.

an idempotent formatter, a rule-based linter and a language server for Scheme, Emacs Lisp and Common Lisp.

Diungkapkan bahwa sift reads a lisp source file, reports what is ill-formed in it, and rewrites its whitespace. The rewrite is a total function on text and a fixed point: formatting a formatted file returns it unchanged, and a comment, a blank line, a #; datum comment or a #. read-time form appears in the output in the place it was in the input. Both properties are asserted over every fixture in the suite, so neither is a promise that expires quietly.

Berdasarkan laporan, three dialects are read, each by the rules of its own report rather than by a compromise between them: scheme, emacs lisp and common lisp. A square bracket is a vector in one of them and a clause in the next, and sift does not average the two.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, check, format, lint. Lossless rewriting is the whole of the argument, and the rest follows from it: a diff whose hunks are the change, a fix that replaces one range, a rule that can be silenced without editing the code it objects to.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one decision carries most of the list: a lisp file is read as a tree of forms carrying source positions, not as lines of text, and the formatter prints that tree back. Preservation, a fix that replaces one range, and a diff whose hunks are the change all follow from it. That the reader and the printer are inverse operations is the oldest property Lisp has; the work here is to keep them inverse while the whitespace moves.

Nothing in format or in a checker knows about ports or exit codes. The module map, and what each module owns, is doc/development. org.

Berdasarkan laporan, six premises the code is measured against: a source file is a datum, not a string; a guarantee that is not a test expires quietly; the author decides what the code says and the tool decides where the whitespace goes; a dialect is a language, not a variant; state what can be decided and report no finding otherwise; and everything a program says should be available as data. doc/design. org states them, and then the decisions that follow from them – a reader of its own, one walk with the answers kept, fuzzy formatting rather than pretty-printing, and a YAML reader small enough to audit.

Berdasarkan laporan, sift itself does not expand macros, does not type-check, and does not know a project’s conventions. That is not modesty – a linter that decided would be useless on the first project it had never seen. Where the answer can be wrong, the rule says so: wrap-in-let is a suggestion, keyword-arguments counts, and the thresholds are settings. It reports; the author decides. The language server can ask the project’s own compiler for the checking sift does not do – on open and on save, in a thread, on a temporary copy of the buffer – and publishes what that compiler says about the names, the arity and the types it can see; compiler-diagnostics: false turns the second opinion off. The language server answers the requests listed on the language server page, and answers the others with “method not found” rather than a guess.

The list of Lisp dialects that deserve a better reader is long, and each item on it is a contribution that can be carried to the end:.

The project’s own style is the style it enforces, so it formats itself:.

Docstrings are Texinfo-flavoured (@var{}, @code{}), the first line is a sentence, and each paragraph states the reason as well as the rule – which is why this README can be read without a specification beside it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a commit message is a type and then a sentence: feat: for something that did not exist before, fix: for something that was wrong, and docs:, test:, refactor:, build:, ci: or chore: for the rest, scoped in parentheses when that narrows the subject (fix(lsp):, refactor(reader):). The reader who matters is the one scanning git log for the change that broke a build, and the type is what lets nine commits in ten be skipped unopened.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, patches arrive as a pull request on github or as a patch sent with git format-patch and git send-email, which is how the author usually works. The review concerns the code.

Sebagaimana diketahui, questions are equally welcome as issues. A question that the README does not answer is a defect in the README, and reporting it is the most useful bug report there is.

Berdasarkan laporan, sift is free software under the mit license; license carries the text. A short permissive license is a practical requirement rather than a sentiment: a formatter that spreads through other people’s pipelines cannot carry a licensing question with it.

Lisp, Scheme and Emacs Lisp formatter, linter and LSP (language server).

Diungkapkan bahwa oddly, these glasses are only compatible with certain devices—google pixel phones, samsung galaxy phones, and iphones—and only select models. 0 or higher, and the iPhone 13 Pro or newer. Gentle Monster's Intelligent Eyewear comes in six different styles.

Diungkapkan bahwa there's an accessibility feature called guided vision, which provides audio descriptions for people with impaired vision, like when reading fine print or locating everyday items. Berdasarkan laporan, to help demystify these features—and convince consumers that smart glasses aren't just a fad for tech bros—warby parker and gentle monster are both launching pop-up experiences in new york city this week. #432. High-Protein Packaged Foods May Not Be As Healthy As They Look

📅 10 Nov 2026

High-Protein Packaged Foods May Not Be As Healthy As They Look

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/is-added-protein-in-packaged-food-really-healthier?utm_medium=RSS

Sebagaimana diketahui, of the three major macronutrients—protein, carbs, and fat—protein has the best reputation, and it’s fairly well deserved. It also helps to make meals feel filling. We need significant amounts of protein in our diet, and nothing particularly bad happens if we get too much. Dietary protein helps you build muscle, and if you’re trying to lose weight it helps stop you from losing too much muscle along with the fat. Great! But.

Diungkapkan bahwa once the general public gets the idea that something is good for you, the companies that make packaged food start putting it in everything. So a lot of packaged food now boasts protein on the label. Or, they make products where the good-for-you thing features prominently on the label, whether or not there is very much inside. Here’s what you should ask yourself about those foods:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, take a close look here—sometimes a food will boast of a certain amount of protein per package but the package contains two or three servings. Other times, the protein per serving is correct, and we're supposed to be excited to have, say, 7 grams per serving. That's just not very much—and certainly not worth paying extra or choosing a less-delicious food just for those few added grams.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s good to know how much protein you need in your diet. (I've done the math for various body weights here. If you’re not gaining or losing weight, and not doing very much exercise, a 150-pound person only needs about 54 grams of protein a day. ) If you’re working out a lot, or if you’re trying to gain or lose weight (yep, either way), that same 150-pound person will need more like 81 to 95 grams of protein per day. More is OK, but not necessary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so if you’re trying to get 90 grams per day, 30 grams per meal is a reasonable amount to shoot for. Coincidentally, 30 grams is the amount of protein that tends to make a meal feel satisfying. You can do the math to figure out whether a protein-added product is going to be helpful in your day’s diet.

Diungkapkan bahwa i think this is the most important question about protein-added foods. It’s not hard to get protein in a meal; meats, dairy, tofu, beans, and grains all tend to supply plenty. So what is this protein-added thing you’re considering, and are you eating it instead of a traditional meal?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, here’s an example. If I’m heading straight from the gym to run some errands, and I need something to substitute for a meal—yeah, this isn’t great planning, but sometimes it happens—a protein bar with 20 grams of protein is a step in the right direction. Much better than a candy bar, anyway.

Berdasarkan laporan, but then there are things like this "protein mix" trail mix: 7 grams of protein with 200 calories. A double serving would be 400 calories and only 14 grams of protein. Hardly a great choice if your goal is just to add to your protein intake for the day.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and then there are the chips that my kid, for a time, couldn't stop eating. Are they better for him than the equivalent amount of Doritos? Arguably, sort of yes. But then he started arguing that since they have protein, he should be able to eat them in place of dinner. He loves Doritos and such; on a whim, we bought him some protein chips (yes, these are a real thing). We nixed that, but admit it: Are you having that same argument with yourself, feeling better about a snack food because it contains extra protein? If so, the marketing is working—you’re feeling good about your supposedly healthy choices, even though you’re just eating a bag of chips.

Keeping your calf muscles strong can benefit your body in many ways.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i didn't know until quite recently that your calves are known as the "second heart" because they help pump deoxygenated blood back up the body. Not only that, but they also play a role in absorbing force during lower-body movement and provide stability to your lower limbs.

I'm not great at sitting still, so during my working days at my desk, I am known to have a quick wander to quell restless legs, and recently I learned about an exercise called a soleus push-up.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i've been performing maximum reps every hour while seated during my workday, and i've noticed a few things so far. Read on to find out more.

A soleus push-up (SPU) is a seated calf raise exercise that targets the deeper calf, or soleus muscles.

Berdasarkan laporan, collectively, the soleus and gastrocnemius muscles form your calves and are referred to as a secondary heart. These muscles help pump blood toward the heart, squeezing the veins with contractions so oxygen-depleted blood travels up the body rather than pooling in your lower limbs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to keep circulation going, being as active as possible helps, including walking, running, or cycling. You may also find elevating your legs at times can be useful, especially after prolonged sitting. But if you don't fancy swinging your legs up onto your desk in the office, seated calf raises or soleus push-ups can help.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but before we get into what happened when i tried it every hour, every day, for one week during work, there's a study i think you should know about. Published in the Journal of Biomechanics, the research found that people with chronic heart failure had smaller calf muscles (namely, the deeper soleus muscle that helps us walk and stand) than people deemed "healthy" with "functional hearts. ".

Performing these muscular contractions seated can be useful for people who have desk jobs or want to limit fatigue and blood pressure issues.

Here's what happened when I tried the exercise every day.

Diungkapkan bahwa research found that people with chronic heart failure had smaller calf muscles (namely, the powerful soleus muscle that helps us walk and stand) than people deemed "healthy" with "functional hearts. ".

I have very mobile, clicky joints, and my ankles get both noisy and stiff if I don't move often enough, so adding as many reps as I could for 60 seconds per hour during my workday really helped.

I set eight alarms, one for every hour, and timed myself for 60 seconds, performing reps at my desk while still working.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when i got up to move around, particularly later in the week, i found my ankles felt more mobile and warmed up, and my calves felt less stiff. I recommend learning how to do calf raises, as well as trying some ankle mobility exercises and lower-body stretches alongside this move to ramp things up further.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, because the movement is driven from the lower limbs while seated, it's extremely accessible and low-impact, meaning most people don't even need to stop working while performing the soleus push-up. That also means you can go for high rep ranges while sitting at a desk.

The soleus muscles thrive on sustained periods of movement, so this makes it an ideal exercise to repeat during the week while keeping those muscle contractions going during seated periods.

Diungkapkan bahwa i added ankle weights to increase the intensity, and this is safe to do because there's no impact. I found it worked my muscles harder and, after stopping 60 seconds later, I felt like I'd been walking up a set of stairs. Add weights just above your knees for even more resistance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, marc hamilton pioneered the soleus push-up at the university of houston and published findings in the journal iscience, saying the exercise provides "optimal activation" and "elevates muscle metabolism for hours, even while sitting. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, he adds that the exercise helps sustain an "elevated local oxidative metabolism" which can improve blood glucose regulation by helping clear blood glucose from the bloodstream. Oxidative metabolism refers to a process where oxygen helps burn blood glucose or fats, depending on the energy needs of your working muscles.

Diungkapkan bahwa “no one ever investigated how to use it to optimize our health, until now,” says hamilton. “When activated correctly, the soleus muscle can raise local oxidative metabolism to high levels for hours, not just minutes, and does so by using a different fuel mixture. ”.

Of course, without a carefully controlled lab setting, I couldn't tell you if this made a difference for me or not.

I can be subject to swollen ankles and a little numbness in certain positions, a condition my musculoskeletal doctor hasn't been able to pinpoint just yet, so I was intrigued that soleus push-ups could boost circulation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a week later, although not life-changing, i have noticed less swelling and numbness while sitting. This makes sense, as your soleus muscle helps pump blood toward the heart.

Berdasarkan laporan, plus, as we age, calf strength can decline, which can have a knock-on impact on gait and balance during movement. By maintaining strong, healthy calves, I know I'm reducing the workload on my joints, namely my ankles and knees, which should benefit me heading into my later years.

Keeping them strong can make everyday activities feel easier, too, while also improving balance, ankle stability and overall lower-limb function.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so, according to science, these muscles protect your heart, aid circulation, help produce movement, and impact gait and balance. What more reason do you need to give this exercise a try the next time you're seated?.

#436. Talking Zen 6 with Mike Clark at AMD In-Depth

📅 11 Nov 2026

Talking Zen 6 with Mike Clark at AMD In-Depth

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://chipsandcheese.com/p/talking-zen-6-with-mike-clark-at

Hello you fine Internet folks,I sat down with AMD’s Mike Clark to talk about Zen 6, the evolution from Zen 5 and what some of the differences are between Zen 6 and Zen 6c and what drove some of those changes.

The transcript below has been edited for readability and conciseness.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: hello, you fine internet folks. We’re here at AMD In-Depth, where we’re talking about Venice. With me, I have a returning guest, Mike Clark. Would you like to tell the audience who you are?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: hi, i’m mike clark, the original architect of zen. Some people refer to me as “Zen Daddy. ” I’ve been working on cores here at AMD for 33 years, and we’ve got another great one coming, so I’m very proud of the design team I get to represent here today.

Diungkapkan bahwa george cozma: i’ve had some hands-on time with zen 6c. Let’s talk about the change that’s happened with Zen 6 and Zen 6c, what I refer to in my piece as the Zen 6 family. Why is it different from previous generations?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: right. Before, we were really just using the denser technology as an area play. And our dense technology is now our top-of-the-line, no-questions-asked performance core, because we’ve also enabled the full L3 in that implementation, at 4MB per core. So if you look more in-depth at what we have, what used to be our classic design, we now think of as our high-frequency design. Starting with Zen 4, we’ve been going through this evolution of having two core families. In this generation, having learned a lot, as we were filling out that denser version of the core, we wanted to leverage it to add some extra IPC within the core. So we have 32 of those cores, 128MB of L3, and the highest IPC you can get in that core.

Diungkapkan bahwa george cozma: awesome. So far, one thing I’ve noticed is that the vector scheduler is a bit bigger on Zen 6c. What was the reasoning for increasing that on Zen 6c?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mike clark: well, that wasn’t the only thing we increased. But because of its reduced frequency target, Zen 6c can have a little more capacity in the queues, since it doesn’t have to reach the maximum frequency the high-frequency core has to hit. We want them to have the same fit and feel, so the same optimizations apply to both. One principle we follow is that we don’t want to create a delta between the two architectures that software has to be optimized for. The floating-point scheduler is just one example. There are other queues throughout the core that are larger in Zen 6c, to pull out a little more IPC and get a little more leverage in that SMT environment as well.

Diungkapkan bahwa george cozma: interesting. Both Zen 6 and Zen 6c build on the design you had in Zen 5, and one of the interesting things with Zen 5 was the dual decode setup. Has the front end changed much to let a single thread make better use of both decode clusters?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mike clark: yes. But it gets quite complicated with one thread running larger-footprint workloads, where some of it might be hitting the I-cache and some of it might be hitting the op cache, and you’re trying to get everything synced up. As you said, Zen 5 was a new foundation, with the ability to fetch two basic blocks and get them down the line. So we spent a lot of time optimizing that and making it more efficient from both a delivery and a power perspective: less power wasted, and more efficient delivery from that new front end.

Berdasarkan laporan, george cozma: awesome. Going down into the execution engine, I also noticed that the number of integer multiply units has gone down from three to two. Could you talk a bit about what drove that choice?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mike clark: it really came out of the zen 5 design, where we had a more unified scheduler. To make a scheduler simpler, you want the units it schedules into to be very uniform, and the way we had set up those schedulers, adding a third multiplier to the group it was scheduling into was easy and didn’t add complication. In Zen 6, we realized that to really scale out the architecture, we needed to go back to more distributed schedulers, which now schedule into the ALUs. We hadn’t seen much uptick from that extra multiplier on Zen 5, so to optimize the area and the schedulers, we went back to two multipliers.

Diungkapkan bahwa george cozma: speaking of integer multiply, on the vector side you’ve added two more vnni units. What was the impetus for adding them, and at what point in the design did you add them?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: as i said in the talk, these are long design programs. So we were always focused on making the core good at AI. It’s not going to beat a GPU, and that’s not the point. But Zen 5 was a whole new foundation for AI workloads, and we’ve always believed the core has a place in AI: orchestration, data type manipulation, smaller models. When we started, no one was really even using that term. We weren’t designing Zen 6 to be an agentic core. We realized we probably should have some more VNNI, given where we were seeing inference go, and the team rallied around that. It was kind of late, since these are long-lead projects and the floor plan was set, but the team rallied, we were able to squeeze a couple more VNNI pipes in there, and it was a big success.

Berdasarkan laporan, george cozma: again on the vector side, one of the oddities of zen 5 was that although the wires were all there, the load unit could only do two vector loads at a time. What changed within the Zen 6 core to allow four vector loads, assuming they’re either 128 or 256 bits?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: we can do the 256-bit loads. Since we were able to do two 512-bit loads, we already had 1,024 wires headed over there. Obviously, using them piecemeal versus as one contiguous set complicates the design. I think it’s something we always wanted to do on Zen 5, but with all the change and getting it working, we left that for the Zen 6 team, and they were awesome. We’re all really one team at AMD anyway, and sometimes things intersect at different points in the roadmap. This was the time to do it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: speaking of bandwidth into the caches, the l2 in zen 5 had some oddities where it couldn’t always hit 64 bytes per cycle on reads. What changed in Zen 6 to allow that? Because I’ve been able to measure it, and it does hit that.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mike clark: honestly, sometimes you just don’t see some of these things. A lot of it was that we would be over-prefetching, and prefetches that hit in the L2 would be robbing L2 bandwidth. So we made sure we could sustain those prefetches alongside demand requests, reduce the conflicts, and deliver the full 64 bytes per cycle that we want.

Berdasarkan laporan, george cozma: awesome. What I also noticed, which is really neat, is that there wasn’t any reduction in accuracy. There seems to have been a reduction in branch misprediction latency, so when you miss a branch, the number of cycles it takes to recover has gone down. Circling all the way back to the front: the all-important branch predictor. So how did you pull off not only a faster branch predictor, but one that’s even slightly more accurate than Zen 5’s already very accurate predictor?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mike clark: the branch prediction team, as you know, is very algorithmic. And we’re always focused on our pipeline length. So each generation, we’re monomaniacally focused on getting going again as fast as we can when we’re wrong. It’s a great optimization problem: the number of TAGE tables, how much information they hold, accuracy. There’s lots of design space and lots of exploration, and AI has even been getting involved in helping us figure out how to optimize it. That was an area where we didn’t really want to grow; we thought we could be more efficient in the way we lay out the tables for prediction. There are lots of unique tricks we pull to get that redirect back into the front end and get it flowing as fast as possible. So we set out to make a more efficient one. No matter how good a branch predictor you build, there are always hard-to-predict branches, and you’re always going to mispredict. And you’ve observed it, which is great.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: yeah. Wrapping this all up and moving outside the core into the L3, there are obviously topology differences between the 12-core and 32-core CCDs. That’s very impressive, especially considering the clock deficit. I haven’t had time on Zen 6 yet, but I have had time on Zen 6c, and in SPECint 2026 it matches your fastest Zen 5 server CPU. How much were you able to mitigate those differences inside the core, building up structures to tolerate latency, to compensate for the slightly increased L3 latency?.

Berdasarkan laporan, mike clark: as i always talk about, the design has to be balanced. As we grow the capacity of a structure, the new technology helps it shrink, so the physical distance doesn’t grow linearly, but unfortunately the distance does grow. Inside the L3, there are a lot of tricks I can’t talk about.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mike clark: [in order to] maintain bandwidth within the l3 mesh so we can keep delivering to the cores. And in the cores, we do grow the queues to handle those higher latencies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: awesome. My penultimate question: Verano is adding LPDDR5X to the EPYC ecosystem. Were there any design considerations between LPDDR5X and DDR5 that you had to think about when designing the core?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mike clark: at the ccx level, we focus a lot on bandwidth per core. I think Mahesh talked a lot about the SDP ports, with 32-byte reads per port, so we try to make sure we have enough bandwidth between the CCD and the IOD. But we were already well provisioned for bandwidth with MRDIMMs, so that construction, the winglets and choosing a different memory technology, didn’t really have a major impact on how we built the core.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: awesome. Usually this is where I’d ask what your favorite type of cheese is, but since we already know that: have you tried any new cheeses lately?.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: i have. My new favorite is Cotija cheese.

Mike Clark: I’ve been eating a lot of tacos.

Diungkapkan bahwa mike clark: thanks for having me, george. I always look forward to coming and talking with you about what this awesome AMD CPU design team has created, and you always have so many good questions. I wish I could answer more, since we do have to protect our secret sauce, but I really enjoy helping you understand some of our thought processes, the challenges we face, and how we’ve been able to overcome them.

Berdasarkan laporan, george cozma: well, it’s always fun to sit down with you and talk, not just about what you’re doing, but also what the team is doing and what you’re looking forward to in the future. So thank you so much.

Sebagaimana diketahui, george cozma: i’ll see you in the next one. Have a good one, folks!.

#437. This Actively Exploited Chrome Vulnerability Is Putting Your Browser at Risk

📅 10 Nov 2026

This Actively Exploited Chrome Vulnerability Is Putting Your Browser at Risk

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/this-actively-exploited-security-vulnerability-is-putting-your-chrome-browser?utm_medium=RSS

Berdasarkan laporan, if you've seen an uptick in security updates as of late, you're not alone. Researchers and hackers alike are increasingly relying on these models in their individual pursuits: Hackers want to find these flaws to exploit them, while researchers want to block hackers from doing so. AI models have become very good at finding new security vulnerabilities throughout 2026. Microsoft's latest Patch Tuesday update included more than 1,400 patches; meanwhile, Apple's latest security update fixed two iMessage flaws that let both bad actors and innocent parties alike access texts they shouldn't.

Diungkapkan bahwa whether you use a mac or a pc, you probably browse the web with chrome, or a chromium-based browser. As it happens, Google's web browsing platform is the latest to receive an important security update—but it's far from the first important Chrome update of the year.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as reported by the hacker news, google released a new update for chrome on monday that patches nine security flaws. While all vulnerabilities are important to patch, one in particular is more serious than the rest: CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component.

Berdasarkan laporan, use-after-free vulnerabilities happen when the system frees up a memory location, but a program tries to access it anyway. It's a glitch in programming, but it offers bad actors an opportunity to break into your system. At worst, it allows arbitrary code execution, or, in other words, gives hackers the ability to run their own code in the app or system.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that's bad enough on the surface, but, unfortunately, google confirmed that cve-2026-125350 has an active exploit in the wild. The company is keeping other details close to the vest, but it's dangerous nonetheless. At least someone, somewhere, has used this flaw against a target, which puts all Chrome users (as well as users of Chromium-based browsers) at risk.

Berdasarkan laporan, what's more, this isn't chrome's first active exploit of the year—this is its eighth. The company is playing catch-up with hackers looking to target users of its browser, which makes sense, seeing as Chrome is by far the world's most popular browser.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you're using chrome on your computer, you'll want to update it as soon as possible. 0. 50 on Linux. 8103. 0. 51 on Mac or PC, or 157. 50/. 8103. Make sure you're running at least versions 157. To check, click the three dots in the top-right corner of your Chrome window, then go to More > Help > About Google Chrome.

Berdasarkan laporan, other chromium-based browsers may not have the update yet, but they are affected by this flaw. If you use browsers like Microsoft Edge, Opera, or Brave, keep an eye on your updates to install any of the latest patches.

#439. There’s a Good Reason the NYC Marathon Winners Wore These Watches

📅 10 Nov 2026

There’s a Good Reason the NYC Marathon Winners Wore These Watches

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/health/theres-a-good-reason-the-nyc-marathon-winners-wore-these-watches?utm_medium=RSS

Berdasarkan laporan, over 60,000 runners crossed the finish line at the new york city marathon last week. When you think of the elites fighting for a spot on the podium, you might expect to see only the priciest, most feature-packed GPS watches money can buy—historically, this meant the most premium Garmin Forerunners. Looking at the wrists of this year's New York City Marathon podium finishers, though,  you’ll see that Garmin—the name most recreational runners reach for by default—was far from the only brand on the course.

Here are the watches I’ve been able to confirm among the top NYC Marathon finishers:.

Men's winner, Andreas Almgren: Coros Pace 4 (sponsored).

Men's runner-up, Yemaneberhan Crippa: Amazfit Cheetah 2 Pro (sponsored).

Women's runner-up, Jessica McClain: Garmin Forerunner 570 (sponsored).

Women's third place, Hellen Obiri: Coros Pace 4 (sponsored).

Nonbinary winner, Ryan Montgomery: Suunto Race 3S (almost certainly sponsored, since this watch was released last month).

Diungkapkan bahwa an important disclaimer: i haven't spoken with any of these athletes. What follows is my opinion, based on what I know running watches offer the people who wear them.

Diungkapkan bahwa "garmin" has long been the default answer to "what running watch should i buy?" it earned that spot with reliable gps, excellent software, and a huge ecosystem. And on this podium, it's represented by a Forerunner 570—a great watch, but at a price tag most runners would struggle to justify.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, sponsorships muddy the water, since athletes wear what their sponsors put on their wrists. But that's exactly the point: Other brands are investing in elite runners because they believe their products can stand next to Garmin's, and it looks like they’re making the right bet.

Diungkapkan bahwa it's fair to ask whether garmin's grip is loosening. Is Garmin still the best running watch overall? For ecosystem, polish, and depth of features, it's still a strong contender. But "best" no longer means "the only serious option," and the gap between Garmin and the field is narrower than it has been in years. The Forerunner 570 starts north of $500. Meanwhile, COROS, Amazfit, and others are proving that a perfectly solid, competitive watch doesn't need to cost that much. The company has increasingly pushed toward the fanciest watches with the most features at higher and higher price points. Sponsored or not, seeing two Coros Pace 4s and an Amazfit Cheetah 2 Pro among the top finishers is worth noting.

Diungkapkan bahwa you don’t need an expensive watch to be elite—just look at the cheap running watches worn by the men who broke the sub-two-hour barrier at the london marathon this past spring. If you're shopping for a watch, spend your money on the basics being done right, and don't feel pressured to pay for features you'll never use. Training load scores, recovery metrics, maps, music, and smart notifications are nice, but they're extras. Everything besides your time and pace is icing on the cake.

Whichever brand you choose, focus on these basics in your running watch:.

Berdasarkan laporan, the new york city marathon podium shows a running-watch market that's a bit more competitive and intriguing than the era of "just buy a garmin" suggests. Garmin is still excellent, but now we’re seeing proof that Coros, Amazfit, and Suunto are all making watches good enough for the fastest humans on the planet. If they can trust those watches on their biggest days, the rest of us can probably trust them with our Saturday long runs.

Berdasarkan laporan, smart glasses have a public perception problem. People wearing Meta's popular Ray-Ban glasses have been labeled “Meta Creeps. ” But it didn't start with Meta—when Google Glass launched in 2013, “Glasshole” was the word used to describe people wearing them.

Diungkapkan bahwa it boils down to the fact that these smart glasses have cameras on them that let people record whatever’s in front of them with the push of a button. The cameras aren't easy to see, and while an indicator light activates when the glasses are recording, they're far less conspicuous than someone holding a smartphone up to record video or photos. It also doesn't help that people have tried to tamper with the LEDs and block them, and have recorded women without their consent.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but google is on a mission to change the perception of smart glasses as socially intrusive tech. The first Android XR Intelligent Eyewear smart glasses—made in collaboration with Samsung, Warby Parker, and Gentle Monster—are now available for preorder, with sales kicking off on December 10. You can read about how they work and what they can do in this separate story.

But you might be more interested in how Google is trying to separate its glasses from Meta's optics and positioning them as the more privacy-minded option to assuage public concerns.

Diungkapkan bahwa “there's this whole feature set of ai privacy that we think is super important,” says juston payne, google's senior director of product management for xr. They're decisions. “Ultimately, what we're trying to do here is say: Look, these are choices. These are, honestly, not hard technical problems. And we would like other companies to make different decisions, sort of like a bar-raising thing. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, all of the intelligent eyewear glasses have a power switch to turn them off completely, so you can wear them as regular glasses. They also have a recording light that illuminates when the glasses snap a photo or record a video, which is intentionally limited to 90 seconds for privacy purposes.

Here's a collection of the things Google says it's doing to make its smart glasses more private:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, payne hopes these policies and actions will encourage other companies to follow suit. “That should not have happened; hopefully it doesn't happen again. “We hope that never again do glasses launch from some other company that doesn't have good algorithms built in,” he says. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa privacy experts i spoke with acknowledged that google is trying not to repeat meta's mistakes, but they point out that smart glasses are still vehicles for collecting sensitive data. Even with an indicator light, it's harder to tell when someone's recording you in public than if someone is holding out their smartphone.

Diungkapkan bahwa reem suleiman, senior campaign director at the nonprofit digital rights advocacy group fight for the future, says camera-equipped glasses shouldn't be normalized in public because they are a precursor to mass surveillance and have the capacity to identify people. (This summer, Meta silently added a face-recognition code to its smart glasses and then subsequently deleted it after a WIRED report; in 2024, two Harvard students built a face-recognition tool for Meta's glasses. ).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “people find ways around it,” suleiman says. “There's no actual aspect of consent. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa janusz swierczynski, who researches human interactions with emerging tech at the university of oxford's saïd business school, tells wired these privacy measures are meaningful. However, they still largely address privacy at an individual level rather than thinking about people affected by them. That's partly because the technology is advancing faster than policy and research.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “a lot of privacy is managed by social norms, by what we think is acceptable to record, and that prevents people from recording anything and everything,” swierczynski says. “Normalizing recording does have unintended consequences, which is why it's important to focus on bystander privacy. ”.

Intriguingly, Payne highlighted that tech companies like Google need to make clear, declarative statements about what the glasses are doing.

Berdasarkan laporan, “ambiguity is not your friend here,” payne says. “I think that a lot of that concern came from some trust being broken. So there is a rebuilding thing happening right now … You can hopefully have your cake and eat it too, which is cool glasses that everybody's excited about—that you're comfortable with. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, picture the scene: you're mentally drained but can't fall asleep. Worse still, after you eventually do nod off, you find yourself wide awake at 3 a. m. , staring at the ceiling, unable to go back to sleep.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that was my reality for months until a sleep doctor explained that the coping mechanisms i was using to get through my days were likely contributing to my 3 a. Ana Casas, a longevity and internal medicine specialist, and Dr. wake-ups. m. Here Dr. Shelby Harris, a Board-Certified Clinical Psychologist at Better Sleep, explain what sleep pressure is and why it's crucial for dropping off and sleeping through the night.

Berdasarkan laporan, "think of sleep pressure as your brain’s natural hunger for sleep," explains dr. Casas, who co-authored the book Take Back Your Sleep: The Science-Based Strategy for Deep Sleep, Brain Longevity, and Peak Performance.

Berdasarkan laporan, "just as your body becomes hungrier the longer you go without food, your brain becomes hungrier for sleep the longer you stay awake. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "this is one of the two primary forces that regulate sleep, alongside our circadian rhythm, or internal body clock," adds dr. Harris.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "when sleep pressure is sufficiently high and aligned with our natural circadian rhythm, we are more likely to fall asleep easily, move through the appropriate stages of sleep, and stay asleep throughout the night. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa healthy adults clocking up between seven and nine hours of overall sleep should be spending 45 to 90 minutes in deep sleep, experts recommend. Deep sleep is hugely important for our overall energy levels and stress management. Here are the common mistakes experts said were robbing me of sleep pressure and, as a result, the amount of time I was spending in deep sleep:.

Berdasarkan laporan, one of the mistakes i've made when it comes to building sleep pressure is using mental exhaustion as an excuse not to incorporate movement into my day. "This doesn't mean you need an intense workout every day," says the sleep doctor. Harris, who notes that incorporating movement into the day supports healthy sleep patterns. The goal is to give your body enough activity and daytime stimulation to support restorative sleep at night. #448. Apple’s HomeView Tries Face Authentication Without FaceID

📅 12 Nov 2026

Apple’s HomeView Tries Face Authentication Without FaceID

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/apples-homeview-tries-face-authentication-without-faceid/

Diungkapkan bahwa apple’s homeview, which debuts on friday, is a smart home device—think of it as a an iphone-apple watch hybrid sitting on your counter—that can be personalized for up to six people and connected to each of their icloud accounts. You can ask HomeView about your schedule for the day and what movie your friend recommended in a text, but you’ll be stopped from asking about your roommate’s travel plans or her texts from last night. Using ambient face and voice data, it is designed to seamlessly switch between users while maintaining each of their privacy. The feature doesn’t rely on one of Apple’s battle-tested biometric locks, like FaceID or TouchID, though. Instead, it uses new “person recognition” technology built off of an Apple architecture for securing sensor data.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is a key departure for apple. On the one hand, the company has still been very careful to think about security and privacy comprehensively. Not only does HomeView check for your face and voice before accessing your data from iCloud, it is also designed like an Apple Watch to check that your iPhone or iPad is on the same Wi-Fi network as the HomeView and has been recently unlocked (with FaceID or a PIN). On the other hand, expanding the architecture used to process biometric data and authenticate users creates more opportunities for mistakes and potential vulnerabilities. And when it comes to attempting to access users’ Apple data, both law enforcement and exploit brokers consistently go to great lengths to attempt to break the company’s on-device defenses.

Berdasarkan laporan, faceid is built for the use case where a person is staring at their device head-on from less than an arm’s length away. It provides reliable security that’s difficult to defeat because it stores your biometric data on a special, physically isolated chip known as the Secure Enclave—first introduced in 2013 for the iPhone 5s. The architecture is so robust that Apple also relies on the Secure Enclave as the foundation of a device’s entire encryption scheme. But Apple concluded that FaceID wasn’t the best fit for the HomeView, because it needs to bounce quickly between users and relies on AI processing, which can’t all be squeezed into the Secure Enclave.

Berdasarkan laporan, as a result, homeview uses apple’s recently announced secure exclave (note the “x”) to handle the video and audio data the device uses to evaluate who is in a room at a given time. Apple says it has actually been laying the groundwork for the Secure Exclave for a long time—early versions of the architecture were already in place for the iPhone 16 and 17 and MacBook Neo. Instead of being an entirely separately chip, the Secure Exclave is a dedicated, memory-protected space in recent Apple processors. It is in Apple’s latest S11 chip for Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, as well as the A20 Pro chip for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even though the secure exclave isn’t based on the tried and true secure enclave technology, apple argues that it is robust and expands the company’s ability to secure a range of features, including improving the security of existing mechanisms. In a blog post on Thursday, the company even goes into some detail about how it used the mathematical technique known as formal verification to vet the “microkernel” designed for the Secure Exclave.

Berdasarkan laporan, “this work both benefits our newest features and strengthens the security of features we already ship, such as ‘hey siri’ detection,” the company writes in a blog post. “Our goal is to keep ambient sensor data secure even against highly sophisticated attacks. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, homeview also uses the secure exclave to govern the indicator light that tells users when their camera or microphone is active. The MacBook Neo uses the Exclave in this same way, though only to indicate when the camera is active, not the microphone. The goal is to isolate this process and the chain of command governing it to make it even more difficult for attackers to try to disable an indicator light when it should be on or stop it from coming on in the first place.

The HomeView’s “person recognition” technology is simply not as comprehensive as FaceID, though, and it is possible that the technology is more susceptible to reconstructed 3D depth map attacks—and potentially voiceprint attacks—than FaceID.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, you don’t have to have a homeview in your house. Or if you do, you can use it on guest mode or a less involved “personalized” mode that only incorporates things like your playlists for other users to access as well and doesn’t access calendar or Messages data. But as Apple forges deeper into AI integration, HomeView’s departure from FaceID provides insight into the scale of the changes Apple is planning.

Updated 11/12/2026 at 11:35 am ET to clarify when the MacBook Neo indicator light is verified by the Secure Exclave.

#449. New Apple TV 4K remote’s best feature requires a newer iPhone model

New Apple TV 4K remote’s best feature requires a newer iPhone model

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/10/new-apple-tv-4k-remotes-best-feature-requires-a-newer-iphone-model/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a new apple tv 4k releases this friday (pre-order here), with an upgraded siri remote. But the new remote’s best feature might not work on your iPhone.

If you’re interested in the new Apple TV 4K launching this week, or perhaps you just want to buy the upgraded Siri Remote separately (available here), there’s a key limitation you should know.

Precision Finding on the new Siri Remote requires an iPhone 17 or newer.

Diungkapkan bahwa the most common problem with the current siri remote is that it’s easy to lose. And once you lose it, Apple doesn’t offer many options for finding it. But that’s changing with the 4th gen Siri Remote.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you can use the new siri remote with any previous apple tv 4k or apple tv hd model. And if you do, you’ll benefit from the remote’s new built-in speaker that can be triggered from the Find My app.

Sebagaimana diketahui, joining the new speaker, the other main change with this latest siri remote is precision finding. If you’ve ever used the Find My app to track down a lost AirTag, you’ll probably be familiar with the feature.

Berdasarkan laporan, precision finding lets you get step-by-step, guided directions that take you directly to the lost siri remote. It’s a huge upgrade from the old tool for finding the remote—which mostly just told you that it’s in your house somewhere.

But Precision Finding relies on the Bluetooth 6 support found in iPhone 17 and 17 Pro models (not iPhone 17e), iPhone Air, iPhone Duo, and iPhone 18 Pro models.

So if you don’t have one of those iPhones, you’ll still benefit from the built-in speaker that lets you play a sound to find the lost remote, but Precision Finding won’t be available.

#450. Ring's New $250 Indoor Camera Drone Sounds Terrifying

📅 10 Nov 2026

Ring's New $250 Indoor Camera Drone Sounds Terrifying

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/rings-indoor-camera-drone-sounds-terrifying?utm_medium=RSS

Sebagaimana diketahui, ring made its name with its smart doorbells with built-in cameras, and now sells more indoor cameras than any other company, capturing more than 40% of the market. When you've already moved tens of millions of devices (enough to raise serious concerns about their use as part of the surveillance state), you always need to keep innovating, and today, the company announced a product it has been working on for a decade: an indoor camera drone powered by artificial intelligence. I got a chance to check it out during a media event yesterday, and I can report that, as harbingers of our dystopian future go, it is only mildly terrifying.

Diungkapkan bahwa the drone camera is one of two products in the company's new ring robotics line, alongside a "rover cam" that looks kind of like the canister of a vacuum cleaner attached to an ipad. While the Ring Rover Cam is priced at $999. 99 and targeted at businesses, the Ring Drone Cam is a much more affordable $249. 99, reasonable enough that it will appeal to consumers looking for another way to keep (robot) eyes on their stuff.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the drone camera records 2k video and has a 148-degree field of view and the ability to rotate 360 degrees. It works with existing Ring cameras, doorbells, sensors, and alarms, as well as the Alexa Home Map. It has a flight time of eight minutes, and once it returns to its base station, it takes around an hour to fully recharge (eight minutes on the dock will give it one minute in the air).

As Ring founder Jamie Siminoff explained during the preview event, the company has been trying to build a workable camera drone for around a decade, but couldn't overcome certain design challenges until the advancement of AI models that allow the device to handle most of the computing—from route programming to threat detection—via the cloud, so the drones can be smaller and lighter.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to ring, when setting up the ring drone cam, you carry it around your house, allowing it to map the interior. " When sent out on "patrol," the drone's AI pilot will travel between hotspots, sensing and avoiding furniture and other obstacles along the way. The Ring Drone Cam works with other Ring cameras, so if an alert is triggered somewhere in your home—say, a window opening unexpectedly—the drone will take off to investigate. It will "intelligently identify rooms and suggest patrol points: spots worth extra attention. It has a built-in security light that will make its presence known, so it can also act as a deterrent, though the screaming sound of its spinning propellers will accomplish that just as well.

According to Ring, the drone camera can deliver peace of mind whether you're home or away, and admittedly I do like the idea of being able to check on my pets or make sure no pipes have burst while I'm at work or on vacation (though admittedly you can get the same sort of monitoring without involving an AI device that looks like a mini version of the flying robots from The Terminator).

Berdasarkan laporan, i admit that the ring drone cam seems pretty cool, provided i don't think about it too much. I don't know that I really feel the need to have every inch of my home covered in security cameras, but I do like the idea that the drone could, for example, go to check out what's going on if one of my smoke alarms' temperature sensors reports that one spot in the house is all of a sudden hotter than it should be.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but there's something slightly unsettling to me about the idea of a robot patrolling my home while i sleep. (This is probably why I don't own a robot vacuum. ) And it doesn't help that the drone sounds absolutely terrifying, which Ring claims is by design: "If someone’s there who shouldn’t be, a flying drone overhead. (Note that the drone we were shown was white, but the final version sold will be dark grey. [The] devices are built to deter, not just monitor. makes it clear they’ve been spotted. " True enough, but there's also no getting around the fact that drone propellers are unavoidably loud, and the sound of the Ring Drone Cam reminds me of nothing more than the screeching violins in a horror movie. Yes, I know that there are privacy and security features in place—Ring says the videos its robots capture are protected by its "strongest default encryption yet"—but it's also yet one more example of how comfortable we've all gotten with cameras being absolutely everywhere, to the point that people think nothing of putting them all over their homes. ).

If you're ready to enter this brave new world of security, you'll have to wait a bit longer: The Ring Drone Camera isn't expected to ship until January 2027, but you can sign up to be alerted when it is available for preorder now.
