Sebagaimana diketahui, waze is a crowdsourced navigation app designed to help you get where you're going as quickly and with as much information about your route as possible. Where Google Maps and Apple Maps offer relatively straightforward directions, Waze tries to outsmart these alternatives by integrating real-time community feedback about hazards, speed traps, road closures, and more. If you are switching to Waze or using it alongside your other navigation tools, these are the hacks to help you maximize everything the app has to offer.

Berdasarkan laporan, if you find yourself losing track of time or running late for events, waze can notify you when it's time to leave—based on your current location and live traffic—so you arrive on schedule. Calendar sync connects to your device's default calendar app, but you can change this to a third-party alternative if you prefer. You can set up "Time to leave" reminders in advance for individual planned drives, or you can sync your calendar to receive notifications for scheduled events. Calendar events must include a navigable address to trigger reminders, and you must select Plan a drive in Waze for the event.

Diungkapkan bahwa waze has a feature called "child reminders," which are notifications to check for children before you get out of the car. This is clearly an incredibly important use case, but you can also use these alerts for custom messages, like "Don't forget the groceries!" In Waze, tap the menu button > Settings > Reminders > Child reminder and select Custom message.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, variable speed limits, especially on unfamiliar routes, can result in you speeding when you don't mean to. But Waze can alert you if you exceed a customized speed threshold so you aren't caught by surprise or at higher risk of being ticketed. From the menu, go to Settings > Speedometer and turn on Show speedometer. Tap Speeding threshold to select what limit you want to trigger alerts, and turn on Alert at threshold if you want Waze to play a sound.

Sebagaimana diketahui, waze offers a wealth of information on routes to help drivers navigate obstacles and hazards, but this can clutter your map and distract you from the most critical information, especially in congested, high-traffic areas. Waze says it limits and prioritizes alerts automatically, but you can actually customize which alerts you see based on what's most important to you. From the menu, go to Settings > Alerts and reports > Reports and select the relevant alerts.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the same alerts and reports menu, you can enable alert while driving, which will give you an audio warning and an onscreen pop-up about your selected hazards. This allows you to run navigation via a different map app (like Google Maps or Apple Maps) in the foreground while still getting Waze data in the background.

Diungkapkan bahwa waze integrates with toll road and hov lane passes, so if you have an express or fast lane subscription, your route will optimize for it. If you don't, Waze can still account for HOV lane eligibility if you tell it how many passengers are in your car. From the menu, go to Settings > Toll and HOV passes and tap the plus icon to add your pass(es) from the list. If you need to add your passenger count instead, you can do so from View routes and enable the HOV option.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you're driving through an unfamiliar, highly congested, or poorly designed area, you can ask waze to help you avoid tricky maneuvers, such as crossing multiple lanes of traffic or turning left at intersections without lights. This prioritizes ease over speed using protected green arrows, roundabouts, and right turns. From the menu, go to Settings > Navigation, Avoid difficult intersections and select Always. You can also ask Waze to avoid toll roads, ferries, freeways, and unpaved roads.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, waze has a built-in audio player that syncs with your preferred listening platform—such as spotify, youtube music, and pandora—so you can control your music without having to navigate between apps. (As Waze is a Google product, Apple Music isn't included. ) Simply tap the music icon on the map to select your audio player and hit Accept. If you don't see the icon, go to Settings > Audio player and turn on Show on the map.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you want to make audio directions more interesting, you can select a celebrity or character voice to help you navigate. Tap the speaker icon > Current voice to search for the voice or language you want to use. Recent appearances include Bill Hader's Cat in the Hat and Ziggy Marley. You can also record directions in your own voice.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you don't want waze storing certain types of data—or if you want to keep your activity hidden from other users—you can adjust various privacy settings in the app. You will certainly want to turn off personalized ads (under Settings > Privacy) and consider enabling invisible mode, which keeps your username, mood, photo, and online status hidden from other Waze users. Finally, you can delete recent locations and drives as well as your navigation history at any time.

#462. Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO

📅 12 Nov 2026

Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-steps-down/

Jensen Huang stepped down as the chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, four days after the company announced its internal investigation into an affair he had with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security.

Diungkapkan bahwa “jensen huang has resigned as president, chief executive officer, and a member of the board, effective immediately,” the nvidia board said in a statement. Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO. The board said it “will consider internal and external candidates” for a permanent replacement.

Berdasarkan laporan, the board’s investigation was announced on november 8, slightly less than two weeks after the new york times reported that the chief executive had been the target of a chinese intelligence operation facilitated through his relationship with alice huang, who has no known relation to jensen. The pair have been spotted in public together at least twice, in June 2024 and May 2025. On November 11, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also allegedly had a relationship with a direct report at Nvidia.

The alleged relationship with a subordinate, along with Huang’s business dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company where Alice Huang previously held a senior position, likely played a greater role in the board’s decision to oust Huang than the Chinese espionage allegations, a source familiar with the matter tells WIRED.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, us intelligence officials reportedly briefed president donald trump on huang’s relationship with alice last year, but the president did not act on it. On November 6, The New York Times and Financial Times reported that Alice was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security and that she had been recruited to collect information on the Nvidia executive. (The Chinese government has rejected all claims that Alice was a spy for the country. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, huang sent a companywide email on sunday acknowledging his affair, apologizing to his family and nvidia employees, and pledging cooperation with the internal investigation. The executive has been married to his wife, Lori Huang, since 1985, and both of the couple’s two children work at the company.

Berdasarkan laporan, on monday, wired exclusively reported that last year huang began working with a crisis pr firm to manage his personal communications. In October 2025, those PR consultants started to be looped in on all press inquiries involving Huang, whether those inquiries were personal or professional in nature.

Berdasarkan laporan, the timing lines up with a new york times report that month that the us commerce department was investigating whether alice huang’s megaspeed was helping chinese companies get around american export controls with the help of a vast web of subsidiaries. The investigation was reportedly halted and transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter inquired about it.

Diungkapkan bahwa huang has been a vocal critic of these export controls, which he argues unnecessarily constrain the market for american chips, create discrete chinese and american tech ecosystems, and spur china to build competitive chips of its own. Huang has worked to develop a relationship with Trump in order to advocate for policies that are advantageous for Nvidia, including the idea of opening its markets to China.

Diungkapkan bahwa huang cofounded nvidia in 1993 with friends chris malachowsky and curtis priem. The trio reportedly brainstormed their vision for the company in a Denny’s diner and aspired to bring realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For the first few decades of its existence, Nvidia was primarily known in the gaming community for creating chips powerful enough to render high-quality in-game graphics.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in 2012, after a new kind of neural network known as alexnet won a high-profile prize in computer vision, nvidia pivoted from high-speed computer graphics to building chips that would support artificial intelligence. Huang has repeatedly said that the introduction of AlexNet, which was developed by AI engineers Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton, was a “Big Bang”–like event for computing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, because its new gpus proved highly effective at powering ai models that require massive amounts of processing power, the value of nvidia shares soared in 2023 and 2024, in lockstep with the broader ai boom that began sweeping through the world economy. In the summer of 2025, Nvidia became the first company in history to cross $4 trillion in value.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as of september 2026, the company controlled about 90 percent of the gpu market. Much of Nvidia’s epic rise over the few decades has been attributed not just to its cutting-edge chips and its software “moat,” CUDA, that keeps developers locked into those chips, but also to the fast-thinking, controlling, charismatic, and often bombastic leadership style of Huang himself. Now, that critical part of the company’s success is out.

Exclusive: Fairphone Lands Its First US Carrier Partner in Boost Mobile

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/exclusive-fairphone-lands-its-first-us-carrier-partner-in-boost-mobile/

Americans overwhelmingly buy their smartphones at carrier stores on contract—nearly 70 percent, according to 2025 IDC data—so any growing phone manufacturer must partner up to succeed, rather than rely solely on online retailers like Amazon.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that's why fairphone, the only mobile manufacturer in the world with a 10/10 repairability rating for its smartphones, has announced its first carrier partnership with boost mobile. Fairphone has sold its smartphones in Europe for more than a decade, but it only began selling its phones in the US this summer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, boost is a mobile virtual network operator (mvno) formerly owned by sprint and dish before dish merged with echostar. Unlike carriers such as AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon, MVNOs lease network access and don't own the underlying infrastructure; Boost primarily relies on AT&T's network for coverage, though it has some access to T-Mobile. While Americans largely rely on the big three carriers, Counterpoint research director Mohit Agrawal tells WIRED that around 16 percent of US consumers rely on MVNOs, including carrier-owned MVNOs like Mint Mobile and Cricket.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the $650 fairphone gen. 6+ is the only cellular device Fairphone sells in the US, and it’s certified to work on T-Mobile’s or AT&T’s networks. Instead, you'll have to buy the device from Fairphone or Amazon, then activate it through Boost with any of the MVNO's plans. Fairphone's website will have Boost plan options at purchase. With the Boost Mobile partnership, you still can’t directly buy it from Boost's online storefront or brick-and-mortar stores. If you go that route, you'll receive an eSIM activation email when the phone is delivered.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rutger sneep, chief commercial officer at fairphone, tells wired in a text message that this is phase one, a first step in a long-term collaboration, and to expect more news soon on “joint go-to-market plans. ” When asked whether Boost will facilitate repairs, since many Americans bring their devices to carrier stores for fixes, Sneep says Americans won't need to go anywhere to get their phone fixed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “you can simply and affordably order all spare parts to your doorstep and carry out the repair yourself,” sneep says. “In the more complex cases, which are also more rare, you only need to send your Fairphone to a repair center. Fortunately, within five years after purchasing your Gen. ” (You need to register the phone within 90 days to get the full extended warranty. 6+, you're also still covered by your warranty. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, the gen. Fairphone sells spare parts on its website, and the components are affordable. 6+ comes with a screwdriver, and owners can replace 12 modular elements, from the USB-C port and battery to the screen and cameras. For example, a replacement battery is $40, and a new display costs $90. For an iPhone 17, a battery replacement costs $99, and a display repair costs $329.

Berdasarkan laporan, the fairphone isn’t just repairable—the company also touts its products as sustainable and promotes fair wages for workers in the supply chain. (It has various independent accreditations, like B Corp certification and a Platinum EcoVadis rating. ) These efforts are partly why the Gen. 6+ costs as much as it does; going by specs alone, you can get a competing device for less cash.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the overall smartphone market is declining, according to counterpoint data, largely because of rising costs stemming from the memory crunch. Yes, phone makers have raised smartphone prices, a broader trend that is affecting all electronics. Shipments declined 19 percent year over year, though smartphone revenue grew 3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 due to higher prices. Fairphone claims it’s in a bright spot, though, with phone sales up 74 percent in the first half of the year and 48 percent growth in the second quarter alone.

#470. This AirPods Feature Fixed My Biggest Problem With Listening to Podcasts to Fall Asleep

📅 09 Nov 2026

This AirPods Feature Fixed My Biggest Problem With Listening to Podcasts to Fall Asleep

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/this-airpods-feature-fixed-my-biggest-problem-with-listening-to-podcasts?utm_medium=RSS

We're highlighting the small changes—from useful new gadgets, to fresh productivity techniques, to efficient hacks—that are improving our lives on a weekly basis.

Diungkapkan bahwa there's lots to recommend about podcasts (and lots of podcasts to recommend), but one of their biggest benefits—for me, anyway—has little to do with what a particular show is about or even who hosts it: they're great for dissociating. I often have a podcast playing to distract my anxious brain from whatever I'm worried about (which, in 2026, is usually slightly less than everything).

Diungkapkan bahwa any time i don't want to be alone with my thoughts (say, when commuting or doing mindless chores), i can put on a podcast and be entertained by a couple of goobers talking about movies rather than spinning my wheels about my son's middle school applications. And there's no time I want to disassociate from reality more than bedtime.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for years i've used podcasts as a non-pharmaceutical sleep aid, and few things are more effective at helping me drop off quickly. Unfortunately, for years this also meant that once I fell asleep, the podcast kept playing. I have my podcast app set to delete episodes once finished, so if it was a show I cared about, I'd need to do a lot of redownloading and scrubbing through to find where I left off—that is, until I upgraded my earbuds to the AirPods Pro 3.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the airpods pro 3 launched alongside ios 26 in the fall of 2025 with flashy features like vastly improved noise cancellation, live translation, heart rate sensing, and hearing health settings, all of them quite welcome on a set of $250 premium earbuds. But the best new AirPods feature was one I didn't even know about when I decided to upgrade my four-year-old Beats Fit Pro.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the airpods settings (accessible via your iphone's settings app), if you tap audio & routing and scroll down, you'll see an option to turn on a setting called pause media when falling asleep. I don't think I need to tell you what this setting does. I can tell you that it works great.

Diungkapkan bahwa according to apple, the feature works by sensing when you're drifting off using the earbuds' built-in accelerometer to track your movement (or lack thereof). Once your earbuds have determined that you're falling asleep, they will pause your audio for you. And it isn't just the 2025 AirPods Pro 3 that support it—it also works on the second-generation AirPods Pro as well as the AirPods 4 and the AirPods 5.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i'll admit that i don't really understand how the airpods pro 3 can tell i'm falling asleep versus just lying very still, but i've never had them pause accidentally during active listening. Conversely, whenever I go back to the podcast I was listening to the night before, I'll find that the audio paused within a minute or two of the last part I remember hearing.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the airpods pro 3 aren't the only earbuds with a feature like this, but you'll most often only find it in dedicated "sleep earbuds" designed specifically for the purpose. While many of those offer extra health features like the ability to track your sleep cycles, I'm not really interested in that (my Apple Watch does most of it, and I don't look at that data anyway). Pausing my audio when I'm asleep is really all I need, and the AirPods Pro 3 do it well enough that I don't need to bother with a pair of dedicated bedtime buds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, under the hood, it’s easily the powerhouse of this trio. Thanks to Apple’s A19 silicon, the iPhone 17e delivers superior CPU and GPU performance that keeps everyday multitasking snappy and handles demanding, graphically-intensive games far better than its Android counterparts. I appreciate that Apple also made a couple of smart hardware upgrades — like bumping starting storage to a generous 256GB and finally adding MagSafe support.

Diungkapkan bahwa that said, the iphone 17e isn’t without a few glaring compromises. Holding onto a 60Hz display feels increasingly dated when 120Hz panels have become standard across the rest of the mid-range market — and the lack of an ultrawide camera means it’s not as suitable for sprawling landscapes and group photos.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and while ios 27 brings some much-needed new features, like the ability to create custom passes and use generative ai with its reframe tool to shift to a new perspective for photos, siri ai remains functionally inferior compared to gemini. While the assistant is more proactive with what I’m doing on the phone to offer actionable recommendations — like creating a reminder when someone texts me about an upcoming event — Siri AI lacks the deeper third-party app support that lets it work across more apps.

Worst of all, its recent price hike to $699 (up from its $599 launch price) makes those omissions much harder to overlook.

Berdasarkan laporan, there’s good and bad with the pixel 10a. Just like the iPhone 17e, the design makes it look like a generic slab — but at least Google’s made the camera housing completely flush and offers some fun color options. Despite these design tweaks, the phone is by and large similar to its predecessor, the Pixel 9a, including how it packs the same Tensor G4 chip as before.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, its 6. 3-inch Actua display is surprisingly sharp and bright, besting its rivals with a peak brightness of 1,896 nits in our lab testing. Even better, it posted the longest battery life of the trio with an average of 15 hours and 16 minutes. Better yet, it also delivers the fastest wired charging times we’ve tested — reaching 64% in 30 minutes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, where the pixel 10a truly separates itself, though, is on the software front. Gemini remains leagues ahead of Siri AI and Bixby, especially in its ability to execute complex, multi-step actions across different apps. I’m not simply referring to asking it to check upcoming New York Knicks home games and add them to my calendar — I’m talking about everyday things like ordering Dunkin’ Donuts through DoorDash, all with a simple voice command.

Berdasarkan laporan, if that’s not enough, the pixel 10a really widens the software divide with how practically the pixel desktop mode works when i connect it to an external monitor, turning the phone into a surprisingly capable workstation when i happen to leave my work laptop at home. Even on the photography side, new AI tools like Auto Best Take and Camera Coach help you nail group shots and framing without any heavy lifting.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, google’s decision to reuse the same tensor g4 chip as its predecessor puts it at a major disadvantage in raw cpu and gpu benchmarking compared to the iphone 17e. And in 2026, having a base storage of 128GB feels stingy. Even though the camera performance is better than most other mid-range phones, I’m disappointed that there's barely any improvement over its predecessor — a tougher pill to swallow now that its $100 price hike has pushed it to $599.

Diungkapkan bahwa out of the bunch, the samsung galaxy a57 has the most premium look and feel — rivaling its flagship sibling, the galaxy s26. Not only does it combine the glass-meets-metal build Samsung’s known to give its top-tier models, but it also manages to have an IP68 rating.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you prefer a phone with a larger screen to see more of what you’re doing or stream your favorite shows while on the go, the galaxy a57’s massive 6. 1- and 6. It’s way bigger than the 6. 7-inch Super AMOLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate doesn’t disappoint. 3-inch screens of the iPhone 17e and Pixel 10a, respectively.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, another notable feature is how it’s the only phone in this trio to pack a triple-camera system on the back, pairing a 50mp main sensor with a 12mp ultrawide and a 5mp macro lens. While that dedicated macro shooter feels more like a forced addition just to give it the upper hand, having three distinct lenses nonetheless gives you extra shooting versatility that neither the iPhone 17e nor the Pixel 10a can match.

Sebagaimana diketahui, throw in some s26-level galaxy ai features — like access to object eraser and a voice transcription tool — and it has a robust toolset to help save you time. I also love how it caters to power users like myself, with the ability to run two apps side by side, which neither the iPhone 17e nor the Pixel 10a can do.

Diungkapkan bahwa where the galaxy a57 stumbles, though, is under the hood. Powered by Samsung’s Exynos 1680 chip, it posted the lowest performance scores of the bunch in our testing, lagging behind both the Pixel 10a and especially the iPhone 17e. Worse yet, it doesn’t even have the luxury of wireless charging — a glaring omission, in my opinion, now that its $50 price hike has pushed the cost up to $599.

3DMark Wild Life Original Unlimited (score/fps).

Diungkapkan bahwa if there’s one i’d buy with my own money, it has to be the pixel 10a — with the iphone 17e not too far behind it. That’s because Google’s mid-range phone checks off more of the boxes on my list than the other two.

Sebagaimana diketahui, all three phones got price hikes, but the pixel 10a’s $599 price tag is easier to swallow than the iphone 17e’s heftier $699 cost. And while the Galaxy A57 matches the Pixel’s price point, its weak processing performance combined with flat camera results aren’t enough to prove to me it offers better value at the same price.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ultimately, the google pixel 10a is the mid-range phone i recommend. I can’t stress enough the value of its software package alone — and backed up by seven years’ worth of major Android and security updates, it’s undeniably the smartest long-term investment you can make in the mid-range market right now.

Update Your iPhone to Prevent People From Seeing iMessages They Shouldn't

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/update-your-iphone-to-prevent-people-from-seeing-imessages-they-shouldnt?utm_medium=RSS

Sebagaimana diketahui, has this ever happened to you? you add someone new to an imessage group chat, and wonder, "huh, can they see any of the messages from before they were added?" the answer to that question is supposed to be "no. " By design, new iMessage group chat members are only privy to texts that arrive after they were added. When they join, it's essentially a blank slate, as if you just created the group for the first time. At least, that's how it's intended to work.

Berdasarkan laporan, as it turns out, there's a bug with imessage that may allow new group chat members to see texts from before they were added to the chat. You don't have to be talking behind people's backs to not want new members seeing existing chats. It means iMessage, and Apple's platforms in general, aren't working like they're supposed to be. That's a problem, and not just for the iPhone users out there talking smack about people before inviting them to join the group chat. Maybe you're planning a surprise party for someone, and add them to the group once everyone's in on the plan; maybe the texts in the chat aren't relevant to the current group, and the person joining simply does not need to access them.

Diungkapkan bahwa that's not all: there exists another security flaw that could allow remote hackers to join an imessage group and receive new messages. You might add a new user to a group chat and inadvertently invite them to read all existing messages, while at the same time being attacked by a bad actor who can then intercept all future messages. Not good.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, luckily, there's currently a fix for these problems. 3, watchOS 27. Not all of the updates include patches for these two iMessage flaws—specifically, some of the updates for older Apple devices. 7. 1, and visionOS 27. 2. 1, macOS 27. 2. 2. 1, macOS 26. 8. But the rest, including iOS 27. 2. 3, macOS 15. Apple patched (and revealed) the bugs, along with seven other security flaws, with a series of software updates on Monday for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro. 1, include the iMessage patches.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, each update includes its own list of patches, but, for this article, i'll take a look at the nine patches in ios 27. 2. 1. You'll find the two iMessage bugs, plus seven other patches, in the list below:.

Diungkapkan bahwa airplay: impact: an attacker in bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113968: Apple.

Diungkapkan bahwa app intents: impact: an app may be able to access sensitive user data. Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113963: László Várady.

Diungkapkan bahwa bluetooth: impact: an attacker in bluetooth range may be able to corrupt process memory. Description: A use-after-free issue was addressed with improved memory management. CVE-2026-113970: Apple.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, brotli: impact: processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption. Description: An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved input validation. CVE-2026-111497.

Berdasarkan laporan, coreutils: impact: a malicious bluetooth device may be able to establish a pairing without user interaction. Description: This issue was addressed with improved checks. CVE-2026-113965: Apple.

Sebagaimana diketahui, coreutils: impact: an attacker in bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts and pair with a device without user interaction. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113964: an anonymous researcher.

Diungkapkan bahwa messages: impact: a remote attacker may be able to join an imessage group chat and receive its messages. Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved validation. CVE-2026-113961: an anonymous researcher.

Sebagaimana diketahui, messages: impact: a user added to an imessage group may be able to access messages sent before they joined. Description: This issue was addressed by removing the vulnerable code. CVE-2026-113960: an anonymous researcher.

Diungkapkan bahwa rapportd: impact: an attacker on the same network may be able to bypass the rate limit on airplay pairing code attempts. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113969: Apple.

For a full accounting of the patches included in the other security updates, check out Apple's official security releases site.

Diungkapkan bahwa to install apple's latest security updates, you'll simply need to update your device as you usually do. On iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro, head to Settings > General > Software Update; on Mac, go to System Settings > General > Software Update. Here, follow the on-screen instructions to download and install the latest version of your device's software.

#475. You Can Buy T-Shirts Glorifying Mass Shootings Almost Anywhere Online

📅 12 Nov 2026

You Can Buy T-Shirts Glorifying Mass Shootings Almost Anywhere Online

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/you-can-buy-t-shirts-glorifying-mass-shootings-almost-anywhere-online/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the day he carried out the columbine high school massacre, 18-year-old shooter eric harris wore a white t-shirt with the phrase “natural selection” printed on it in black lettering. His fellow assailant, 17-year-old Dylan Klebold, wore a black T-shirt with the word “Wrath” printed in red across the chest.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ever since, this apparel has been closely linked with mass murder, part of an ever-growing mosaic of niche allusions to deadly attacks on schools, places of worship, government buildings, and social gathering spaces. While you might not think twice about a person wearing one of the shirts Harris and Klebold chose for their assault on their classmates, let alone recognize the reference, there’s an online community that revels in this aesthetic, using it as a means to valorize and motivate nihilistic violence.

According to a report publishing later this week from the Institute for Strategic Dialogue, a research organization that analyzes extremism and online threats, statement shirts associated with such horrific acts are widely available from at least half a dozen internet retailers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, isd found sellers peddling “wrath” and “natural selection” tees modeled after the columbine shirts on tiktok shop, redbubble, temu, etsy, aliexpress, and walmart. Shirts with the slogan “Humanity Is Overrated”—like the one worn by a teen gunman who killed nine people at his high school in Finland in 2007—turned up on AliExpress, Temu, and the TikTok Shop, according to the report.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a statement, a representative for tiktok us said: “discriminatory and offensive products are prohibited from sale on tiktok shop and will be removed. ” A representative for Redbubble said that the marketplace prohibits “content that glorifies or trivializes violence” and that it had removed listings for “Wrath” and “Natural Selection” shirts flagged by WIRED.

A representative for Walmart said that a shirt flagged by WIRED was removed in accordance with its policies for third-party sellers.

None of the other retailers immediately replied to a request for comment.

Berdasarkan laporan, katherine keneally, isd’s senior director of threat analysis and prevention, tells wired that these clothes are promoted by a cohort known as the true crime community, or tcc. Not to be confused with fans of podcasts and documentaries about unsolved or unusual crimes, the TCC “is a predominantly online fandom that is rooted in an obsession with mass killers, regardless of the mass killer’s motivation,” Keneally says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the tcc’s fascination with the lore around specific killers can lead to dissection of details as minor as what they had for breakfast on the morning of their attack, keneally says. But the statement shirts offer a convenient way to covertly endorse such massacres, with most people outside the in-group none the wiser.

Berdasarkan laporan, “what we see from attackers is that they are often trying, in many ways, to mirror previous attackers, but putting their own sort of spin on it,” keneally says. The shirts are used to “signal interest and glorification of the violence, and also can serve as a sign of someone's plans to engage in something, engage in some sort of attack,” she adds. The ISD’s report cites the cases of a 13-year-old arrested in South Africa last month after allegedly stabbing a 6-year-old while wearing a “Wrath” shirt and an 18-year-old accused of fatally shooting two people in a California library in June, who was apprehended wearing a “Natural Selection” tee.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the isd analysis of the sale of shirts connected to past shootings is part of a planned series by the nonprofit covering various warning signs of future attacks. The idea is to give parents, teachers, and law enforcement more guidance in understanding when a young person may have intent to harm others, particularly because “within the TCC, we are seeing predominantly youth and minors being involved,” Keneally says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, adolescents aren’t just engaging with this content in “the darker corners of the internet,” keneally says. “It's happening very openly across mainstream and fringe platforms. ” The prevalence of the clothing across an array of online shops is an indication of how the TCC’s extremist messaging flies under the radar.

Diungkapkan bahwa meanwhile, as isd revealed in its research, younger affiliates of this diffuse collective are trading tips on how to disguise the meaning of paraphernalia tied to mass shooter fandom. One screenshot in the report shows a TikTok user asking their followers, “How do y’all convince your parents to buy the natural selection shirt,” with commenters advising that they pretend “Natural Selection” is the name of a movie, a video game, or a brand. One person replied: “My parents don’t know what tcc is so i can buy it without any problems. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, tcc enthusiasts have also made it clear in their product reviews of the t-shirts that they admire perpetrators of deadly gun violence. ” A third person ominously noted that they would use their “Wrath” shirt “to become a bit more popular at school. In their five-star feedback on a “Wrath” shirt, a customer wrote “we love dylan klebold!” Another attached an anime-style cartoon of Eric Harris in the “Natural Selection” shirt on their review of same, noting that they were hiding it from their mom but that it was “so cute” and “good quality too. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, keneally acknowledges that there’s a “fine line” to consider with clothing that may suggest an unhealthy fixation on infamous killers, since even the best-known examples are not offensive or illegal in themselves. Context also matters: The TCC has an affinity for the German industrial band KMFDM because they were a favorite band of the Columbine shooters, but a fan wearing a KMFDM shirt could have no idea of the connection.

Diungkapkan bahwa while a teen’s purchase of the most flagrant tcc shirt doesn’t help them commit an attack or necessarily indicate the planning of real-world violence, keneally says, adults should weigh it against other factors. “If they have access to weapons or maybe another student has heard them talk about committing violence, then it can help serve as a warning sign and provide an opportunity for intervention,” she says. And wearing the shirt at all communicates a likely need for mental health support.

Berdasarkan laporan, as for the retailers that facilitate the sale of this apparel, keneally believes that if they adequately enforced their established safety policies, much of it would be taken down. The clothes are something that youths seek out to be “a part of” the True Crime Community and fuel this toxic subculture, she says. “It shouldn't be that easy to access. ”.

Update, Thursday November 12 at 1pm: The story was updated to include a statement from Walmart, which has removed the shirts mentioned in the story.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there have been so many heist thrillers in movies and tv that it’s tough to find a fresh angle on the well-worn subgenre. The new Apple TV series “12 12 12” attempts to make its heist story stand out by dividing it among three timelines, inspired by a dubious-sounding FBI statistic quoted at the beginning of each episode: A high-level, professional heist requires 12 months of planning, 12 hours to execute, and if the robbers aren’t caught within 12 days, they never will be.

That gives creators Jim Keeble and Dudi Appleton a strict format to follow, but fracturing the narrative mostly serves as a distraction from the basic heist-thriller elements.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, just because it’s basic doesn’t mean that it’s bad, and as a connoisseur of this type of story, i still mostly had fun with “12 12 12. ” Eight episodes is a long time to spend on a single crime, though, and the momentum flags as the season progresses, especially when the creators are simply filling in the gaps for events that viewers have already seen.

Jamie Dornan and Anthony Mackie are compelling as the central criminal and cop, respectively, and “12 12 12” is slick and propulsive enough to make for a mildly entertaining watch, even if it’s far from reinventing the heist thriller.

Sebagaimana diketahui, although it could be confusing to follow three separate timelines of the same characters engaged in the same project, “12 12 12” makes it relatively simple, with onscreen graphics indicating exactly which part of which segment is taking place at any given time. The individual tracks (months, hours, days) unfold in a linear fashion, so that the first episode begins with the first month of planning, the first hour of the robbery, and the first day of the getaway. Each episode moves the story forward in all three time periods.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in that way, “12 12 12” is rarely disorienting, but the structure also robs the story of some potential suspense. Viewers already know that the planning stage will lead to an actual heist, and that the heist will succeed well enough for the perpetrators to get away. Even so, Keeble and Appleton are able to consistently deploy surprise twists, and they use the show’s structure for misdirection, when something that happens in one particular time period turns out not to be what it seems once information from later or earlier is revealed.

Diungkapkan bahwa laid out in a straightforward manner, the plot is pretty standard. Reformed robber Paul Galvin (Dornan) is drawn back into criminal activity by his screw-up older brother Bobby (Jack Kesy), who’s gotten himself in trouble with a powerful French mobster. That menacing crime boss threatens to kill Paul’s wife Severine (Agathe Rousselle) and his unborn child if he doesn’t take on the job of stealing nearly $1 billion in cash stored by the Russian mafia in a Swiss bank.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sign up to the weekly tom's streaming guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Meanwhile, FBI agent Jack Strickland (Mackie) has transferred to Europe so that he can track the Galvins after a failed takedown in Newark that left Jack’s partner dead.

Diungkapkan bahwa to pull off the heist, paul recruits an extensive crew that includes his drilling-expert father-in-law, the bank’s disgraced head of security, and a contortionist who can fit inside a safety deposit box, among others. Most of the characters get limited screen time, and even a recognizable star like Kali Reis of “True Detective” is little more than a cog in the heist plan, playing an expert in train engineering who plans the getaway. It’s a bit disappointing given the lengthy running time that there isn’t more room for character development beyond the combative relationship between the Galvin brothers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that fraternal dynamic wears out quickly, but jack has a more complex, rewarding arc, as he has to transcend his desire for revenge against the galvins and find a way to move forward. The most compelling relationship in “12 12 12” is between Jack and Swiss police detective Lena (Sallie Harmsen), who goes from wary colleague to devoted ally to something more. Their scenes together have more emotional resonance than all of the Galvin brothers’ macho bluster.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even if the characters never acquire that much depth, the plot moves so briskly that there’s rarely a chance to stop and wonder what makes these people tick. There are a couple of exciting car chases, especially one through the streets of Zurich in the first episode, plus plenty of nail-biting moments as the crew tries to solve various problems under the threat of imminent discovery or danger.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if nothing else, “12 12 12” puts its budget to great use, with action that spans multiple european countries and set pieces that include a giant avalanche and a narrowly avoided train collision. It’s not as lively or witty as the “Ocean’s” movies, and the rivalry between Paul and Jack has nothing on Robert De Niro and Al Pacino in “Heat. ” But it holds the audience’s attention almost all the way to the end, until a final episode that has one or two superfluous conclusions.

Diungkapkan bahwa the timeline trickery proves to be largely superfluous, too, but it keeps viewers on their toes and offers a few satisfying “aha” moments. That’s about all a heist thriller needs. If the formula works, there’s no reason to mess with it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i’ve been a democrat my whole life,” karp told politico, which noted that he called the democratic party “totally irresponsible” in the distant time of october 2025. “I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir—all of our products are essentially progressive. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in his most recent quarterly letter to palantir shareholders, karp actually doubled down on his basic premise. In it, he argued that Palantir employees are “the pioneers of a genuine and viable antiwar movement. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, karp went on to say that palantir has both a “moral imperative” and a “mission reason” for having the “somewhat crazy aspiration” of dominating its market. That mission, Karp said, is supporting the war fighter. Conveniently, it’s also very profitable.

“We are delighted that we can support the war fighter even more because we're making so much money,” Karp said.

Diungkapkan bahwa karp’s recent comments in politico could also be seen through the lens of convenience. Palantir has seen continued success, after all, across Democratic and Republican administrations.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, karp doesn’t care about cultivating favor with everybody. ” (Karp didn’t name examples, although many critiques of Palantir have come from the American left. Berdasarkan laporan, i love my peace lily. Its glossy green leaves and elegant white blooms add a gorgeous touch to my home — except lately, it’s been all leaves and no flowers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to figure out where i’m going wrong, i asked the experts how to get it blooming again. Thankfully, it doesn’t necessarily mean it’s unhealthy; often a few adjustments to its growing conditions, along with some patience, can make a difference.

Berdasarkan laporan, having a peace lily that doesn’t flower is a common frustration for owners, according to elizabeth waddington, garden designer and writer at first tunnels. But she says, “Often slight adjustments to the light levels, warmth, water provided, or other growing conditions can encourage blooms to form. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and, of course, another reason why your peace lily might not be flowering yet is that it’s simply immature and not at the flowering stage. Plus, they don’t flower year-round.

Sebagaimana diketahui, most commonly, houseplant peace lilies will flower in spring and summer. “Don’t panic if you’re not seeing any growth during the winter months, as this is when they slow down,” says David Denyer, florist and gardening expert at Eflorist.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, this may change if you see them growing in their natural, tropical environment, with waddington adding, “if well cared for indoors, in optimal growing conditions, peace lilies can flower at any time, and may even flower more than once a year. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unfortunately, peace lilies don’t flower indefinitely. Denyer says, “A peace lily flower will usually last for a month, or even two with the proper care, before changing to black or brown. ” Did you know it’s not really a flower?The white section of a peace lily, often called a flower, is actually a modified leaf called a spathe or bract.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Diungkapkan bahwa the best way to keep your peace lily flowering for longer is to make sure it is cared for properly. “If your peace lily is struggling to bloom at all, this usually means it’s needing a bit more care and attention,” says Denyer.

Berdasarkan laporan, “flowering takes a lot of energy, so it’s key that during the growing season you feed your plant little and often,” explains denyer. And he suggests using a balanced, water-soluble fertilizer every few weeks from April to October. During winter, he recommends reducing the feed to every 4-6 weeks, to maintain your peace lily without encouraging excessive growth or overwhelming your plant.

As a tropical plant, peace lilies prefer a consistently warm temperature, and they can be particularly sensitive to temperature changes; that’s why Denyer says it’s important that you adjust your care for them as the seasons change.

Berdasarkan laporan, “one of the biggest mistakes people can make when caring for their peace lily is positioning it near windows and air vents,” denyer explains. “Although you may think your peace lily will love the light that comes from being right next to the window, exposing it to cold drafts is actually detrimental to the health of your plant. ”He adds that if exposed to low temperatures for a long time, you may notice your peace lily wilts, and it can even die. Similarly, placing your peace lily near a heat source can damage it, too.

The ideal temperaturePeace lilies don’t adjust well to unstable temperatures and perform best between 64 and 80°F (18 to 27°C), according to Waddington.

Berdasarkan laporan, while peace lilies need light, which can be lacking in winter, denyer says not to be tempted to move your plant into direct sunlight, as this will scorch the leaves. This Aokrean Grow Light for Indoor Plants is just $17 at Amazon. Instead, move it to a position where it can gain bright, indirect light or use a suitable grow light above it. Placing your plant next to a window may also expose it to cold drafts, which it will hate.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “as tropical plants, peace lilies enjoy relatively humid conditions,” says waddington. If the air in your home is dry, especially during winter, she suggests grouping houseplants together, using a room humidifier, or placing the plant on a pebble tray with water, ensuring the bottom of the pot stays above the waterline.

Diungkapkan bahwa she also suggests misting the leaves, but warns, “make sure you do this in the morning so that the excess water can evaporate, or you may experience some fungal growth on your peace lily. ”.

What’s more, because peace lilies love humidity, they are the perfect houseplant for a steamy bathroom!.

They are perfect when you need a medium-duty glove that provides dexterity. Plus, they come in a pack of two.

Diungkapkan bahwa you should continue watering your peace lily regularly throughout winter, but denyer says you may need to adjust your watering schedule. “Your weekly watering routine may turn into every 10 days during the winter months,” he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he also adds that peace lilies like consistently moist soil, so when the top inch of soil is dry, you can give it a little bit of water to maintain the plant’s health. But be careful not to overwater your plant, which can lead to waterlogged soil, or leave it completely dry, which can cause the leaves to turn brown.

In Photoshop, the new Relight tool offers a way to non-destructively and dynamically add, reposition, and resize light sources in the composition, while Generative Restylelets users** prompt the platform to generate variations of an image’s style and fine-tune the results using adjustable sliders.

#486. Google Wanted Spirit Airlines Data. Flight Attendants Found a Way to Opt Out

📅 12 Nov 2026

Google Wanted Spirit Airlines Data. Flight Attendants Found a Way to Opt Out

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/google-wanted-spirit-airlines-data-flight-attendants-found-a-way-to-opt-out/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you care about privacy, don’t feed your own personal information into a chatbot, which—among other concerns—could use it to train ai tools. Employees, though, mostly don’t have a choice.

Berdasarkan laporan, a new, multibillion-dollar industry is dedicated to selling and buying work files and emails to companies seeking fresh sources of data to improve their ai models, and it’s only getting bigger. Data privacy laws tend to focus on consumer protections and rarely consider the rights of workers who create that information. What happens when your doctor’s notes, employee contracts, and Slack gossip are fed into the machine?.

Diungkapkan bahwa an agreement reached this week between google and a union representing an unlikely workforce—flight attendants—could reveal a more permanent answer by creating a process that might reliably separate the data that workers produce from their own personal information. A judge still needs to approve the agreement next week.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the first-of-its-kind deal is part of the liquidation process for spirit airlines, which suddenly ceased operations earlier this year. But the union, the 55,000-member Association for Flight Attendants, argued that Google’s proposed safeguards would not prevent serious privacy violations for Spirit Airlines flight attendants, whose records—including 1. In August, representatives for the budget airline said in a legal brief that it would be selling decades’ worth of data to Google for $10 million; Google said it would not receive personal information as part of the sale. 99 billion emails, 664 million Microsoft Teams messages, and employee travel and training information, all dating back to 1986—would be included in the sale.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the revised deal requires spirit to hire a third-party data de-identification company, called tonic ai, to exclude information that could potentially be associated with individual consumers or employees. Tonic will also be charged with ensuring that data, once de-identified, cannot be relinked to specific people. Google has promised to maintain the data in this new, de-identified form.

Sebagaimana diketahui, many sensitive records will be excluded from the sale, including employee medical records, documents related to employee investigations and labor relations, and information about industry-wide safety management systems. In early November, a trade organization representing airlines chimed in on the sale, arguing that including that information could make employees less willing to come forward to report safety issues through voluntary programs, which are widely regarded as critical to the US aviation industry’s strong safety record.

Diungkapkan bahwa the proposed agreement also includes an opt-out clause. Google can choose to renege on the sale if the data-cleaning process reduces the assets by more than 8 percent. Google didn’t respond to a request for comment.

Association for Flight Attendants president Sara Nelson tells WIRED she’s as surprised as anyone that flight attendants are at the forefront of AI-related workers’ rights issues, which often focus on employees who, willingly or unwillingly, train their machine replacements.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it’s very hard to replace a flight attendant—you’d need a high-functioning robot, and that seems to be further off,” she says. This is an issue for everyone. “What this shows is that this is an issue even in jobs you think are most protected from AI. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa she said the union will immediately begin to demand that other airlines include worker-data-protection clauses in their labor agreements. “If you’re not willing to meet these standards for your workers, we’re going to shame you,” she says. The Association for Flight Attendants has begun meeting with state-level politicians to craft legislation that would write worker data protections into law.

Berdasarkan laporan, ari ezra waldman, a professor at the uc irvine school of law who studies law and technology, calls the proposed settlement “a pretty good outcome” for spirit airlines employees. He points to another, and maybe easier, alternative: Banning the sale of data altogether. “From now on, unions will know to negotiate to protect the privacy rights in the event of future sales of data assets,” he wrote to WIRED in an email. “Privacy protections are necessary now more than ever,” he says.

Berdasarkan laporan, tech leaders have argued that workers understand that their information will train ai models, which will ultimately make their lives better and easier. “You have to think of the upside, the abundance that AI can result in,” one executive told WIRED this month.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nelson says us workers aren’t buying the upside of ai and that they’re part of the wider electorate that seems to be growing warier of the tech by the day. She says the vision of AI abundance is “a fantasyland of people in boardrooms with beanbags who wear hoodies. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, november is a huge month for video games. But the game we've been waiting for most of all also launched this month: WendyQuest, the free RPG from Wendy's. (No, this is not a joke. Nintendo dropped its remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2 last week, and the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI is right around the corner. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, despite the absurdity of a hamburger chain making a full video game (complete with wendy's-themed puns), the thing is, this game is pretty solid—even if it is a promotion at the end of the day. WendyQuest's main purpose is to offer customers coupons they can use toward purchases in real life, though it's a bit of a commitment. It took me just under an hour of gameplay before I earned my first coupon, and Wendy's says it takes roughly 15 hours to beat. All that to say, this is a pretty unique marketing campaign.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i was surprised booting up wendyquest on my iphone. This doesn't necessarily feel like a thrown-together product. On the flip side, the production quality is quite high. Berdasarkan laporan, there's even a story, albeit cheesy (no pun intended): as the game explains, the "four great spirits of flavor" created savoria, "a food-rich paradise. " All was well until Mech Corp, led by the evil Dr. MechBorg, built robots to take over Savoria. The plot is far from compelling, and the writing can be a little over the top, but hey, I'll give them credit: They thought through a full story here.

Diungkapkan bahwa you play as wendy, the "representation of true culinary excellence and taste as dictated by the four ancient spirits of flavor. " Wendy (or The Wendy, as some call her) is tasked with saving the world, traveling between villages and picking up new characters along the way. The game world even has "real" Wendy's locations you can visit. These act like inns and shops in other RPGs, giving you a chance to heal while also buying equipment.

Diungkapkan bahwa like other rpgs, wendyquest uses turn-based combat. You have to charge up your attacks, but stop before they hit 100%, or you'll miss. That, combined with the spatulas the game encourages you to buy, lets you mow down enemies. ) I'm pretty impressed with how challenging some of these battles can be, though you are quickly given the option of an amulet that gives you a huge leg-up in combat. You can also utilize your companions here: "Frygor," for example, can either attack enemies with a barrage of fries, or use those fries to build a shield to protect you.

Diungkapkan bahwa while there are tons of enemies to fight, the key baddies are the "mechs. Spoiler alert: The first mech drops the "Fry Stone," which nets you a coupon for a free order of medium fries—though you need to buy something in tandem, as well as use the Wendy's app. " There are five in total, and after you defeat each, you get a coupon. While I stopped my gaming here for this article, the other four coupons are:.

Free biscuit or croissant (I didn't even know Wendy's sold biscuits and croissants).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, again, it's wild that wendyquest has a 10+ hour campaign, with over 1,000 lines of dialogue to boot. I respect it. Sure, they could have run a promotion in the Wendy's app to give people coupons, but instead, they built an entire RPG. I'm not sure this is a game I'm going to see through to the end, but I'll admit, it's a fun marketing approach from Wendy's. You can download the game for iOS, Android, or Steam.

#493. Google DeepMind analysis proves Signal and WhatsApp encryption is secure

📅 10 Nov 2026

Google DeepMind analysis proves Signal and WhatsApp encryption is secure

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/10/google-deepmind-analysis-proves-signal-and-whatsapp-encryption-is-secure/

Diungkapkan bahwa the signal protocol has long been considered the gold standard for end-to-end encrypted messaging, with edward snowden a notable advocate. Now a Google DeepMind analysis has “formally verified” the security of the protocol.

In addition to its use in the Signal app, the same protocol is also used by WhatsApp and Google Messages, and the work has been described as “a landmark development” ….

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “formal verification” is the term given to mathematically proving or disproving that a cryptographic algorithm or protocol satisfies its security claims under all conditions. It guarantees that there is no situation in which the protocol will fail. This is a far higher standard than traditional testing methods which seek to find vulnerabilities but cannot promise that others do not exist.

Sebagaimana diketahui, using agentic ai to carry out formal verification is a huge breakthrough for cryptography and ai alike. It is, however, extremely computationally demanding, so Google told Wired it’s unclear as yet how practical it will be to use it more broadly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, deepmind researchers emphasize that their findings are just one milestone in a larger process. “We are very excited by this result, but there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale this to all the software of the world, and we want to do that,” Swarat Chaudhuri, a DeepMind research scientist, tells WIRED.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s important to note that the validation is for the protocol itself rather than the signal app as a whole. However, encouragement can be taken from the fact that when tested against older versions of Signal that contained known vulnerabilities, it identified those and flagged them as failing formal verification.

Berdasarkan laporan, also worth stating is that google was able to build on some past formal verification work already completed without the use of ai. This analysis took four weeks, and the scale of resources required has not yet been disclosed, so we shouldn’t expect a whole array of other protocols to be validated overnight. All the same, this is a very big deal.

#495. Rocco Classic Smart Fridge Review: A Cool Conversation Piece

📅 12 Nov 2026

Rocco Classic Smart Fridge Review: A Cool Conversation Piece

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/review/rocco-super-smart-fridge/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, updated november 2026: the rocco super smart fridge is now called the rocco classic, after rocco released two new fridges in 2026, the lower-priced essential and desktop-sized mini mini. Copy has been updated to reflect the new moniker.

Opening up someone else’s kitchen refrigerator is an intimate act.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i for one would prefer my guests don’t go in there for a beer and see the raspberries that are probably moldy, revealing a dark side of my personality. I’ll just get their drink for them. Having a separate mini fridge just for drinks can help, and when I saw how fresh and innovative the Rocco seemed, I had to know more.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the rocco classic feels more like a piece of furniture sitting in my living room, as opposed to a regular mini fridge, which often looks like it’s out of a college dorm, or a more industrial-looking regular wine fridge. I have the matte graphite color (it also comes in white, green, brown, and mirror-black).

Berdasarkan laporan, the whole thing is mostly made of steel, which makes it strong and heavy, and the rounded edges give it more of a soft appeal. It seems to be engineered very well, with quality materials, which I’m sure is why it costs as much as it does. This should last me a very long time in my home. Overall, it’s a beautiful statement piece that people who like to host in their home will love, but the features that make this a smart fridge are not perfect.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a typical wine fridge will generally fit full-size bottles of wine only, but the classic can fit 77 12-ounce cans (though rocco's website says 88) or 27 wine bottles in its 34. There are six shelves, each of which is designed so you can store bottles and cans of any size and stagger them to fit like a puzzle. 5 x 24 x 16-inch body (H x W x D). Each shelf is also reversible so the grooves match whichever shape bottles you choose to place on each shelf.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rocco connects to an app on your phone (currently available only for ios; rocco hopes to have an android version at some point). It really is extremely quiet. The app is simple and easy to use, but there aren’t that many things to do on it, and some of the features feel forced. I keep mine on Quiet Mode. First of all, there are a few modes you can control from the app. I rarely hear much of a rumbling noise from the compressor compared to other fridges.

Diungkapkan bahwa similarly, there’s smart mode, which makes it work more like a thermostat when the fridge is sitting in a warmer temperature. There’s also Party Mode, which prioritizes keeping the drinks cold more so than making less noise. I opened it a few minutes later, and it was definitely colder in there. (Rocco gives the temperature range as 37 to 64 degrees Fahrenheit. After a few minutes, I did hear the compressor get a little louder. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, but if i want the drinks to stay colder while i’m having a party where people are opening it often, i could just lower the temperature to where i want it myself. I gave each of them 10 minutes to change and tested each shelf on both ends of the fridge. Using a wireless Bluetooth thermometer, I tested the temperature changes inside the fridge for each mode to make sure they work properly. I really don’t see much of a need for all of these modes. I was pleased to find these were all within just a few degrees difference of what the fridge read.

Diungkapkan bahwa the other primary feature of the app is the vision system. Every beverage then shows up on your app, organized by drawer. When you first set up the app, sensors in the fridge scan everything you’re storing in it. I’m storing some pretty obscure drinks, like OoMee algae-infused beverage and Yaté yerba mate, and it recognized most of them, so I was impressed, although some, like my Dolin vermouth, which is one of the most popular vermouth brands, were not recognized.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nutrition facts also pop up for each drink, although many of them are incomplete. I found that I didn’t do this much, although I was curious if I was running low on LaCroix once and checked the app to see that I certainly was. In theory, you could go to the grocery store and see which drinks you’re running low on just by looking at the app. So it came in handy.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, the system is not perfect. Right now it’s showing that I still have one LaCroix remaining, although I haven’t had one in there in a couple of weeks. I would love it if I could purchase something I’m running low on directly from the app.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the dual-temperature system also allows you to make half of the fridge one temperature and the other half another, which you can adjust manually or through the app. While this is important so that I can keep seltzers and wines at different temperatures, this is the one feature that’s on many wine fridges, so it’s not unique to the Classic.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the classic has a kind of mid-century vibe but also feels contemporary. I love the fluted glass door, which looks stunning when it’s nighttime and the lights inside are peeking through it. Any time someone comes to my apartment it becomes a topic of conversation. You can turn the light on and off and adjust the brightness from the app.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the top surface of the fridge is flat and sturdy, so it doubles as a bar cart. The raised lip on the sides also helps so that bottles I’m placing on it have less of a chance of falling off. I have a bar cart that’s overflowing with bottles, so it’s nice to have this right next to it for some overflow.

Diungkapkan bahwa as someone who loves to make a nightly martini, i’ve hated having to go to my kitchen fridge for the vermouth. Now I store my vermouth right in my Rocco and I don’t have to break up my rhythm as much (other than grabbing ice and the chilled glass from the kitchen freezer). The Classic also comes with a pack of round playing cards that double as coasters. They’re a little flimsy for coasters, but it’s a cute touch.

Berdasarkan laporan, the fridge beeps when the door doesn’t shut all the way. I wish I got a push notification when the door wasn’t shut. It’s a pretty soft beep—I didn’t hear it over the TV playing. That would have been a much better use of the app. You really have to make sure the door is all the way shut, because it’s not soft-close, nor are the drawers, which I wish were. The small bottom drawer on mine is also a little bit stubborn to pull out and close, although all the other doors slide nice and smoothly.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the price does make your heart skip a beat. But that aligns with other higher-end wine fridges on the market. You also don't need to worry about installing this fridge into your cabinetry, as it’s a stand-alone piece. The precision and engineering of this fridge make the price seem reasonable when compared with others, and it actually has character, whereas just about every other wine fridge looks the same.

Diungkapkan bahwa additionally, the price includes a 10-year warranty. For an additional fee, you can get white glove delivery, where it’s placed in your home exactly where you want it and the packaging is removed for you. This is probably not worth it. Otherwise, shipping is free.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rocco makes your living room more of an active social space by keeping your guests in the same cozy area. I think people are going to buy this fridge more because of the way it looks rather than the fact that it’s a smart fridge. It’s furniture, which I wouldn’t say about most other fridges. I’m a beverage enthusiast, so I love having the Rocco to show for it.

#501. The Polar Vortex Is About to Make Weather Weird From the UK to the US

📅 12 Nov 2026

The Polar Vortex Is About to Make Weather Weird From the UK to the US

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/the-polar-vortex-is-about-to-make-weather-weird-from-the-uk-to-the-us/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a critical blockade against some of nature’s coldest air has temporarily broken down—and much earlier in the year than normal. Disruptions in this circulation, known as the polar vortex, often push intensely cold air out of the Arctic toward lower latitudes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, experts still aren’t entirely sure how the current collapse will play out in our everyday weather. But it’s another sign that we may be in for a wild ride over the weeks and months to come.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the polar vortex is a band of upper-level winds wrapping around the arctic circle like a dam. This circulation is usually strong and stable, helping to keep the season’s coldest air locked near the North Pole. But the winds occasionally weaken or even reverse course, which can set off an atmospheric chain reaction, allowing bitterly cold air to spill southward.

Berdasarkan laporan, the manner in which the polar vortex breaks down determines what kind of weather conditions we might expect. Upper-level winds dipping southward in troughs are responsible for brief spells of cold temperatures. These “lobes” of the polar vortex, as they’re known, are relatively common in a typical winter.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sometimes, this circulation can splinter into smaller pieces. If the vortex were a flowing river, these fragments are like leaves stuck on the riverbank, forcing extremely cold air to linger over the same areas for days or weeks at a time.

Berdasarkan laporan, one such case made this phenomenon a household name. Chicago recorded its coldest February in nearly 140 years. A highly disrupted polar vortex in early 2015 sent a weeks-long burst of cold air sweeping over the eastern US. In Lexington, Kentucky, temperatures bottomed out at –18 degrees Fahrenheit, as subfreezing air dove all the way to the Gulf of Mexico.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, seeing a breakdown of the polar vortex this early in the season is unprecedented in the historical record. Disruptions of this extent typically don’t occur until the latter half of winter. Based on the latest data, the circulation’s reversal began on Tuesday, and computer model guidance expects it to last through Thursday.

Berdasarkan laporan, weather patterns take a few weeks to respond to a polar vortex disruption, if at all. Given that reliable forecasts only extend about 10 days into the future, we can’t know where in the northern hemisphere cold air from the Arctic may spill.

While experts are still debating the exact causes driving this polar vortex breakdown, the event throws another wrench into a cool season already dominated by another unprecedented event: the strongest El Niño on record.

Historically warm sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific Ocean have already significantly affected conditions around the world, and this influence will only grow heading into the winter months.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, much of north america can expect warmer-than-normal conditions during a winter dominated by a strong el niño. But every event is different, and now with a sudden disruption in the polar vortex, those forecasts are less certain, because unexpected things can happen when unprecedented phenomena overlap.

#502. Canadian court certifies class action against Apple over Google search deal

📅 10 Nov 2026

Canadian court certifies class action against Apple over Google search deal

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/09/canadian-court-certifies-class-action-against-apple-over-google-search-deal/

Sebagaimana diketahui, a british columbia supreme court judge has certified a class action against apple over allegations that its search agreement with google stifled competition and inflated advertising prices. Here are the details.

In recent years, Apple’s deal with Alphabet to make Google the default search engine on Safari has drawn regulatory attention in the US, the UK, and Australia, while related search competition concerns have also come under scrutiny in the EU and Japan.

While the details of each investigation differ, they all raise concerns about the impact of Google’s dominance in search, as well as the extent to which its agreements with other companies might be limiting competition.

Sebagaimana diketahui, more recently, apple’s agreement with google received significant attention during the us department of justice’s antitrust case against the search giant, which included testimony from apple executives eddy cue and john giannandrea. The latter joined Apple from Google in 2018 and led its AI efforts until stepping down earlier this year.

As a result of the US case, a federal judge ruled in August 2024 that Google had illegally maintained its monopoly in online search through anticompetitive agreements, including its deal with Apple.

Now, evidence presented during that trial has become central to a class action against Apple in Canada, which a British Columbia Supreme Court judge recently certified.

Berdasarkan laporan, the case was initially brought in 2021 by spark event rentals ltd. , an event rental company based in British Columbia. The plaintiff alleged that Apple and Google conspired to limit competition in the search market, allowing Google to charge advertisers artificially inflated prices.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apple, meanwhile, argued that its agreement with google was a legitimate distribution arrangement rather than an unlawful conspiracy. The company also maintained that Google was the appropriate defendant, describing itself as an “innocent bystander. ”.

Interestingly, the lawsuit originally named both Apple and Google as defendants, but the plaintiff later dropped Google from the case following a dispute over an arbitration clause in its advertising contracts.

With Apple now the sole defendant, Justice Thomas has allowed the case to proceed as a class action, finding sufficient grounds to examine whether Google’s payments discouraged Apple from developing its own search engine.

The lawsuit seeks financial compensation for advertisers who allegedly overpaid for Google search ads, and the court has also allowed the question of punitive damages to proceed.

The class action covers Canadian residents who purchased search ads from Google since 2005, when Apple and Google first agreed to make Google the default search engine on Safari in exchange for a share of advertising revenue.

Importantly, the ruling does not establish that Apple engaged in anticompetitive conduct, but simply allows the allegations to proceed as a class action.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the central proposition raised by these pleadings is that apple could have used its resources and distribution network to enter the search engine market, but chose not to because google paid apple billions of dollars in revenue-share payments to make google the default search provider on apple products. This arrangement gave Google market power, enabling it to charge supracompetitive advertising prices on search engines.

In my view, this pleads a common purpose to perform an act prohibited by s 45 of the Competition Act, such that it is not “clear and obvious” that the plaintiff has not pleaded an agreement between Google and Apple not to compete in the search engine market.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at one point in his decision, justice thomas cites giannandrea’s testimony and directly quotes cue’s from the us antitrust trial, before concluding that “this provides some basis in fact, supporting the inference that apple did not compete with google in the search engine market because of its agreement with google. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, interestingly, the judge also acknowledges apple’s objections to the evidence, agreeing that “the plaintiff has cherry-picked evidence to support his case,” but adding that, in his view, “it is appropriate to do so at this stage in the proceedings. ”.

With the class action greenlit, the case can now move forward toward trial, though no date has been announced yet.
