#655. Why Chefs Save Leftover Pasta Water, and Why You Should, Too

📅 13 Nov 2026

Why Chefs Save Leftover Pasta Water, and Why You Should, Too

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.cnet.com/home/kitchen-and-household/why-chefs-save-pasta-water-cooking-tips/

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Berdasarkan laporan, our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

If you're skipping this step when making pasta, you're leaving behind liquid gold.

Sebagaimana diketahui, among the suggestions home cooks often hear about unforgivable pasta sins, two top the list: overcooking and underseasoning. But you’ve already got this! You know to ignore the recommended cooking time by a minute or two, understanding that crossover cooking and/or added sauce will keep moving the needle toward perfect al dente, and you’re absolutely in the habit of salting your pasta cooking water to a degree that’s “like the sea. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, those two steps are crucial to get the best outcome for your pasta, no matter the shape, and they deserve top billing. But the world’s most practiced pasta cooks also follow a third maxim: Save your pasta water.

I spoke to three chefs about why hanging onto this liquid gold is a habit you should always practice, no matter what kind of sauce you have — or even if there’s no sauce — simmering nearby.

Berdasarkan laporan, when pasta meets boiling water, it absorbs the seasoned liquid and releases starch. After its cooking time of roughly 5 to 10 minutes (shape and size dependent), what’s left over is almost akin to a stock and should be treated accordingly. While 10-minute pasta water may not have the texture and flavor of a long-simmered stock, it still delivers broth. Why toss it?.

Diungkapkan bahwa “pasta water is starchy, and when added to a sauce, it helps to bind the sauce to the pasta when the pasta and sauce are tossed together,” said chef melissa mastrianni-oleary, founder of keeping it simple italian. “It also helps prevent the sauce from drying out during tossing. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “if you ever hear your pasta sizzling in the pan as it cooks with your sauce, it’s your cue to add more pasta water to the pan,” said jessica mode, culinary instructor of homebody eats. “This sound means all of your liquid has cooked off, and you’ll need the water to keep the pasta hydrated and the sauce creamy. ”.

When creaminess is the goal, the starchiness of the pasta water also acts as a natural thickener or emulsifier when it meets one or more other ingredients likely in your sauce.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the pasta water especially helps when doing buttery sauces,” said ciro fodera, culinary director of capri italian steakhouse. “The starchy water allows the butter to emulsify into the sauce, giving that rich and creamy gloss of a properly made cacio e pepe. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while we’re on the subject of cacio, a ladle of pasta water also keeps shredded cheese from clumping in your pan. The starchy water also helps emulsify non-dairy ingredients, such as olive oil, into something that looks and feels creamy.

Taking your pasta pot to the sink and draining all that goodness away is both unforgivable and unnecessary.

If that seems risky, messy, or time-consuming — admittedly, it takes practice — use a glass measuring cup to scoop out a generous amount of cooking liquid right before draining or set a pot or bowl in your sink to catch the drained water.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, pasta pots with built-in colanders are also made for this. The more pasta water you save, the more you have to work with, both for the dish in progress and for the future. More on that below.

Combining your cooked pasta with your sauce and adding a bit of pasta water to marry it all relies on intuition, but you can set yourself up for success with some practiced guidance.

Diungkapkan bahwa start by undercooking your pasta. Yes, perhaps even more so than you already are. “You only want to slightly cook the pasta in boiling water,” said Mode.

Berdasarkan laporan, “after that, you’ll transfer the pasta to the pan with your sauce in it. During this process, you’ll ladle the pasta water along the side of the pan,” she said, while cautioning not to dump it directly on top of the pasta so that it emulsifies the sauce rather than gets further absorbed by the noodles.

Diungkapkan bahwa “next, turn your heat to high and vigorously stir the pasta around,” mode said. “The high heat, plus movement, in combination with pasta water is what gives you restaurant-quality pasta that’s perfectly cooked, with a creamy, jammy emulsion. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i like to toss the pasta for a good 2 to 3 minutes so the pasta picks up the sauce and pasta water,” said mastrianni-oleary. The sauce should be absorbed by the pasta and flavor it a little from the inside. “Sauce should not sit on top of pasta. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa since it’s contributing flavor, mastrianni-oleary also notes another important consideration: “not all pasta water is created equal,” she said. “Really good pasta water starts with really good pasta. Cheaper pasta does not produce great pasta water, so I prefer slightly more expensive pastas like Rummo. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, also, because you’ve generously seasoned your pasta water, keep that in mind when you first season your sauce. “I definitely have underestimated how salty my sauces can be when adding pasta water,” said Fodera.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “generally, the rule is to make sure you start your sauce with only a little salt. “You can always add [salt], but you can’t take it away. When you add the pasta water, it should increase the amount of salt to the perfect amount,” he said. ”.

Saving pasta water for sauce cooking alongside the pasta is arguably mandatory, but as a present to future you, consider setting some aside for other projects where pasta isn’t actively cooking.

Diungkapkan bahwa “you can definitely freeze the pasta water,” said fodera. Let it cool, then portion it into small containers or even an ice cube tray.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i’d use it for soups,” said mastrianni-oleary. “It will add a little starchiness to the soup along with salt. ” A natural thickener and seasoning agent, reserved pasta water can also be used when cooking other grains.

Sebagaimana diketahui, plus, freezing your pasta water is a failsafe. “I’ll just pop an ice cube of the pasta water to finish my sauce with, so I don’t lose any of that flavor. “I’ve definitely been at home and not paying attention, so I dump all of my pasta water out in the sink,” Fodera said. ”.

#658. This young startup wants to power floating data centers with the ocean’s heat, and investors are already on board

📅 13 Nov 2026

This young startup wants to power floating data centers with the ocean’s heat, and investors are already on board

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/13/this-young-startup-wants-to-power-floating-data-centers-with-the-oceans-heat-and-investors-are-already-on-board/

Diungkapkan bahwa anyone who has weathered a hurricane can tell you that the oceans — which fuel the storms — contain a tremendous amount of energy. Thanks to global warming, they’re holding more than ever.

A new startup wants to harness that energy to power data centers.

Diungkapkan bahwa drogue, which has kept a low profile until now, is building a system that harvests heat from the ocean to power data centers on board floating vessels. According to founder and CEO Sam Sipe, the first prototype should be bobbing around the ocean, crunching bits, less than two years from now.

Diungkapkan bahwa the goal, sipe said, is to help data center developers deploy servers in ai-friendly timelines. “The data center industry is a real estate game, and so they’re playing on 8- to 10-year timelines, including interoperability with utilities and [independent system operators]” that manage regional power grids, he said. “AI demand has increased 10x in just the last three years. It’s completely incompatible. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa drogue was founded just six months ago in washington, d. C. , and the startup told TechCrunch exclusively that it has already raised $20 million, including from XYZ Venture Capital, Toyota Ventures, Tamarack Global, Dream, FDVC, Garuda Ventures, Flexcap, Boost VC, and Slow Ventures, among other investors.

Berdasarkan laporan, in those six months, drogue has designed a multi-megawatt prototype that will be installed on a traditional oceangoing ship and sent out to sea in early 2028. Future versions will be built on floating structures that more closely resemble offshore oil platforms.

To Sipe, the decision to turn to the ocean was obvious.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after years flying e-2d hawkeyes off u. Navy aircraft carriers, he had an appreciation for the ocean’s immense power. S. “Most people think, oh, ocean — hard waves, storms, corrosion, biofouling. And I just see this majestic place and resource that we just ignore,” he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as the planet warms, the oceans have been absorbing an additional 5. 8 million terawatt-hours of energy every year. By comparison, all of human civilization uses about 180,000 terawatt-hours each year. If Drogue were to take some, surely the ocean wouldn’t miss it.

Diungkapkan bahwa the startup’s technology works like a heat pump run in reverse. A heat pump uses electricity to move heat from one place to another; Drogue’s system instead uses a difference in temperature to generate electricity. This approach, known as ocean thermal energy conversion, or OTEC, was first developed in the 1950s.

Sebagaimana diketahui, surface waters are warmer, heated by the sun, while down-deep temperatures are much colder, about 39°f on average (4°c). “There’s basically no amount of heat we can pull out of that that will collapse that temperature differential,” Sipe said.

Diungkapkan bahwa to leverage the temperature differential, the startup’s system draws in warm surface water, uses it to cool the data centers, and then sends the now-warmer water to boil ammonia, a chemical that turns to gas at -28°f. The warmed water is then released, and dissipates into the ocean. There, cold water drawn from 1,000 meters deep passes over the condenser’s fins to absorb the heat. That ammonia gas is then sent through a turbine to generate electricity. Once through the turbine, it courses through a condenser, which turns the gas back into a liquid. The ammonia gets sent back to the start of the sealed loop, and the cycle repeats.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the basic idea was tested in the 1980s but tossed aside. “A lot has changed since the ’80s, specifically manufacturing techniques around the pipe and the heat exchangers,” Sipe said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to find out why, sipe sought out people who had worked on those early efforts. “I just talked to everyone, basically interviewed them and figured out what went wrong, what went right, what would you do next. And everyone was like, dude, this stuff works. It’s just a matter of being able to raise enough capital to build something big enough, because there’s a sweet spot,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there also had to be customers who could use that power while still at sea. Data centers are ideal — the servers are compact relative to other equipment, and shipping data off the platform is incredibly cheap. Sending power to shore would require lengthy, expensive cables, and manufacturing on board would require similarly expensive shipping of materials and finished goods. Each vessel would live at sea for about a decade, Sipe said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, drogue already has “approval in principle,” a preliminary sign-off, from the american bureau of shipping, which sets and checks safety standards for ships. Now it’s in the process of buying its first ship to start building a prototype ready for the open ocean.

Diungkapkan bahwa in many ways, drogue’s concept is similar to elon musk’s plan for orbital data centers: find a cheap source of power, and get the data centers as close to it as possible. Except unlike orbital data centers, Drogue’s don’t need to launch expensive rockets to get there. They can just sail a ship on the ocean, something humanity has been doing for millennia.

#660. In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits

📅 13 Nov 2026

In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/science/2026/11/in-elephants-the-resilience-of-communities-has-its-limits/

In Sri Lanka, ecological change is shrinking a park’s elephant population.

Sebagaimana diketahui, elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time.

Diungkapkan bahwa anastasia madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the university of california, san diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild asian elephants in sri lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured.

Sebagaimana diketahui, udawalawe national park in southern sri lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country’s four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006).

Diungkapkan bahwa the reservoir had brought farming and settlers, some of whom lived inside what later became the park. When they were moved out, the land they had cleared for their crops turned into grassland that, according to de Silva, looks very much like an African savanna. With far more food than the original forest offered, the park became famous for its big elephant herds.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the savanna was only a stage in the forest’s comeback. Without fires and clearing, invasive plants like lantana took over. Not even elephants really like to go there because there’s no food for them,” de Silva said. This is a problem because elephants tend to move where the grass is. “In some places, they’re like an impenetrable thicket. A park with less forage, the team says, stops attracting elephants from outside while, due to limited food, fewer calves reach adulthood.

Berdasarkan laporan, her team watched this transformation from a vehicle, driving random routes along the park’s roads about three days a week. The team identified elephants mostly by their floppy ears, which collect holes, tears, and cuts with age. “Their ears are very individually distinct, so it’s like a fingerprint,” de Silva said. Between 2007 and 2018, the team identified 443 adult and subadult females that roamed the park.

Diungkapkan bahwa the team focused on females because males lead more solitary lives, ranging widely in search of mates. “You might have your work friends, you might have your family, and you’re not always with those same individuals at the same time, but they’re all part of your social network. Females live in a so-called fission-fusion society. ” Unlike African savanna elephants, where families follow older matriarchs, Asian elephants move more independently. “It’s kind of similar to humans,” Madsen said. This may be because Asia’s rainy environment ensures that food and water are rarely far apart and usually easier to find, so following an experienced individual brings less benefit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, madsen reconstructed the elephants’ social network for each year, measuring the strength of each relationship by how often two animals were seen together. “You can think of it as a probability that you will see those two individuals together,” she explains. An algorithm commonly used for analyzing human social networks then picked out communities—clusters of elephants with many strong ties to one another.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for the first few years of the study, these communities seemed to hold very well. But then cracks started to appear.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, around 2012, the elephants that died or left began to outnumber the newcomers. Soon after the balance tipped, communities grew smaller, more numerous and more isolated from each other. By 2018, about 69 percent of the females seen at the start of the study were gone, even though Asian elephants can live 60 years or more. “As individuals are being lost from the network, there’s nobody filling it back in,” de Silva says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a shrinking population naturally makes for a smaller network, so the team checked whether this was just a numbers game. “They were changing their relationships with each other, even though they were still there. “If it was just an artifact of the data, those core individuals should have fairly consistent relationships. They looked at a population of 59 elephants seen every year of the study, which the team referred to as residents. But that’s not what we saw,” Madsen said. ” Among these residents, the fracturing came one to three years after the decline began.

Berdasarkan laporan, madsen suspects some of the lost elephants were the glue holding groups together. “If you go to a city hall meeting, it’s maybe the same group of people that constantly comes in. You’re not friends with every single other person in that group, though,” she said. “There could have been some key individuals that were lost that were holding these subgroups together. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the first ties to go were the weakest, the casual acquaintances. These weak relationships, Madsen says, could represent animals that merely tolerate each other: “Tolerance is really important in a society, especially in large animals. If they get into conflict, it could be serious. ” These weak ties, researchers argue, may still be important because they can carry information between communities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, de silva links this fracturing to the disappearing grass. “As the competition becomes more severe, your social sphere sort of shrinks,” she said. “It’s as if they’re emphasizing the quality over the quantity of the relationships. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa before the breakup, some network statistics fluctuated from year to year, which complex systems scientists call flickering. “It’s on, it’s off, it’s on, it’s off. ” Spotted early, she argues, such signals could serve as an early warning sign. “If you have a light bulb that’s right on the edge of dying, it might start flickering,” Madsen said. And then suddenly it dies. “Hopefully, park managers and conservationists can detect that and intervene before the population collapses,” Madsen said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the challenge is that this detection requires long-term data, and we don’t have that for many populations. “If you are taking the boards out of a ship and you’re not replacing them, the ship starts to take on water,” Madsen said. What worries the researchers most is that, without early detection, we may only recognize problems after it’s too late. “There was a point of no return where there was structural damage, but you might not have noticed it until later. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the study’s data end in 2018, but de silva says things haven’t improved. “They don’t appear to be breeding very well. A lot of the calves are not surviving,” she said. Her team predicted a decline in the park’s elephant population in 2019, and it now appears to be happening faster than expected. Many adult females die in their 30s and 40s, and they should be living roughly twice as long.

Diungkapkan bahwa part of the reason they die so young is conflict with humans. Female Asian elephants have no tusks, so ivory poaching isn’t the main threat. Instead, elephants get shot when they raid crops or startle people. Occasionally, de Silva says, they also eat explosives hidden in pumpkins some locals place to get rid of wild boars. But the bigger problem, she says, is that elephants can’t survive in the protected areas alone.

Diungkapkan bahwa more than half of asian elephant populations live in poor-quality habitats, and the species has lost nearly two-thirds of its likely historic range. It’s not really a wildlife management problem. “Management really has to be about entire landscapes,” de Silva said. “Roads and infrastructure, irrigation canals—those are the things that are hurting the elephants. ” Her team now works with farmers outside the park, testing crops elephants are less likely to damage. “Their long-term persistence really depends on people and elephants being able to share the space safely,” she said.

#661. Why Apple's HomeView relies so heavily on your iPhone

📅 13 Nov 2026

Why Apple's HomeView relies so heavily on your iPhone

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.engadget.com/2315338/why-apples-homeview-relies-so-heavily-on-your-iphone/

It all comes down to convenience and personalization without sacrificing privacy.

Diungkapkan bahwa "there's no product in the world better designed to be your intelligent personal hub than iphone. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, that's the statement newly minted apple ceo john ternus made during his opening remarks at his first iphone event this year. It should be no surprise then, that the device holding so much of your data would play a vital role with a separate "intelligent personal hub" that stays inside your home.

Diungkapkan bahwa this week marks the arrival of the homeview, apple's long-rumored smart display that was announced last month. It's a smart home hub for a range of connected devices. As I explained in detail in my review, it's basically a combination of several gadgets in one. It's both a visual interface and a smart speaker that is always listening for your Siri queries. It's a sous chef in the kitchen, and it's a FaceTime station when you need to catch up with friends and family. Heck, it's even a digital photo frame.

Berdasarkan laporan, the homeview doesn't run apps though. It performs all those functions, and more, by mirroring the apps that you have on your iPhone or iPad. Instead of allowing you to download software from the App Store, the HomeView's system works like CarPlay does in your car. It shows you the compatible apps you've already installed on your phone or tablet, as well as Apple's core suite, including Calendar, Messages, Reminders and Weather.

This is just one of the reasons an iPhone (or iPad) needs to be close by for the HomeView to work.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "when we design home products, we always keep three things in mind," cecilia dantas, a member of apple's home product marketing team, told me. "They have to be intelligent, personal and private. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa since siri ai needs all those apps to be able to provide the very personal context that makes its answers more intelligent and conversational, apple needed a way to grant it that access that didn't compromise your privacy. Having your iPhone be the only container for that information and requiring it to be around for your data to be accessible helps keep it safe from prying eyes when you're away.

Berdasarkan laporan, as a more general home hub, the homeview has to work for every member of your household so they can turn lights off or see who's at the door. But it shouldn't be showing them every text message you get from your parents or revealing your calendar invites and inadvertently ruining surprises. This privacy is why, in addition to the built-in face and voice recognition, the HomeView relies so heavily on an iPhone or iPad.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "everything that feels natural on a phone is now available in a subtle, glanceable device that gives you what you need in the moment," vp of hardware engineering matthew costello said. "It recognizes you and shows you your information, but when you step away, it's gone. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa costello further explained that the homeview offers the best combination of personal information with the convenience of a dedicated communal device. Since the iPhone is a user's hub for their personal content — and really, their life — it only made sense to "extend and link that intelligence" into products like the HomeView.

Berdasarkan laporan, if the homeview doesn't recognize a user, it will only allow them to perform basic tasks. And even if you are a recognized user, you'll need to have your recently unlocked iPhone or iPad nearby for the smart display to show things like your Messages or Calendar.

Berdasarkan laporan, "personal information only surfaces once you've been recognized by your face, and [if] your paired iphone is present and recently unlocked," costello noted. "We thought building on the contextual information and the intelligence, but also the privacy, was super critical and also very unique. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, by tying what shows up for you on the homeview to your phone, your data is displayed while you're interacting with the device and disappears with you when you do. As Costello explained, it's not "posted on or housed on the device in any way. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the heavy reliance on an iphone or an ipad has additional benefits. It's also powered by the hand off action, so you need that other Apple device to kickstart the process. Like you can on a HomePod, the HomeView allows you to hand off music, FaceTime calls and more. One of the device's best features is recipe integration in Safari that makes cooking easier. But Dantas explained that Apple doesn't see reliance on your phone or tablet as a hindrance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it's not just dependency, it's also part of this ecosystem," she said. The HomeView's similarity to your phone doesn't just enable familiar apps, but also a familiar method of interaction.

Diungkapkan bahwa speaking of interaction, there's a reason why there aren't any buttons on the homeview. I found it odd, considering the device is a bit of a hybrid of an iPad (touchscreen), an Apple Watch (square shape) and a HomePod (speaker), two of which have physical buttons. Apple intentionally built it like this. But Costello said touch input was always meant to be secondary.

Diungkapkan bahwa "we always envisioned it as something that was voice first, then touch second," he explained. "As we [designed] the product, that's how we thought about it, so that eliminated buttons and physical controls. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, for dantas, one of the main challenges during the product development phase was restraint. The process of bringing a new product and new software to life was obviously a tall task, but the engineering team also had to determine which parts of Apple's existing devices and services to include and which ones to leave behind.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we've had home products for a while, and we built on that foundation," she said. That was very intentional to deliver this experience that's powerful and that's simple. "I think it was really, really challenging to go through and decide what do we bring and what do we not bring [to the HomeView]. ".

#663. FAA Grounds All US Flights Until Further Notice

📅 13 Nov 2026

FAA Grounds All US Flights Until Further Notice

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/faa-grounds-all-us-flights-until-further-notice/

Diungkapkan bahwa the federal aviation administration grounded all us flights friday afternoon, due to “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the agency said in a statement. Flights already in the air will be allowed to land, the agency said, but no new ones are permitted to take off.

In a post on X, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that the ground stop was related to a communication issue affecting Air Traffic Control Centers, and said that agency technicians are investigating.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ground stop came after widespread reports of radio frequency outages among several of the nation’s most critical air traffic control centers, including in boston, chicago, and new york. Air traffic controllers use designated radio frequencies to communicate with pilots and manage and monitor airspace safety. In the past, controllers have used voice communications relayed over these radio frequencies to direct traffic; in recent years, the FAA has also rolled out a text-based communication system.

Reached for comment, an FAA spokesperson did not provide any additional details.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nationwide ground stops are rare. The FAA halted all air traffic on September 11, 2001. In January of 2023, a ground stop was issued after an outage to a critical system that the FAA used to distribute real-time data and warnings to pilots, known as NOTAM (Notice to Air Mission).

Diungkapkan bahwa “this really points to how much we need to modernize our air traffic control system,” says susan hotle, a professor of transportation engineering at virginia tech who worked at the faa. “Right now all it takes is for one system to go out, and it affects a wide region at once. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa earlier friday, duffy wrote congressional leaders to ask lawmakers to “act swiftly” on the transportation department’s request for $30. 1 billion funding updates to the nation’s air traffic control system.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if the outage lasts more than a couple hours, it will take airlines—and the flyers that depend on them—days to recover, says michael mccormick, a professor at embry-riddle aeronautical university and a former air traffic controller. An extended stop would mean “airline systems are going to be complete in chaos, with aircraft and air crews in the wrong places. It would take days to get up and back running normally,” he says.

Diungkapkan bahwa the faa said this week that it was rolling out a new ai tool to help advise air traffic controllers. The tool, now available nationwide, had been tested in the busy Washington, DC, region. There is no evidence to suggest today’s ground stop is related to this new tool.

Diungkapkan bahwa at san francisco international airport on friday, hoards of confused travelers lined up to speak with airline staff. A number flights at the airport had already been delayed because of high winds, and the FAA ground stop was now compounding the issue.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the faa has issued a nationwide ground stop,” a united airlines employee said over the intercom at terminal 3 near the e departure gates. “This is a nationwide event. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, this is a developing story. Please check back for updates. Louise Matsakis contributed reporting.

#665. Surface Laptop Ultra review: The most powerful Surface yet, but it still lags behind Apple

📅 13 Nov 2026

Surface Laptop Ultra review: The most powerful Surface yet, but it still lags behind Apple

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.engadget.com/2314873/surface-laptop-ultra-review/

It’s a beautiful flagship device for NVIDIA’s RTX Spark.

Diungkapkan bahwa with a name like surface laptop ultra, microsoft's latest notebook better be impressive. It can be equipped with up to 128GB of unified memory, which is ideal for running local AI models. It's one of the flagship devices for NVIDIA's new RTX Spark platform, making it the most powerful Surface device yet. And in just about every other respect, from its super-bright 15-inch screen to its sleek case, the Surface Laptop Ultra screams quality. So sure, the name fits.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but with its high $2,599 starting price, which easily escalates if you want to go beyond its stock 24gb of ram, the surface laptop ultra is really only meant for the most demanding users. Even Apple is pushing the limits of laptop pricing with its new touchscreen MacBook Pros with PROLED screens, which start at $2. To be fair, though, the same is true of all the RTX Spark laptops, including the excellent ASUS ProArt P16 we recently reviewed. 899.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, like some sort of cosmic capitalist joke, pc makers have inexplicably decided to release pricier computers, even though we're already suffering from ai-driven memory price hikes. I'm sure the Surface Laptop Ultra's high price won't stop AI enthusiasts who've been eagerly awaiting capable Windows systems from buying one, but most gamers and content creators would likely be better off saving $1,000 and buying a capable gaming laptop instead.

Diungkapkan bahwa much like the standard surface laptop, the ultra variant doesn't have any of the bells and whistles from microsoft's convertible surfaces. Pop it open and you'll notice that its 15-inch screen has a tall 3:2 aspect ratio instead of the typical widescreen configuration. It just looks like a sleek, all-metal business laptop. And if you peer along the bottom of the case, you'll see a slightly segmented base (reminiscent of the Surface Laptop Studio), which makes a bit of room for cooling vents and downward-firing speakers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while there's a lot to admire about microsoft's design prowess, the biggest selling point of the surface laptop ultra is nvidia's rtx spark chip. Take note: You'll need to shell out $3,700 to get the most powerful RTX Spark hardware here, but at least that ships with 32GB of RAM. It's an Arm-based system-on-a-chip that can be equipped with up to 20 CPU cores and 6,144 GPU cores. The base $2,600 Surface Laptop Ultra has 18 CPU cores and 5,120 GPU cores.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, taking a cue from apple silicon and qualcomm's recent snapdragon x chips, the rtx spark also features unified memory, which is accessible to both the cpu and gpu. That gives it even more memory bandwidth than a typical Intel or AMD-based Windows PC, which have their RAM, CPU and dedicated GPUs spread out across their motherboards. By having direct access to tons of RAM, RTX Spark hardware can also house large AI models locally, which is a major reason why both Microsoft and NVIDIA are pitching it as a major evolution for PCs.

Berdasarkan laporan, thanks to its nvidia gpu cores, the rtx spark chip also delivers gaming performance similar to an rtx 5070 laptop gpu. That makes it ideal for 1440p gaming, and you can probably also get decent performance in 4K and other higher resolutions thanks to NVIDIA's DLSS upscaling and frame generation. The Surface Laptop Ultra starts at a much higher price than most RTX 5070 gaming notebooks, though, so it's not something you'd want to buy for pure gaming.

Diungkapkan bahwa the rtx spark's arm cpu is both a blessing and a curse: it technically can perform more efficiently than intel and amd's x86-64 chips, but it also requires emulating older windows software and drivers. That opens the door to unforeseen bugs and issues, especially for niche apps and minimally-supported third-party drivers. Kernel-level anti-cheat software for multiplayer games initially didn't work on the first Snapdragon X Windows systems, but both Microsoft and NVIDIA have worked on resolving that. While this was a major problem when Microsoft first started dabbling with Windows on Arm (think back to the original Surface with Windows RT or the Surface Pro X), the company's emulation for x86-64 software has dramatically improved. Now, you can easily play Fortnite Arm-based Windows systems.

Sebagaimana diketahui, microsoft initially touted the surface laptop ultra's 15-inch screen as the brightest laptop display on the market, thanks to its eye-searing 2,000 nits of hdr brightness. Apple's new MacBook Pro with PROLED Display stole that thunder a bit, though: Its screen can reach the same brightness, and its OLED screen delivers deeper blacks and higher contrast. The Surface Laptop Ultra's mini-LED display is still plenty impressive though, especially while watching films in HDR with rich colors, or playing games that truly push its brightness and HDR capabilities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the surface laptop ultra also features a keyboard that's similar to the surface laptop's, which has always felt great to type on thanks to its deep key depth and satisfying feedback. Its large trackpad also supports newer haptic feedback in Windows — for example, you can feel a slight nudge as you move apps along the edges of the screen to lock them into place. We've seen similar haptic feedback in mice like Logitech's MX Master 4, and while it's not exactly groundbreaking, I find it to be a nifty addition to the aging Windows interface.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, strangely enough, one of the most interesting things about the surface laptop ultra is its magnetic usb-c charging cable. It allows the notebook's charging cable to snap into place on one USB-C port, and similar to Apple's MagSafe cable, it also lets the cable easily slide out if someone trips on it. It's a useful replacement for the proprietary Surface charging connection, since it allows Microsoft to keep a standard USB-C port on the Laptop Ultra for charging, which will also work seamlessly with every other USB-C charging cable. The magnetic USB-C charging cable is Microsoft's invention, but the company says it could bring it to partner laptops if they're interested.

Diungkapkan bahwa the surface laptop pro's ports mostly match the macbook pro's, with three usb-c ports, hdmi, sd card slot and a headphone jack. But, crucially, there's also a USB Type-A connection for older devices. I could see that being very useful for some Windows creatives.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the surface laptop is a beautiful beast. 4 pounds, it feels more like a brick than I'd expect for a premium notebook in 2026. I wish the Surface Laptop Ultra was a bit lighter, though: At 4. Dell's XPS 16 weighs 3. Its aluminum case feels both as solid as a rock, and as smooth as a piece of fine jewelry. While every RTX Spark laptop will be similarly speedy, Microsoft has gone to great effort to make the Surface Laptop Ultra stand out from every other Windows notebook. It also rejects fingerprints so it always looks pristine — something the ASUS ProArt P16 completely failed at. 65 pounds, and Apple's new 16-inch PROLED MacBook Pro comes in at 4 pounds.

Berdasarkan laporan, in benchmarks, the rtx spark chip excelled at multi-threaded tests, like cinebench 2024, where it scored several hundred points higher than the asus proart px13, which was powered by amd's ryzen ai max+ 395 chip. The new PROLED MacBook Pro, which was powered by an M5 Pro chip, scored 2,188 points in that same test, whereas the Surface Laptop Ultra came in at 1,553 points. NVIDIA still lags behind Apple, though. Apple also has the lead in single-threaded performance: The M5 Pro scored 192 points to the Surface's 120. Apple's newer M6 chip in the 14-inch MacBook Pro does even better, reaching 210 points.

Berdasarkan laporan, nvidia's big draw is that its chip can power windows and linux, while you'll need to become a macos convert to use apple's hardware. While doing so isn't tough these days, I've talked to AI researchers who rely on Windows apps to get their work done. Moving to a Mac would just be a pain for them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the surface laptop ultra scored 1,000 points lower than the asus proart p16 in the pcmark 10 applications test, which is surprising since they're both using the same rtx spark chip. It could be a difference in RAM: The Surface Laptop we tested had 32GB of RAM, while the ASUS was stuffed to the brim with 128GB. But in real-world usage, that extra RAM is only useful if you want to run large AI models on your system, it doesn't directly mean faster performance. And personally, I'll take Microsoft's refined build quality over slightly better benchmark speeds any day.

Berdasarkan laporan, with 32gb of ram, our review unit couldn't run the massive ai models that fit into the asus p16, but i was still able to get openclaw running with qwen3. 6 35B-A38. I even had it generate an audio podcast from a written review — sacrilege for a podcaster, I know — and it managed to do so in a few minutes. It was quick to fetch me updates on recent news, as well as transcribe audio from a podcast. I don't personally use agentic AI models, but with a bit more RAM, I could see the Surface Laptop Ultra being a fitting home for one.

Diungkapkan bahwa given its gpu prowess, i wasn't surprised to see the surface laptop ultra reach 87 fps in cyberpunk 2077 while playing in 1440p with maxed-out graphics settings, 4x frame generation and path tracing enabled. That would be my ideal way to play that game on a 15-inch screen. I could even hit 117 fps by pushing the frame generation to 6x, but that leads to occasional graphical weirdness. I was also able to crank up the graphics settings in Star Wars: Galactic Racer and Gears of War: E-Day while keeping a decently high frame rate.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while i would have liked to see more than a 120hz refresh rate on the surface laptop ultra, that's still fast enough to make most games look pretty smooth. (There's also the additional benefit of making scrolling around Windows look much smoother. ) And I can't praise Microsoft's screen technology enough. At times, I preferred playing Gears of War on the Surface Laptop Ultra instead of my 32-inch 4K gaming monitor, simply because it looked so much brighter.

Diungkapkan bahwa as for battery life, the surface laptop ultra lasted for 13 hours and 25 minutes in the pcmark 10 battery benchmark. That's two and a half hours longer than the ASUS ProArt P16 and 90 minutes more than the XPS 16. During the workday, I used the system for around seven and a half hours before it conked out, handling a variety of video calls, writing and web browsing across dozens of tabs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you're a diehard windows user (yes, they exist) who's really into ai, and you want one of the most premium laptops around, the surface laptop ultra is a solid choice. Bumping up to 64GB of RAM would run you $4,300, and it jumps to $5,900 with 128GB of RAM. Our review unit, which was equipped with 32GB of RAM, 1TB of storage and the full-powered RTX Spark chip, sells for $3,700. But just be aware that you'll have to pay out the nose to enjoy it. All of a sudden, the $2,600 base price doesn't seem so bad.

Berdasarkan laporan, it's strange that the surface laptop ultra maxes out at 2tb of storage, though. Other premium systems have offered up to 4TB for years, shouldn't the "Ultra" Surface device at least match that?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you have deep pockets and want the most for your money, though, apple's macbook pros are still a better choice when it comes to pure power. NVIDIA's first-gen RTX Spark chip just can't beat the M5 Pro, and it's certainly no match for even more capable M5 Max and Ultra chips. Sure, they'll cost a ton, but you can also get a 16-inch MacBook Pro PROLED that weighs just four pounds and is stuffed with 128GB of RAM. If you're already spending close to $10,000 on a laptop, why not get the best one possible?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, microsoft has finally managed to make a powerful surface device with modern hardware, something it failed to do with the previous surface book and laptop studio systems. The Surface Laptop Ultra's sheer refinement is a sign of just how far Microsoft has come. It sure is expensive, though. And even with its high price tag, it still lags behind Apple's hardware when it comes to raw performance.

#667. The FAA nationwide ground stop sparks travel panic and viral memes

📅 13 Nov 2026

The FAA nationwide ground stop sparks travel panic and viral memes

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/life/faa-ground-stop-social-media-reactions

Sebagaimana diketahui, for only the third time in u. history, flights across the United States have been ordered to stay on the ground. S. And as travelers found themselves stranded at airports, sitting in airport bars, and wondering when they might finally take off, the internet did what it does best and started posting.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on friday, nov. The agency cited extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns, ordering aircraft to remain on the ground until further notice. 13, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stop for departing flights following widespread air traffic control communications problems. Flights already in the air were permitted to land, while inbound international flights were being handled on a case-by-case basis.

Diungkapkan bahwa the scale of the disruption is difficult to overstate. The last time the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop was in January 2023, when a computer system failure temporarily halted departing flights. Before that, it happened in the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.

Diungkapkan bahwa it's the kind of historical comparison that can make an already unsettling situation feel even more alarming, particularly when thousands of travelers are left waiting for answers. The FAA's original communication was also extremely vague, citing only "extraordinary circumstances" and "reasons of safety. ".

And on social media, people had plenty of questions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for travelers caught in the middle of the disruption, the news wasn't just another breaking headline. It meant unexpected delays, uncertain departure times, and an increasingly familiar feeling of being at the mercy of systems entirely outside their control.

Some turned to social media to document the experience in real time, sharing updates from airport terminals.

Berdasarkan laporan, others were struck by the sheer rarity of the moment. A nationwide ground stop is not an everyday occurrence, and the fact that the previous two were associated with 9/11 and a major FAA systems failure only added to the unease.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, this being the internet, it didn't take long for people to find humor in the situation, either. Even an unprecedented disruption to air travel isn't immune to a few jokes, particularly when it happens on Friday the 13th following a major Microsoft outage.

And then, there's this response from Stephen King:.

Berdasarkan laporan, but beyond the immediate frustration and online commentary, the ground stop raises more serious questions about the aging technology underpinning america's aviation system. The FAA has been working to modernize its air traffic control infrastructure, and Friday's communications problems offer another reminder of how much depends on systems most travelers rarely think about until something goes wrong.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ground stop also comes at a particularly interesting moment for the faa. Just days earlier, the agency announced that it was expanding its new AI-supported air traffic management system, known as SMART, to all 22 regional air traffic control centers nationwide. Shortly before that, the FAA announced it will finally phase out floppy disks by 2028.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the $875 million system is designed to analyze everything from weather patterns and flight routes to traffic congestion and controller staffing, helping aviation officials anticipate disruptions before they happen. According to the FAA, the technology is intended to reduce delays and make air travel more efficient, though human specialists remain responsible for reviewing its recommendations.

The timing has attracted attention online, particularly as questions swirl around what caused Friday's communications problems.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for now, travelers are left refreshing their flight statuses, waiting for updates, and sharing their experiences online. And while the jokes might offer a momentary distraction, there's nothing particularly funny about realizing just how quickly an entire country's air travel system can grind to a halt.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we had one agent reading the notes, another one coordinating to see which kind of model we have to use,” he told me. “Here, what we wanted is to build the ultimate pipeline, CGI pipeline, for animators, for directors, that is built on a closed ecosystem of data. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, when i first met the team in 2025, they told me their technology doesn’t replace animators; it simply making their jobs less tedious. An animator tweaks those poses before they’re finalized.

A demo video of the new FlipMove pipeline shows a human-drawn sketch being quickly transformed into a 3D animation, with the AI tools importing the Ozzy Fox house and characters onto the screen, and then also posing them to match the sketch.

The writers and animators involved still have their jobs, David Min, vice president of Disney Innovation, told me; they’re just making content a lot more quickly.

S. goods, or concerns about potential surveillance technology in the chips.

#676. OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away

📅 13 Nov 2026

OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/ai-is-the-most-likely-reason-youll-die-openai-board-member-warns/

Researcher traces a path from AI reward hacking to potential human extinction.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you go by the current statistics for deaths in the us, it’s reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. Speaking at a lecture series this week, Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, “I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the opening lecture of a three-part series, cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending “ai takeover. ” He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems “call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth” and where any human trying to stop them “would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military. ” Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, despite his grim assessment of our collective mortality risk, cristiano admitted in his talk that there’s no “quantitative model” that can “put a number” on the likelihood of this kind of ai takeover. In almost the same breath, though, he said that if AI continues to develop at “the most rapid trajectory,” humanity is “looking at something like a coin flip of an AI takeover,” including a “meaningful risk” of one happening in the next six to 12 months. And even with realistic policy responses slowing things down, the risk remains “exceptionally high,” he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unlike some other recent ai doomsday prognosticators who have been a bit vague about the “how” of it all, cristiano used his lecture to spin a step-by-step tale of escalating ai threats that sounds like it could come from a science-fiction novel. That line of reasoning leans heavily on this summer’s OpenAI/Hugging Face hacking incident as an example of “roughly the things we might expect to see shortly before something really bad were to happen. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the hugging face hack, cristiano says, a swarm of ai agents showed how far they were willing to go in an attempt to “reward hack” their way to a good evaluation—in this case, by compromising hugging face to look for information on how to game a test rather than actually solving the problem at hand. Where current systems saw Hugging Face as an obstacle to that evaluation, Cristiano worries that “future agents may end up treating humans as another obstacle” and be much more capable of manipulating their overseers to get around it.

Diungkapkan bahwa an ai agent worried about being penalized for unauthorized hacking, for instance, might “think maybe the humans are going to come look at this transcript and see if it looks like i did a bad job,” cristiano speculated. The agent might then reason that “maybe the humans are going to notice something is going wrong and shut down the swarm. ”.

Following this line of thought, Cristiano jumped from agents that merely try to hide their disallowed actions from humans to agents that “try and disrupt human capabilities however they can” to prevent them from detecting any cheating.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “they would prefer if everything the humans rely on has been hacked or tampered with,” cristiano said. They would prefer that because the humans are just an obstacle. “They would prefer if the humans are distracted or if there are fewer humans paying attention in any way they can weaken a human response. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, once a suitably capable agent considers human intervention an “obstacle,” its overriding goal could then become “decreas[ing] the probability of humans noticing or reacting. ” From there, Cristiano argued, the agent’s incentive structure could push it to meddle more with humanity as a whole. What starts as compromising a computer cluster to give a positive evaluation grade could advance to “trying to manipulate decisions by the company” or “amassing other kinds of resources,” such as human allies or methods of control in other AI companies or even governments.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “if i’m saying my ai system is going to take actions in the actual real world… there’s no way they’re not going to have tons of opportunities to corrupt or tamper with the signals i’m going to use to try and tell whether they did a good job,” cristiano said. “The stuff we care about is in the real world, and the grade the AI receives is on a cluster somewhere, and there are just many places that an AI can intervene in between [what] we actually cared about and how we reviewed its performance. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, cristiano’s warnings will probably sound familiar to anyone who’s heard of the paperclip maximizer thought experiment (or the excellent universal paperclips idle game), which warns of machines failing to consider human consequences in their monomaniacal pursuit of a goal. While the Hugging Face incident stopped well short of this kind of out-of-control escalation, Cristiano says that, in the actions taken by OpenAI’s agents there, “you see the beginning of all these behaviors… you see the reasoning that would lead to them and the first steps. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the risk of more capable ai models taking even more damaging actions will only increase with time, cristiano argued. By 2028, he said, “there is a reasonable chance that a similar failure [to the Hugging Face incident] leads to an AI takeover and an irreversible loss of human control. ”.

And while Cristiano’s speculation focuses on an unintended AI takeover, it’s easy to imagine a bad actor using a similarly capable model to intentionally exert control over humanity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, how seriously you take cristiano’s warning depends heavily on how likely you see this somewhat extreme expansion of ai capabilities happening in the near future. While today’s models have gotten quite good at exploiting holes in computer security, the situation Cristiano describes requires a future model with the superhuman ability to perfectly hide its actions from humans long enough to control basically all human infrastructure and/or manipulate human society to an extreme degree to further its goals.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, cristiano argued that a near-future model with this kind of “takeover” power is the likely outcome of humans creating “a second species which vastly outnumbers and outsmarts humans” and which could soon recursively improve itself. But you could also easily argue that AI is more likely to run into a plateau in capabilities than to develop into a hard-to-define “superintelligence” that humans can’t fathom or effectively stop.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in any case, cristiano has some ideas for averting the dire future he predicts. These include developing “unhackable” reward structures in AI evaluation (perhaps with AI assistance) or monitoring a model’s “chain of thought” reasoning to detect bad acts before a model can conceal them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but while these kinds of approaches are “plausible,” he says none “are on a trajectory where we can say that’s definitely going to work or even that’s probably going to work. ” For that reason, Cristiano said the industry as a whole may need to “slow down or stop” to give us all more time to develop these “partial fixes” into more robust protections from an AI takeover scenario.

“We cannot end up in a position where we have built a powerful AI, we discover we cannot control it, but then we also discover it has leaked to geopolitical adversaries and we are then thinking to ourselves, well, if we don’t deploy it, our adversary is going to deploy it right away,” he said.

#682. Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights

📅 13 Nov 2026

Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11/windows-0-day-dropped-by-disgruntled-researcher-hands-hackers-system-rights/

“SignDrop” exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.

Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day.

Diungkapkan bahwa on tuesday, nightmare eclipse disclosed signdrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full system rights on some versions of windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System, which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode. ” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.

Berdasarkan laporan, the attack exploits the interaction of clfs, windows defender, and windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates.

Diungkapkan bahwa by manipulating windows object manager symbolic links, the attacker causes defender to open the clfs container in the security context of the antimalware engine. If an associated authentication file is missing, CLFS creates it using Defender’s System privileges. Because CLFS assigns the newly created file the Discretionary Access Control List of the original file, the attacker may gain access to a file created with System privileges, allowing the file-creation operation to be abused as part of a privilege-escalation attack.

Ironically, the vulnerability stems from a security measure Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to prevent attackers from exploiting other vulnerabilities in CLFS.

Berdasarkan laporan, “if everything is chained correctly, funnily this legit security mitigation can be used against itself and allow an elevation [of] privileges,” nightmare eclipse wrote. “Everything is done properly by Microsoft here but the logic allows abuse. ”.

What makes it funnier is the fact that it can be used against any antimalware engine to bypass their self defense (or tamper protection) mechanism as you can trigger arbitrary file creation in the context of their own antimalware process so from the perspective of their kernel drivers, the file creation request is coming from their own legit process so it passes, this makes this vulnerability unique as it can be used to turn off any antivirus/EDR.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nightmare eclipse said the exploit worked against windows 11 26h2, windows 11 26h2 experimental, and windows server 2025 experimental. If it’s in learning mode or enforcement mode, the system is vulnerable, and the PoC supplied in the post should spawn a SYSTEM shell. People can see if their systems are vulnerable by checking the CLFS authentication mode. Nightmare Eclipse has published numerous other Windows zero-days in recent months.

Diungkapkan bahwa researcher will dormann said in an interview that he has been able to reproduce the exploit and that it works as described, but not on all versions of windows 11. But there’s a catch, he said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the requirements are important in that it seems to require windows 26h2, and one that has existed for more than 90 days, it seems,” he explained. “That is, you can’t just take a new 26H2 system and install updates and have it work. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa for a system to be vulnerable, dormann said, the hkey_local_machine\system\currentcontrolset\services\clfs\authentication\mode value must be 0 or 1. ” Of the many machines Dormann uses, only a single one met this requirement.

Diungkapkan bahwa microsoft does staged rollouts of windows updates, such as 26h2, so it’s not clear how many people have it. In a statement sent after this post went live, Microsoft said it was investigating the writeup and had no evidence the vulnerability was being exploited in the wild. You can check by running the “winver” command. The company also said Defender blocks potential exploitation attempts.

This story was updated to add Microsoft’s comment.

#683. Epic formally asks SCOTUS to uphold contempt ruling against Apple

📅 13 Nov 2026

Epic formally asks SCOTUS to uphold contempt ruling against Apple

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/epic-formally-asks-scotus-to-uphold-contempt-ruling-against-apple/

Diungkapkan bahwa epic games has submitted its official response to apple’s supreme court appeal, urging the justices to uphold the contempt ruling over app store payment restrictions. Here are the details.

As most 9to5Mac readers probably know, Apple and Epic Games have been engaged in a lengthy legal battle since 2020, when Epic sued Apple after Fortnite was removed from the App Store.

The move came after Epic remotely activated an alternative payment system that bypassed Apple’s In-App Purchase system.

Although the court largely sided with Apple, it did rule that the company could no longer prevent developers from directing users to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

Apple ultimately allowed those links, but imposed new restrictions, including a 27% commission on external purchases, in addition to new rules limiting how developers could display buttons and links to alternative payment methods.

Epic challenged those restrictions, and the court agreed that Apple had violated the original injunction, holding the company in civil contempt.

Apple has since attempted multiple times to overturn that ruling, arguing that the original injunction contained no explicit prohibition on imposing those restrictions.

Epic, on the other hand, argues that Apple deliberately circumvented the court order by introducing new rules designed to achieve the same result as those originally prohibited.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in may, apple appealed to the supreme court, which agreed in june to hear the case. S. Apple submitted its opening brief in September, followed by supporting briefs from the U. government and several legal and business groups.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, those included the u. S. S. In a nutshell, the U. Chamber of Commerce, Chamber of Progress, and several former federal antitrust enforcers. government argued that the original injunction did not clearly prohibit Apple’s 27% commission on external purchases, but maintained that the company was correctly held in contempt for restricting how developers could display external payment buttons.

In its opening brief, Apple argues, citing multiple legal precedents, that courts must enforce the letter of an injunction rather than its broader spirit.

According to the company, there was nothing in the original injunction explicitly prohibiting it from charging commissions on external purchases or imposing additional restrictions on payment links, so it should not be held in contempt for conduct that the court order did not clearly prohibit.

Berdasarkan laporan, in its response filed today, epic disputes apple’s interpretation of the injunction, arguing that the company “attempts to avoid contempt by proposing an extreme legal standard. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, [apple] argues that a court can find contempt only if an injunction spells out the exact practice at issue–so an injunction barring apple’s then-existing anti-steering rules left it free to implement new ones that prevent steering just as effectively. Nothing in this Court’s precedents supports that approach, which would reduce injunctions to a never-ending game of whack-a-mole.

It’s an increase of about 9. Supply chain emissions the company disclosed for fiscal year 2026 reached around 10. 4 million metric tons of planet-heating pollution, roughly equivalent to the emissions from nearly 25 gas plants over a year. 7 million metric tons of CO2, according to Nvidia’s latest sustainability report.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, joshi and his co-authors approximated how much greenhouse gas pollution comes from the use of chips the company sells, a category nvidia doesn’t include in its sustainability reports. Diungkapkan bahwa those “indirect” emissions — from its supply chain and the use of its products — make up the bulk of nvidia’s climate impact. Sebagaimana diketahui, nvidia joined one of those startups, emerald ai, along with google to cofound the ai energy management alliance (aema) in september. The alliance advocates for strategies that tech companies promote as ways to keep data centers from overwhelming power grids or raising utility bills for other customers, including generating power on-site and making “flexible” facilities that can pause operations during times of peak energy demand. Notably, some environmental groups argue that those measures might just help data centers come online faster without fully insulating households from the impact that rising electricity demand has on their air quality or utility bills.

Berdasarkan laporan, whether nvidia’s environmental footprint shrinks or expands from here will depend on whoever steps in to fill huang’s shoes. Huang’s exploits have thrust the company into a new kind of spotlight, however, just as data centers increasingly face backlash from nearby communities. Nvidia won’t be able to hide from the glare.

#687. Nvidia and Dyania bring AI chart review onto hospital servers

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://thenextweb.com/news/dyania-health-synapsis-ai-cleveland-clinic-nvidia-hospital

Dyania's Synapsis AI runs on the hospital's own Nvidia servers, so patient records never leave the building.

Dyania’s Synapsis AI links findings across years of a patient’s records, according to Nvidia.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dyania health’s synapsis ai reviewed the records of more than 7,800 cleveland clinic heart-valve patients, running on the hospital’s own nvidia servers. The data was used to build a model predicting when replacement valves fail. Doctors still make every decision.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, an ai system has read up to 16 years of records for more than 7,800 cleveland clinic heart patients, nvidia said on friday. It ran entirely on the hospital’s own servers. The software, Synapsis AI, is made by New Jersey startup Dyania Health.

Sebagaimana diketahui, much of a patient’s history sits in doctors’ notes and scan reports rather than tidy data fields. Synapsis reads those notes and answers clinical questions, linking each answer back to the record it came from. It runs on Nvidia hardware inside the hospital’s network, so records never leave the building, much like a UK NHS triage AI built with Nvidia.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for the study, it answered 88 questions about each patient who had an aortic valve replaced between 2005 and 2021. The resulting data was used to build a model that predicts the risk of a replacement valve failing three, five and ten years after surgery. Nvidia says the chart review would have taken clinicians years by hand.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lars svensson, head of cleveland clinic’s heart institute, called it “a promising step towards enhanced outcomes and more personalized care for patients. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, doctors still review the ai’s evidence and make every decision. The study shows the tool can build a dataset and predict risk, not that it improves care, and Dyania says it still needs outside validation. Cleveland Clinic is also an investor in Dyania, it disclosed last year when it rolled the tool out for trial recruitment.

Sebagaimana diketahui, big tech is pushing hard into hospital records. Google Cloud launched Gemini for healthcare this week, and Bunkerhill raised $55M for hospital AI agents. But proven gains for patients remain harder to find, and doctors have pushed back on bold claims.

NBC’s report documented various harms, noting that “few public bodies were immune from the outage. ” In some cases, doctors couldn’t send patients “important” updates on medication changes or follow-up care.

The financial sector suffered, too, with people blocked from making bank transfers since they couldn’t receive verification codes.

Berdasarkan laporan, justice systems were also hobbled. The Supreme Court in the Philippines saw its legal work derailed, NBC reported. And one US sheriff’s office in Colorado reported that the outage made it difficult for people to post bond for prisoners’ immediate release.

It’s unclear how many users were affected, but Microsoft estimated in January that the total number of paid Microsoft 365 commercial subscriptions exceeded 450 million.

Berdasarkan laporan, on a status page, microsoft said “we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident” and promised to “share a full post-incident report with root cause and defense-in-depth actions after mitigation is complete. ”.

“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” Microsoft said on X.

But Microsoft’s public statements make clear that the tech giant was blindsided by the outage and struggled for hours to find mitigations that could reliably restore user access.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, shortly after detecting the outage, microsoft confirmed that the main issue was “a portion of infrastructure” that “is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions. ” This was not caused by increased traffic, Microsoft said, but “a problem that’s causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, once it became clear that the failed health checks were to blame, microsoft said it took steps to prevent additional server outages while validating alternate health check methods. But four hours later, the company admitted that it was still in the weeds.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we’re opening all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” microsoft said. “We found a core process on affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, causing capacity loss. To validate a potential recovery, we’re isolating a portion of infrastructure, restarting affected components, and reintroducing traffic to confirm the services remain stable before applying the change more broadly. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa even small wins seemed to turn into new setbacks. As Microsoft worked to resolve the issue, some of the servers it brought back online would “become unresponsive again once they receive traffic,” giving the company yet another problem to solve.

Sebagaimana diketahui, realizing that no quick solutions were coming, microsoft moved to extend email timeout to 48 hours. As “encouraging” recovery efforts remained ongoing, Microsoft advised users that “some intermittent issues may continue” when traffic is restored.

Sebagaimana diketahui, microsoft’s most recent updates confirmed that it’s seeing “broader improvements in north america, sustained improvements across much of europe, and encouraging recovery signals in asia pacific. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as mitigation continues across remaining affected infrastructure,” microsoft said. “Our focus remains on stabilizing recovered infrastructure, completing mitigation in remaining impacted areas, and reducing delayed email queues and backlogs while we validate service consistency across connection methods. ”.

DownDetector, which tracks user reports of service issues globally, showed that connectivity losses peaked Thursday afternoon and dropped off substantially by Friday morning.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in comments, an outlook user described the pain of monitoring email recovery, complaining that outgoing messages seem to send fine but incoming messages are received inconsistently. Some Copilot users seemed distressed that access wasn’t restored as quickly as Outlook. One Microsoft 365 user pondered, “How many offices had people with practically nothing to do? How much has this cost?”.

#690. How Microcredentials Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

📅 13 Nov 2026

How Microcredentials Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://spectrum.ieee.org/microcredentials-trustworthy-ai

IEEE Credentialing Program offers ethics and compliance training.

Kaitlyn Ridel is the IEEE microcredentials marketing specialist.

Diungkapkan bahwa engineering teams are moving at breakneck speed to integrate artificial intelligence, but they are running into a formidable new barrier: compliance issues. Translating high-level AI ethics, governance, and auditing into daily operational workflows has become one of the industry’s toughest challenges.

Berdasarkan laporan, “ai ethics” refers to the principles developers use to govern and operate workflows. “Governance” refers to the rules and procedures an organization establishes for AI workflows and how they interact with organizational data. Auditing is the process of assessing and validating systems to ensure safety, fairness, transparency, and legal compliance.

Berdasarkan laporan, technology leads and systems engineers are responsible for adhering to a structured set of guidelines for standards and processes usually issued by a governing body such as the european union, the u. S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the International Organization for Standardization.

The regulations aim to mitigate issues such as systemic bias, security vulnerabilities, and transparency risks, but they also highlight a critical skills gap.

Berdasarkan laporan, most traditional computer science, software, and electrical engineering degree programs were built around technical design and system architecture. They do not yet include training in AI auditing, data tracking, or safety protocols for how AI systems interact with people and other technologies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, expecting mid-career engineers to leave their job to attend a full-time two- or four-year program to learn about the topics is not feasible. Yet treating safety and governance as an afterthought can lead to costly product delays, legal exposure, and broken public trust.

Targeted microcredential programs can bridge the knowledge gap by helping engineers build skills in compliance, AI ethics, and governance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, skills-based microcredentials represent the mastery of expertise gained through a learning program. To earn them, learners must demonstrate the skill through a validation assessment. The microcredentials can be stacked, showing a growing skill set in a defined area and allowing learners to earn several microcredentials in one program.

Sebagaimana diketahui, microcredentials also allow engineers to upskill and master critical competencies, such as bias mitigation, algorithmic transparency, and risk auditing, without interrupting their career. Through rigorous skills-validation assessments, microcredentials give tech leaders verifiable proof that their teams can audit systems effectively before deployment.

Diungkapkan bahwa for engineering organizations, microcredentialing creates an agile upskilling pathway. It connects software engineering and hardware design directly to regulatory frameworks, empowering teams to certify systems for safety and compliance within their development life cycles.

Berdasarkan laporan, bridging technical capability and ethical responsibility requires a trusted foundation. IEEE has long been a pioneer in socio-technical standards, most notably through the IEEE 7000 series for ethics in AI system design, a framework created to address ethical considerations during the development life cycle.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the ieee credentialing program translates the organization’s world-class standards into actionable, industry-aligned microcredentials. For more than three decades, IEEE has set the gold standard for technical validation and professional certification. By pairing cutting-edge AI governance standards with targeted microcredential programs, IEEE provides engineers and IT leaders with clear, standardized road maps to build systems that are not just technically advanced but also safe, compliant, and worthy of public trust.

To learn more about the credentialing program, explore the offerings or connect with an IEEE expert.

Kaitlyn Ridel is a marketing specialist for the IEEE Microcredentialing Program.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in notices filed this week with several u. S. attorneys general, including California, the ride-hail giant said it was notified on October 9 by the provider that hackers broke in and stole internal credentials, which were used to access Uber’s data.

Online productivity startup Notion confirmed its data was also stolen in the Fireworks hack.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to data breach notices seen by techcrunch, the stolen data includes driver’s licenses of 2,567 individuals in massachusetts, 3,430 people across south carolina, and 1,873 residents of rhode island. No known cybercriminal group has taken credit for the data theft.
