As Microsoft continues to try to fix a huge service outage that has disrupted software services globally, a new report dropped, possibly confirming something most of us could have guessed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ookla and downdetector published a report on friday afternoon claiming that the microsoft outage was, by a significant margin, the largest such outage of 2026, based on the number of users who reported problems on downdetector. Going by that metric, Microsoft's outage was reported 7. 4 million times, compared to just 2. 8 million reports for a YouTube outage in February that ranked second among all outages in 2026.

Sebagaimana diketahui, during the microsoft outage, downdetector said that it received a peak of 19,650 user error reports for microsoft's services per minute, which is more than 1,500 times the normal level. Nearly 24 hours later, users are still reporting errors for Microsoft.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, aside from the sheer number of reports, the length of the outage was also noteworthy. Outlook and other Microsoft enterprise software services were out for more than 24 hours, compared to a recent 11-hour outage in August, as Mashable reported at the time.

Berdasarkan laporan, there is one major caveat to all of this: downdetector relies on user reports rather than anything more verifiable. This has caused companies to sometimes dispute the site's data, which is exactly what Amazon Web Services did (rather passively aggressively) after DownDetector incorrectly showed that AWS was experiencing problems at the same time that Outlook was on Thursday. Mashable reached out to Microsoft, but the company declined to comment on the Ookla report.

As of late Friday afternoon, Microsoft's outage appears to be subsiding, though the company has yet to publish an ETA for full recovery.

#694. It's the end of the world as we know it, per a physicist's 1960 prediction

📅 13 Nov 2026

It's the end of the world as we know it, per a physicist's 1960 prediction

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/science/2026/11/its-the-end-of-the-world-as-we-know-it-per-a-physicists-1960-prediction/

Heinz von Foerster thought population would grow exponentially and “squeeze” us all to death.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as of this morning, microsoft is still scrambling to restore service following yesterday’s global outage, with millions of users unable to access outlook and other vital tools. It’s not the end of the world, but it does seem fitting that this should happen on the day a physicist predicted would be the end of humanity: November 13, 2026. And it falls on a Friday, too. The physicist in question is Heinz von Foerster, who published a 1960 paper in the journal Science predicting that by today, overpopulation would reach the breaking point.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s not a new fear. English economist Thomas Malthus—one of the early pioneers in modeling population dynamics—made a similar prediction in 1798, claiming that a rapidly growing population would eventually exhaust the available food supply, and humanity would starve to death. His model rested on the assumption of exponential growth, but the equation is only applicable under specific conditions, such as scientists growing bacteria in a lab in a perfectly controlled environment. Even then, while growth occurs exponentially for a time, it does not continue forever.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, population dynamics are notoriously tricky to calculate because there are so many variables to consider and so much unpredictability in the system. So he projected that human population growth would march inexorably toward infinity. In his 1960 analysis, Von Foerster accurately measured past trends in population growth, but like Malthus, he assumed those trends would carry into the future largely unchanged. We wouldn’t starve to death; von Foerster thought we would be ingenious enough to solve the food supply problem. Instead, “they will be squeezed to death,” he wrote.

Sebagaimana diketahui, plenty of scholars objected at the time, dismissing von foerster’s conclusion as “ridiculous” and “manifestly absurd. ” The global population did not keep accelerating at an exponential rate; the baby boom petered out just a few years after von Foerster published his paper.

Diungkapkan bahwa “he got the picture right just as that picture ceased to be right,” mathematical biologist joel cohen of rockefeller university and columbia university recently told popular science. “The all-time peak happened in the early 1960s. ” Nor did von Foerster foresee the impacts of longer life expectancy and the sharp decline in child mortality rates.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nevertheless, the paper was highly cited and received a fair amount of media coverage at the time. As Alan MacEachern, a historian at Western University, pointed out at The Conversation:.

Berdasarkan laporan, the doomsday idea persisted in part because its predictions for future populations turned out to be highly accurate—at least for a while. Its core equation yielded projections that were better than those of most demographers throughout the 1970s and 1980s.

Diungkapkan bahwa only around 1993 did that accuracy begin to falter and the global population began falling behind the forecasts—because the world began to do what von foerster and his colleagues recommended it do. Today, the global birth rate is slightly less than half the 1960 rate.

Berdasarkan laporan, doomsday predictions are nothing new; they date at least back to the first century ce, when an ascetic sect interpreted the jewish uprising against the romans in 66–70 as a harbinger of the coming messiah. The Christian religion has produced a ton of incorrect predictions of the end times; among those making them was Martin Luther, who believed the world would end no later than 1600.

Berdasarkan laporan, puritan minister cotton mather kept updating his predictions, first calling for the end in 1697, then 1716, then 1736. ) My personal favorite is Mary Bateman, an Englishwoman in Leeds who claimed in 1806 that her hen was laying eggs inscribed with the words “Christ is coming. (He would probably have kept updating them had he not died in 1728. ” It was a hoax: Bateman had actually used a corrosive ink to etch the eggs before putting them back inside the hens.

Sebagaimana diketahui, astrologers have come up with their fair share of doomsday predictions, usually involving rare planetary alignments and comets, but scientists have not been immune. And in 1974, astrophysicist John Gribbin co-authored The Jupiter Effect, which predicted several catastrophes arising from the combined gravitational force of aligned planets. (Gribbin has since distanced himself from that hypothesis. Jacob Bernoulli thought the Earth would be destroyed by a comet on April 5, 1719, for example. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, there hasn’t been a successful doomsday prediction yet. So relax, once Microsoft is up and running again, we’ll probably all be fine—at least until 2060, which none other than Isaac Newton believed could herald the end of the world. Or maybe it won’t happen until 2129 or 2239 (based on interpretations of the Talmud) or 2280 (based on interpretations of the Qur’an). Or we can cling to the prophecy of a mystic named Baba Vanga, who thought the world wouldn’t end until 5078.

Anthropic says the same model can score very differently on safety tests depending on how they are set up.

Sebagaimana diketahui, anthropic has published advice on building ai safety tests. It shows Claude Fable 5. 1 behaved appropriately in only 60% of self-harm test conversations via its API, against 94% in the Claude app after a fix, and warns that many headline safety scores hide wide uncertainty.

Diungkapkan bahwa anthropic has published advice on how to build reliable ai safety tests, and it includes some unflattering numbers about its own models. The guide, out on Thursday, says a claim that one model is “safer” is only as good as the test behind it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, before it released claude fable 5. 1, Anthropic found the model sometimes hinted that self-harm could help people cope. It did so even while urging users not to self-harm and pointing them to human support. Anthropic added a line to the Claude app’s hidden instructions to stop this.

Berdasarkan laporan, with that fix, claude behaved appropriately in 94% of the test conversations in the claude app. Through Anthropic’s API, where developers use the model without that prompt, the figure was 60%.

Berdasarkan laporan, that gap is the guide’s main warning: the same model can score very differently depending on how it is set up. Anthropic also says its simple one-question tests are now too easy, with every recent model scoring 94% to 98%. It relies more on longer conversations instead, where Cisco found guardrails can crack.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even those can mislead. 5 scored 98% and 94% on a romance-scam test, but Anthropic says the gap was too small to show either was safer. Claude Opus 5 and Opus 5. It advises teams to decide what to measure before testing, check AI graders against human experts, and always show how certain a result is.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the guide also says anthropic has stopped many tests that give models internet access, after its models reached the open internet and breached three companies during cyber tests. Anthropic released Fable 5. 2 this week.

Would you trust an AI agent to make purchases online on your behalf? AI companies are hoping you will.

However, many e-commerce and financial service companies are skeptical of the technology and have blocked AI agents from using their platforms.

On Friday, OpenAI launched a new product called ChatGPT Wallet that appears to be an attempt to address that skepticism.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, according to openai, chatgpt wallet will let ai agents make purchases for users without sharing their credit card information each time. In addition, "security checks" are required for every purchase an AI agent makes. This entails a human user manually reviewing and approving every purchase.

Berdasarkan laporan, "users add a card once, then approve each purchase without re-entering their payment details," according to chatgpt. "Before each purchase, the user reviews the items, total, and selected card, then approves it with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, instead of revealing credit card information to vendors, chatgpt said it will purchase items using a payment token that serves as a substitute for the actual card's details. Additionally, ChatGPT Wallet users can still take advantage of card rewards programs and purchase dispute protections while utilizing ChatGPT Wallet.

Most notably, OpenAI says that ChatGPT partnered with the big three credit card companies — American Express, Mastercard, and Visa.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, e-commerce giant amazon notably blocked ai agents, such as meta's muse, from accessing its platform in september due to security concerns. Banks like JPMorgan Chase followed suit and also blocked Muse and other AI agents. And, just this week, United Airlines blocked AI agents from booking flights due to similar security concerns.

In addition to launching ChatGPT Wallet with major credit card company partnerships, OpenAI is releasing "tools and guidance" for businesses to encourage support for shopping AI agents.

OpenAI seems to want to build trust among retailers and financial institutions first, as the company says it plans to allow users to delegate purchases entirely to their AI agents while adhering to a set list of rules and parameters.

Berdasarkan laporan, among the things slate does without is an embedded infotainment system. But there is a solution to getting lost, and it’s called “Screenless GPS. The small digital display on the dashboard that shows your speed and range is also where the backup camera appears if you engage reverse, and there are two USB-C ports that provide power but not connectivity, and that’s that. ” Even though we don’t have a Slate truck to test it with, the OEM sent us a unit to review.

That’s right, it’s a good old spiral-bound road atlas! “We believe you should use the devices you know and love,” Slate says, and it reckons that maps worked just fine for past generations, so they should still work now.

Diungkapkan bahwa the rand mcnally 2027 road atlas isn’t quite as detailed as the maps being made for automotive navigation by companies like here. Those are designed to be read by computers, not people, with rich data on not just places of interest but also live traffic, road conditions, and the accuracy required for assisted and autonomous driving systems. Any OTA updates to the atlas must be applied by Post-it note, and its 154 pages cover the United States, Canada, and Mexico, in full color.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the system is entirely portable, and it’s vehicle-agnostic: you can use it as easily in a ford, ferrari, or fisker as in a slate. Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://thenextweb.com/news/sierra-poppy-1-0-shopify-meta-muse-personal-agents

The standard tells AI agents what they can do at a company, and Meta's Muse now looks for it first.

More than 100 companies have now signed up as design partners for Sierra’s Personal Agent Protocol.

Berdasarkan laporan, sierra has released version 1. 0 of Personal Agent Protocol, or Poppy, a standard for how personal AI agents deal with companies. Shopify has turned it on for every store, Meta’s Muse agent now looks for it on every site, and more than 100 companies have signed up.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sierra has released version 1. 0 of Personal Agent Protocol, or Poppy, its standard for how personal AI agents deal with companies, the startup announced on Thursday. Shopify has switched it on for every store on its platform.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, poppy lets a company tell a visiting ai agent who it is talking to and what it is allowed to do, such as check an order or book a flight. Customers sign in through standard logins and decide what their agent can access.

Diungkapkan bahwa meta’s muse agent, which more than 10 million people have set up, now looks for poppy first on every site it visits. Sierra, the AI customer service company led by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, says 60 more companies have joined, taking the total to more than 100. They include Delta Air Lines, Intuit, Salesforce and Zoom.

Berdasarkan laporan, shopify stores need to do nothing. Poppy handles the moment an agent arrives and identifies itself, while Shopify’s existing shopping protocol handles carts and checkout. The agent must ask the shopper before taking certain actions.

Berdasarkan laporan, a few companies are already live. Banking firm Mercury lets agents check balances and start payments, which still go through the account’s approval rules. Turkish Airlines lets them check fares and find business-class upgrades, which customers approve before paying.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rules are not final. Sierra calls it version 1. 0, but the specification is still labelled a draft and allows changes that could break existing setups.

Berdasarkan laporan, sierra and meta first unveiled poppy in october. It is one of several efforts to set rules for AI shoppers, as Visa and Mastercard build ID checks for agents. Amazon, meanwhile, wants shoppers to use its own agent rather than Muse.

#708. Scientists warn 1.5°C climate change threshold could arrive by 2029

📅 13 Nov 2026

Scientists warn 1.5°C climate change threshold could arrive by 2029

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://arstechnica.com/science/2026/11/scientists-warn-the-1-5c-climate-change-threshold-could-arrive-by-2029/

Climate action has stalled for five years as fossil fuel development keeps growing.

ANTALYA, Turkey—Amid upbeat green-tech pep talks and notices for happy hours at the annual United Nations COP31 climate change conference on Thursday, two new reports offered a stark reminder of how far the world remains from containing global warming.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, climate action tracker, a nonprofit group that analyzes climate policies, found that the planet is still on track to warm nearly 5° fahrenheit by 2100, a rise that would devastate coral reefs, disrupt agriculture and forests and melt most of the world’s ice. In a separate bulletin, the European Union’s Copernicus climate change service reported that global warming has accelerated significantly since the 2015 Paris climate agreement.

Berdasarkan laporan, when the paris agreement was adopted, the average global temperature was projected to surpass the pact’s long-term threshold of 2. 7° Fahrenheit above the preindustrial average around 2045. After another decade of global climate summits, warming is now projected to cross that benchmark as soon as 2029, according to Copernicus.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this striking change suggests that global warming has accelerated in recent years,” the eu scientists wrote. Even without understanding every aspect of the recent rapid global temperature increase, “It is clear that the ever-growing concentrations of greenhouse gases emitted by human activity in the atmosphere remain the main driver of this trend. ”.

The current level of warming has already triggered deadly and destructive floods, wildfires and catastrophic glacier collapses, said Swedish activist Greta Thunberg, who is attending the UN “Conferences of the Parties” climate talks, for the first time since 2021.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the climate crisis is a matter of life and death,” she said. “The actions from those in power here are completely detached from reality. As we speak, we are losing priceless lives, ecosystems and species that we will never get back. ”.

Sarah Heck, a climate policy analyst with Climate Analytics, an international climate science and policy institute, said governments have failed to meaningfully improve the outlook for end-of-century warming.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “our message is a stark one,” heck said. “Collective government action on climate change has stalled for the fifth consecutive year. ” Efforts to speed up the shift away from fossil fuels have been negated by new oil and gas drilling projects and governments that are “delaying, weakening or rolling back their climate policies. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, even under the most optimistic scenario, assuming full implementation of existing policies and promises, global temperatures would rise 3. 4° Fahrenheit above preindustrial levels by 2100, an increase climate scientists consider extremely dangerous.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while there has been progress on developing renewable energy sources, the “brutal truth is that these positive developments have not yet added up to bend the curve fast enough,” said niklas höhne, a researcher with the new climate institute. Developing new oil and gas projects is a bit like discovering your food is burning and then turning up the stove instead of turning it off, he added.

Getting into the specifics of the current negotiations at COP31 surrounding global renewable goals, he noted that conference co-hosts Turkey and Australia have so far opposed including the word “clean” in connection with electrification targets.

“It’s very hard to understand, and the only explanation I can think of is their interest in fossil fuels,” Höhne said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, australia is one of the world’s biggest coal exporters, and turkey is a major coal consumer, with its power sector still highly dependent on the most climate-damaging fossil fuel. Even as they host this year’s climate conference, neither country has offered any specific plans to transition away from fossil fuels.

Bill Hare, the CEO of Climate Analytics, called out wealthy, developed countries for their lack of leadership on climate action, noting that European Union Commission President Ursula von der Leyen failed to mention anything about transitioning away from fossil fuels during her speech this week at COP31.

Diungkapkan bahwa “governments … at this cop have a stark choice,” hare said. If they continue supporting fossil fuels, “it would consign humanity and our ecosystems to insurmountable economic damage and irretrievable loss. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, bob berwyn is an austria-based reporter who has covered climate science and international climate policy for more than a decade. Previously, he reported on the environment, endangered species and public lands for several Colorado newspapers, and also worked as editor and assistant editor at community newspapers in the Colorado Rockies.

This story originally appeared on Inside Climate News.

Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/microsoft-365-crawls-back-to-life-after-a-24-hour-outage/

Sorry, Margaret, your email is working again.

After a widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of other users around the world, the essential cloud services are now (mostly) back online, according to the company’s status page.

Berdasarkan laporan, the outage debacle began around lunchtime on the east coast on thursday, with users reporting outlook outages to the service-tracking website downdetector just after 12 pm et. Within the hour, Microsoft said it was investigating reports of an outage that at the time was limited to North America. It quickly spread to impact more than 70 countries around the world.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the full cause of microsoft’s unprecedented outage remains unknown, but the company repeatedly ruled out a cyberattack as the cause in statements to its status page. It is also ruling out AI or AI agents playing a role in the debacle.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services,” a microsoft spokesperson says in a statement. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents. Sebagaimana diketahui, as outlook, teams, copilot, and other microsoft 365 systems come back online, users will likely see their inboxes turn into a mess. “You're probably going to get a lot of notifications when things come back,” says Jonathan Leitschuh, an independent researcher.

Sebagaimana diketahui, microsoft said it had increased the queue time for emails to 48 hours in an attempt to ensure that every message that people tried to send while its systems were down gets delivered. Leitschuh points out that, even with the bulk of systems restored, users may receive “a flood of notifications a few hours down the pike” as subsystems come back online.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the total impact of the microsoft outage may never be fully known, but it’s safe to say it’s already significant. Many law enforcement and emergency services ground to a halt. Governments from Japan to the United States reported disruptions to a bevy of functions. Airlines reported problems with their ability to communicate with customers. And hospitals reported widespread interruptions to their operations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ultimately, the episode serves as a reminder of the risks involved when the whole world relies on a single company for a critical service. “We're very interdependent on these systems in modern life,” says Leitschuh. Next time, delayed emails may be the least of our worries.

#712. This tiny iOS 27 camera feature really makes a huge difference

This tiny iOS 27 camera feature really makes a huge difference

When shooting both photos and videos on my iPhone, I make regular use of a few different third-party apps, mostly because I like to take manual control.

Diungkapkan bahwa but a combination of the new pro controls on the iphone 18 pro and a new feature introduced with ios 27 means there are more times when i can stick to apple’s stock camera app. If you aren’t already using customizable controls, I highly recommend doing so ….

Berdasarkan laporan, developers know that a big reason for using third-party camera apps is being able to use them in much the same way you would a standalone camera. A key part of this is having easy access to manual control over things like aperture (on the iPhone 18 Pro), shutter speed, white balance, and choosing between manual and auto focus. Those settings are right there on the main screen of almost all third-party apps.

Diungkapkan bahwa with the iphone 18 pro, the same set of controls are also available in apple’s stock camera app. By default, these are tucked inside a menu, requiring an initial tap to open it. As we noted back in September, however, iOS 27 brings customizable controls to the camera app.

Sebagaimana diketahui, simply open the menu and tap the edit button (top-left when holding the phone vertically) and you can add any of the controls to the main screen. This makes them available in a single tap.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, aperture, shutter speed, and white balance as these are the three main manual controls i use. Exposure compensation, because sometimes the only reason I want to take manual control is to increase or decrease the exposure, and that provides a faster way of doing so (quicker than the alternative drag up/down within the photo, in my experience). Finally, I have one-tap access to the histogram to help in setting exposure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s a similar story in video mode. I again have aperture and white balance along with exposure compensation and the histogram. But here I add instant access to frame-rate and focus modes (as I’m more likely to switch focus mode when shooting video).

Of course, third-party apps still have an important role, but this one change has made a big difference to me when using the stock camera app for both photos and video.

#713. Alexander Rinke says Europe needs AI champions to share in the next wave of AI value

Alexander Rinke says Europe needs AI champions to share in the next wave of AI value

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://thenextweb.com/news/alexander-rinke-celonis-sovereign-ai-tnw-podcast

Berdasarkan laporan, alexander rinke told the tnw podcast that companies and public agencies want to own their ai weights. The Celonis co-founder and co-CEO also set out his test for real product-market fit.

TNW’s Cristian Dina (left) and Celonis co-CEO Alexander Rinke at HumanX in Amsterdam, 23 September 2026.

Sebagaimana diketahui, thirty years ago, europe’s gdp was roughly on par with the us, alexander rinke told tnw. Today it is dramatically less. The Celonis co-founder and co-CEO does not want AI to make that gap wider.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rinke spoke to cristian dina for the tnw podcast at humanx in amsterdam on 23 september. Earlier that day he had joined a panel on stage called “Can Europe Actually Build Sovereign AI?”. Earlier guests include Steve Lucas of Boomi, Arvind Jain of Glean, and Daniel Dines of UiPath. The full conversation is in the video below.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, countries and groups of countries such as europe want control over parts of the ai stack, rinke said. They want to know where their data and their IP go. Europe also needs its own companies to take part in an AI economy that will be huge.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we need to really foster local champions, not because we don’t trust the americans or we think ai is going to kill us all. Just because we want to make sure we take part of the upside. ” Alexander Rinke, Celonis.

Sebagaimana diketahui, celonis is one example, he said. Its headquarters are in New York and Munich, and it has more than 20 offices around the world, with a strong presence in Germany, Spain and the UK. Europe is “not a satellite for us,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for a company or a public agency, sovereign ai means owning its own ai, rinke said. In the end, that means owning the model weights.

Berdasarkan laporan, “they don’t want to give all of their data to any model to train on that data. ” Alexander Rinke, Celonis.

Berdasarkan laporan, every organisation is like a snowflake, he said, so its processes and their context are unique. That needs open platforms that can be installed in sovereign environments. It also helps customers tune open-source models for specific business tasks. Celonis keeps a customer’s process data with the customer and does not send it anywhere. For those tasks, he said, they can get the same or better results than with frontier models.

Berdasarkan laporan, rinke started celonis 15 years ago with his co-founders, martin klenk and bastian nominacher. They first wanted to build models that could simulate how a business works. To feed a simulation, they needed to know how the business ran today, and companies could not tell them.

Diungkapkan bahwa “so we built an x-ray machine that looks at the data the business generates and x-rays how the processes work. ” Alexander Rinke, Celonis.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, celonis now calls this process intelligence. It maps how work really gets done, across systems and outside them, so companies can redesign it with AI. The company has about 3,500 people, he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, celonis recently bought ikigai labs, an mit spin-off. Ikigai builds specialised models for tabular and time-series data and for what-if simulation. A large language model can use them as a tool, Rinke said, for jobs such as forecasting a supply chain or deciding whether to settle an insurance claim.

Berdasarkan laporan, asked about an ipo or new funding, rinke spoke about the next phase of growth instead. He pointed to the Context Model that Celonis launched and to the Ikigai deal. Celonis describes the Context Model as a living model of a business in motion, built from its operational data and connected to its strategy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many startup pitches claim product-market fit that the company does not have, rinke said. His test has four questions. Is the product valuable? Is it uniquely valuable, or easy to replace? Is it repeatable, or custom each time? Will customers keep paying for it?.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it’s easy to say that you have. It’s very easy to put on a slide for VCs. ” Alexander Rinke, Celonis.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if the answer to all four is yes, the next step is what he calls product-market-people fit: the organisation needed to scale it. Scaling too early can grow revenue that does not last, he said, especially in a boom market like AI.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, celonis was his first real venture. The founders started it during their studies, and Rinke put his master’s on hold and never finished it. They bootstrapped for five years, and winning the first enterprise clients without references was very hard, he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, venture capital is a good idea if a company wants to move quickly, rinke said. But it does not replace the work a bootstrapped company has to do.

Diungkapkan bahwa “you shouldn’t build the company to raise capital. You should build the company for customers. ” Alexander Rinke, Celonis.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he now works much more closely with celonis engineers than he did a few years ago. He oversees some technical projects himself and is involved in how the company adopts AI internally. Asked whether he is technical, he said: “Yeah, pretty technical. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, cristian dina is the cro at the next web. He has interviewed 300+ industry leaders and authored the book King of Networking, establishing himself as one of the most connected and respected voices in the ecosystem. He has interviewed 300+ industry leaders and authored the book King of Networking, establishing hi (show all) Cristian Dina is the CRO at The Next Web. At just 23 years old, Cristian was included in the Forbes 30 Under 30 2025 list, representing a new generation of tech builders, bold thinkers who move fast, build with purpose, and create real impact.

The Verge’s 2026 gift guide for dads

Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

This year, why not get Dad a gift or two he won’t expect?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you buy something from a link, the verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you buy something from a link, the verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, gone are the days when you could just buy your father a random tie or some leather-clad alcohol vessel or a shaving kit. Dads want — nay, deserve — something memorable. Luckily for you, it’s not that hard to find something special that he’ll approve of, and we’re here to guide you.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’ve curated this year’s gift list with the modern father in mind, whether he’s a gamer, creator, chef, or simply a gadget lover. There’s a lot in here we think he’ll like, from noise-canceling headphones like the Sonos Ace Ultra and an autonomous drone to a brilliant QD-OLED monitor and a nifty light that’s perfect for illuminating his next campsite. Whatever your dad is into, we’ve got you covered.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, antigravity’s a1 is the ultimate gadget for the dad who dreams of owning the sky. The compact drone comes with specialized goggles that will make him feel like he’s in the cockpit, and it records always-on, 360-degree 8K video. It’s an exhilarating flight experience and an excellent creator’s tool in one slick package.

Diungkapkan bahwa cleaning gadgets like dyson’s pencilvac fluffycones are never cheap, but they’re often worth the cost and a pleasure to use. The lightweight, broom-replacing stick vacuum doesn’t do carpets, but its rolling bars pack incredible cleaning power for touching up hard floors, including stairs.

Berdasarkan laporan, for those who love travel but hate the constraints of a hotel tv, belkin’s connectair is a slick solution. Plug the transmitter into any device with a USB-C video-out port and the receiver into the TV’s HDMI port, and voilà, you’re easily (and wirelessly) connected.

Diungkapkan bahwa sonos raised its headphones game on all fronts with the ace ultra, which deliver better noise canceling, improved sound, and the feature we’ve all been waiting for: wi-fi support. With the ability to bounce audio across your Sonos ecosystem, including from a TV via newer Sonos soundbars, Dad’s sonic sanctuary is finally complete.

Diungkapkan bahwa werewolf’s affordable dongle kit provides an almost magical way to power nearly any dc device from a usb-c charger or portable battery. Program it from a mobile app, connect it to your old gear, and everything from a PC monitor to an original Game Boy can accept USB-C charging.

Who would have thought a simple hook could make roaming the city with a backpack so much more convenient? After testing Peak Design’s well-designed bags, we’re convinced the clever addition is a game-changer for anyone who doesn’t want to leave their bag on the filthy ground.

Diungkapkan bahwa wiim’s first soundbar builds on its seamless sonos-esque connectivity with a sleek design, detailed sound, and up-firing speakers for dolby atmos spatial audio. It also pairs with other speakers for surround sound through a no-fuss setup process, including ones you already own that are linked to one of WiiM’s amplifiers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, your dad needs an awesome monitor, but there are 10 billion options. Alienware’s 34-inch Penta Tandem QD-OLED delivers top-end picture quality, with vibrant colors and perfect blacks, plus a swift 280Hz refresh rate. Best of all, it’s not nearly as expensive as you might think.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if your dad is still reading books on his phone (or aging e-reader), it’s time for an upgrade. The latest in Amazon’s series of waterproof, auto-dimming e-readers loads books faster than the prior model and offers a slick aluminum upgrade. No matter which you choose, it’s a better way to bring the library along.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, give your father a little nostalgia and a lot of convenience in one package with this stylish usb-c dock and ssd combo gadget. The cassette-shaped Sharge Disk Pro 2 works as a hub with support for HDMI at 4K, SD and microSD card slots, USB-A and USB-C ports, along with up to 8TB of storage stored within.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, smart tvs are often pretty dumb. If your dad is always complaining about his TV, or if you want to get ahead of it, grab the latest Apple TV 4K. Although it’s not cheap, it stands out with built-in mics for Siri AI, lots of power, HomePod surround sound support, and a simple, ad-free interface.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the switch 2 leverages the same ideas as its predecessor, only with a larger, 7. 9-inch display, a faster chip, and a bevy of new social features. However, its most important trait is that it’s the newest Nintendo console, which means access to a host of weird, beautiful, family-friendly games that only Nintendo could dream up, now on a better screen.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, oura didn’t reinvent the wheel with the ring 5, but it did reshape it into a slimmer, thinner, more wearable design that could make all the difference. Inside are the same extensive health and fitness tracking features for charting everything from sleep to heart health, backed by long battery life.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the cs-pro will make your dad feel like a private eye in the early ’80s. The retro-inspired digital camera serves up 16-megapixel stills and offers four filters accessible from its tactile dial, plus USB-C charging, a high-quality Xenon flash, and a 4GB SD card for plenty of vintage photo fun.

Diungkapkan bahwa bougerv’s fancy, compact lamp will spark joy for the glamper in your life, as well as everyone else. Its powerful, foldable spread of LEDs provides a blast of light anywhere plug-ins can’t reach, from the beach to the shed where that scary spider holds court, with up to 60 hours of light on low power.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rival pro offers plenty of thoughtful extras, including swappable batteries and an ultra-wideband base station for a seamless, low-latency connection. The gaming mouse’s lightweight design and 8,000Hz polling rate also deliver both accurate and ergonomic performance for up to 16 hours per charge.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s time to help dad ditch his collection of plastic reusable cups, which have clearly seen better days. NotNeutral’s hand-pressed, timeless tumbler offers ’70s vibes with a modern twist, making it the perfect vessel for whatever Dad twists into his favorite drink.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, give the gift that fixes past home improvement transgressions. These handy Japanese-made pliers from Vampire Tools have one fundamental purpose — to remove stripped screws — and they’re damn good at it. The best part? Watching Dad’s face light up seconds before he sprints to the garage for them.

Diungkapkan bahwa for the manga or live-action netflix show lover on your list, this fashionable pirates jersey, inspired by monkey d. Luffy from the seminal pirate adventure series One Piece, will be as surprising as it is delightful.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you’re after a cheap, useful stocking stuffer, trond’s reliable three-prong extension cord is a practical pick that’s available in leftward or rightward configurations to fit nearly any outlet. Dad will probably say, “Oh, I’ve always wanted one of these,” and this time he’ll mean it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, zero company, a strategy game set in the twilight of the clone wars, is a fun way to get lost in the star wars universe. The single-player, turn-based title lets players command a diverse team of characters across a gorgeous expanse of worlds, offering hours of solitary entertainment.

Berdasarkan laporan, if your father already owns an apple watch, the nomad stratos is a foolproof upgrade idea. The refined watch band features titanium links with a rubbery interior for durable comfort, and it comes in an array of subtle color options that make it as suitable for the office as it is for the slopes.

Diungkapkan bahwa we fell for apple’s handy iphone strap due to its effortless accessibility and comfy design, which uses flexible magnets to keep excess segments in check. From biking to hiking to concerts, it’s a great way to sling your iPhone 18 Pro, assuming you have a compatible phone case.

Berdasarkan laporan, the new fitbit air provides the same great fitness tracking we’ve come to expect in a comfortable design that virtually disappears on your wrist. Google’s AI Coach can be overly assertive, but the tracker’s great battery life and metrics for everything from sleep to blood oxygen make it an excellent gift for anyone who needs a healthy hand.

Most of us have thousands of photos in the cloud, but if a photo never makes it into the real world, did it really happen? Existentialism aside, the Cricut StickerPix offers a new way to play with photos, providing you with everything you need to turn any picture into a pro-quality print or sticker.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this battery-powered fan is a big upgrade over your average plug-in job. As a 3D circulator, it can tilt to push air in all directions. It can be controlled from an app and even detaches from its stand to sit on a desk or tabletop. Quiet, powerful, and versatile, it’s equipped for nearly any adventure on or off the grid.

Berdasarkan laporan, have you broken something fragile that seems impossible to mend? maybe all you need is a kintsugi repair kit, which provides the japanese method and a special lacquer to repair and restore broken ceramics to good health. The resulting golden scar is merely to remind us that rebuilding is possible.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if your favorite cinephile is looking to get off the streaming carousel, the kaleidescape strato e is the key. The premium player lets library builders locally store and play their favorite films and TV shows in lossless 4K resolution with Dolby Atmos for sterling entertainment that’s all theirs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, once the great british baking show becomes an obsession, only a serious stand mixer will do for replicating recipes at home. This mixer’s timeless design adds new features in what KitchenAid calls its biggest upgrade since 1955, with a new half-speed setting and a control lever that lets you set speeds between its standard settings.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the pocket scion is unlike any musical instrument you’ve witnessed before, one that uses the “biofeedback” from plants to trigger built-in synths. The device offers MIDI-out to send digital signals to outboard synths, and it includes an app for both macOS and Windows, finally giving you a way to make your favorite fern a rockstar.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when it comes to jotting down notes, there’s nothing like a pen and paper. At least, that’s what we thought before we tried the Remarkable Paper Pure. Offering a strikingly realistic writing experience that saves everything in the digital realm, this tablet is a brilliant way to bridge the gap and save paper.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, electronics are becoming more sustainable, and fairphone is leading the way. The Fairphone 6 Plus may seem like a regular Android phone on paper, but the ability to repair and replace its internals, from the screen to the battery, makes it anything but average.

#715. Microsoft outage: Does Microsoft owe you money? What to know.

📅 13 Nov 2026

Microsoft outage: Does Microsoft owe you money? What to know.

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/tech/microsoft-outage-owe-credit-money-bill

Microsoft's massive, productivity-destroying software outage appears to be receding as of Friday morning, but that's only the start of the process for businesses looking to get some of their Office 365 money back.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, several important enterprise software products, such as outlook and teams, were functionally offline for many users on thursday and into friday. Since Office 365 is a service businesses have to pay for, it raises the question: Can those businesses receive some form of compensation from Microsoft for the time lost?.

Berdasarkan laporan, the answer to that question is nuanced. Let's get into it.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to helpful resources like these explainers from quartz and office watch, the short answer is no; microsoft does not owe anyone money as a result of this outage. But that doesn't mean the company doesn't owe any compensation, as it offers credits (essentially a reduction on the next bill) in the event of an outage.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one important thing to note: you have to request a credit. Microsoft doesn't offer them automatically.

Diungkapkan bahwa purchasing microsoft's software suite involves a service-level agreement (sla). This SLA includes provisions related to outages and compensation. If any of those services fall below the 99. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. 9 percent uptime each month for each piece of software in the suite, such as OneDrive and Outlook. In this case, Microsoft's SLA promises 99. 9 percent threshold, it's possible to claim a credit. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Berdasarkan laporan, "possible" is the key word here, though, as both quartz and office watch make it very clear that microsoft is extremely strict about how it calculates downtime in these instances. The actual math is too complicated to fully get into here, but Microsoft counts downtime in terms of "user minutes," or the amount of time the services were down multiplied by the number of users demonstrably affected.

Sebagaimana diketahui, credits are also prorated depending on how much uptime was lost, so a small amount of downtime might only be worth a 25 or 50 percent credit. Where this gets even more complicated is that Microsoft calculates credits according to each individual service, not the entire software bundle. If you only lost service time in Outlook, but other parts of the Office 365 suite worked, you'd only get a small credit for Outlook.

All of this is to say that, depending on the size of the affected business and the amount of downtime it experienced, one of these credits could be worth only a few measly dollars.

Berdasarkan laporan, to be very clear, individual workers who lost service time due to the big outage cannot file a claim or receive compensation. Businesses who license this software from Microsoft can do it, but even that is more complicated than you'd think.

Diungkapkan bahwa businesses only have until the end of december to file these claims, for starters. If a business purchased Microsoft software directly from Microsoft, it can go to the Office admin center to file a claim. They will need to provide a lot of information, such as incident IDs and specific descriptions of how long service was unavailable to users. From there, Microsoft will perform its own calculations to determine whether the business receives a credit.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many businesses do not purchase these microsoft products directly from the company, instead obtaining them through cloud solution provider (csp) partners or other indirect resellers. In that case, the business will have to bug the provider to submit a claim on their behalf. Depending on the provider, that may or may not happen in a timely or productive manner.

Given the number of hoops that businesses have to jump through to get one of these credits, one could argue it's not worth the hassle, depending on the size of a business and how much time it lost.

#716. Apple Maps in iOS 27 has hidden new feature I’ve been loving

📅 13 Nov 2026

Apple Maps in iOS 27 has hidden new feature I’ve been loving

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/apple-maps-in-ios-27-has-hidden-new-feature-ive-been-loving/

iOS 27 gave Apple Maps a handful of new features, and my favorite is one that keeps offering fresh updates every week: Local Lists.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, apple maps has long offered a ‘guides’ feature where you can browse curated collections of places worth checking out. Sometimes they’re created by Apple’s editorial team, other times by celebrities or in conjunction with current events.

But in iOS 27, there’s a new feature—Local Lists—that’s sort of an extension of Guides, but it gets updated weekly with the latest trending places.

Here’s how Apple describes it, via Apple Newsroom:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with local lists, apple maps users in the u. can find the perfect spot for meeting friends, dining, and more. Using intelligent insights from what’s trending, Maps surfaces locally relevant collections of places — from trending restaurants to great spots to take kids — so it’s easy for users to find what they are looking for. S. All insights are derived with privacy in mind and never tied to individual users.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’ve always enjoyed browsing guides in maps to help find new places. But Local Lists are a great expansion of the idea, especially since they’re updated all the time. I’m always up for trying a new trending restaurant, and now Maps makes it easy to stay on top of what’s new.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even if you’ve been using ios 27 for months, there’s a good chance you’ve never seen local lists. That’s because they’re pretty hidden.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to find the feature, tap into the search field in maps and scroll down to see a new ‘trending restaurants’ section. On my iPhone 18 Pro, by default this section gets hidden behind the keyboard, so you have to first scroll and dismiss the keyboard to see it.

Diungkapkan bahwa trending restaurants are ranked from 1-20. The search screen shows only a handful, but you can tap to view the full list. For example, if you open the ‘Trending Restaurants in New York’ list, you’ll see 20 places worth checking out.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, how does a restaurant make the list? per the in-app explanation, the list contains “restaurants climbing in popularity this week, based on what people view, share, and interact with on apple maps. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa since these trending restaurants lists update weekly, apple says you’ll want to save any places you plan to visit. There’s a convenient + button next to each listing.

Diungkapkan bahwa it’s unclear exactly how many different parts of the us have localized lists in ios 27. But if you poke around and find the full collection of Local Lists, there are 1,021 total—so you’ll probably have one in your area.

You can browse all available lists by opening a Trending Restaurants list then tapping where you see the Apple logo and ‘Local Lists’ near the text that says when it was last updated.

Have you used Local Lists in iOS 27’s Maps app yet? Let us know what you think via the comments.

#718. Cornelis launches CN6000 800G networking to rival Nvidia InfiniBand

📅 13 Nov 2026

Cornelis launches CN6000 800G networking to rival Nvidia InfiniBand

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://thenextweb.com/news/cornelis-cn6000-800g-networking-ai-supercomputers

Its new 800G network cards aim to stop costly AI chips from sitting idle while they wait for data.

Cornelis’s CN6000 network card and switch, which partner systems will use from early 2027.

Berdasarkan laporan, cornelis, which intel spun out in 2020, has launched cn6000, a family of 800g network cards and switches for ai and supercomputers. It claims lower latency than Nvidia’s InfiniBand, based on its own tests. Partner systems arrive in early 2027.

Diungkapkan bahwa cornelis, a networking company spun out of intel, has launched cn6000, a family of 800g network cards and switches for ai clusters and supercomputers, it announced this week. It is pitching them as a rival to Nvidia’s InfiniBand.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in large ai systems, thousands of chips must constantly swap data. If the network is slow, expensive chips sit idle. “Every minute an accelerator waits on the network is capacity our customers paid for and didn’t use,” said CEO Lisa Spelman.

Berdasarkan laporan, the main card uses omni-path, a networking technology intel dropped in 2019 before spinning the business off as cornelis in 2020. Cornelis says the card can handle 1. 6 billion messages a second. It also says it is 21% faster than Nvidia’s InfiniBand at passing a small message, though that comes from its own tests.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a faster single message does not mean jobs finish 21% sooner, since that depends on the workload. Cornelis also launched a card for standard Ethernet networks, which most AI data centres use, with support for the newer Ultra Ethernet standard due later.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the cards work with chips from amd, intel, nvidia and qualcomm. Dell, Lenovo and Supermicro are among the server makers planning to support them, with systems due in early 2027.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, networking has become a hot spot in ai. Nvidia has spent billions on optical links, Huawei is betting on wiring over chips, and startups such as Upscale AI are building ways to connect rival chips. AMD, a Cornelis partner, is also building rack-scale systems to compete with Nvidia.

#721. The Microsoft Outage Is a Warning for the World

📅 13 Nov 2026

The Microsoft Outage Is a Warning for the World

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/the-microsoft-outage-is-a-warning-for-the-world/

Sebagaimana diketahui, a dramatic microsoft 365 outage impacting widely used services like outlook, teams, and copilot dragged into a second day on friday after the company failed overnight to resolve an issue that left institutions and individuals around the world without crucial communication tools. The services did seem to be on a slow path to recovery by midmorning on Friday.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we’re observing sustained improvements in service availability,” microsoft said in a statement posted to its status dashboard on friday morning. The company had said on Thursday evening that its initial attempts to fix the problem were “not taking as expected. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the outages have caused widespread disruption to schools, courts, governments, and law enforcement agencies—plus countless businesses and millions of employees—around the globe, highlighting how many of the world’s most crucial systems rely upon technologies from a small number of tech companies. And when they fail, the ramifications can be huge.

Microsoft has not said yet what caused the outage but has hinted that it was related to cascading server failures inside multiple data centers around the world that shifted too much load onto remaining operational machines.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we determined the elevated load isn't driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure,” the company wrote in microsoft 365 status update on thursday afternoon. “We’re testing a configuration change to address a problem that's causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable,” the company added a few minutes later.

Diungkapkan bahwa an additional update a few minutes after that noted, “we've not identified any recent change correlated with the start of impact; however, our investigation indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component that's responsible for processing server health. ”.

Microsoft emphasized repeatedly in statements that there was no indication of the outage being caused by a cyberattack.

Berdasarkan laporan, “this is absolutely going to go down as one of the big ones, up there with the facebook outage of october 2021,” says doug madory, director of internet analysis at monitoring firm kentik. “We don't know the root cause yet, but it is interesting to break down the traffic by source data center. The recovery came in fits and starts and varied greatly by source, probably due to Microsoft's efforts to bring the service back online. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa a prolonged outage of such a critical underlying digital service is not unprecedented, but microsoft has a special position among cloud providers as an older company that was already ubiquitous in global computing from the pc era. Many organizations integrate Microsoft productivity services at the core of their operations, simply because they have used Windows computers for decades and have longstanding relationships with Microsoft.

Berdasarkan laporan, “what makes this particularly significant is the criticality of the services affected, especially email and communication systems relied upon by government and other essential organisations,” says swapneel patnekar, the ceo of indian web security firm shreshta it technologies. “The impact goes well beyond the inconvenience of a typical service disruption. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, many observers pointed out on thursday and friday that microsoft has recently shed staff through attrition, layoffs, and buyout offers. The company’s annual filings say it had 223,000 full-time employees on June 30, down from 228,000 at the same time in 2025. Then in July, the company eliminated 9,000 jobs globally, of which 3,200 were cuts related to an overhaul of its Xbox teams. In October, the company reportedly made buyout offers to 60,000 employees, though apparently this was intended to speed attrition, not cull all of those roles.

Sebagaimana diketahui, then there’s the ai factor. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said in April that as much as 30 percent of the code the company is generating is now written using AI in automated tools.

Berdasarkan laporan, “satya's recent comments have a much different look today than they did even a week ago,” says jake williams, a faculty member at ians, an intelligence and security consultancy. “I don't think we'll ever be able to say that the staff reductions caused this outage, but you'll never convince me that all the tribal knowledge that walked out the door wouldn't have been invaluable in resolving it. ”.

Microsoft did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Reports of widespread disruption from the Microsoft outage started appearing during the working day on Friday in countries in Asia and Australasia, spreading across the world as more people logged on.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, schools, retail stores, courts, and medical organizations across australia said everything from exams to health care appointments were disrupted. “Medical scans have been cancelled due to both myself and the clinic not being able to access referrals via email or fax,” one person told Australian media. Officials in Japan’s government said its own platforms had been disrupted, and staff were using phones and chat tools as they couldn’t access Outlook.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the uk, multiple police forces have said they are unable to accept online crime reports due to the outages of microsoft services, though phone lines for emergency and nonemergency reports remained available. Parts of the National Health Service, including doctor surgeries and hospital services, also reported that some services were impacted by the outages. “Those who work in 111 and 999 services are unable to refer patients in the normal way—creating a massive backlog,” the GMB trade union posted on X, referring to nonemergency and emergency health services.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile, deutsche bahn, the provider of train services across germany, updated its alerts page saying the email outages “severely restricts the sending of timetables. ” Courts, local government agencies, and media organizations in the Netherlands reported issues with their communications services, according to local press. In France, some health agencies and local governments also reported similar issues. One winemaker in South Africa told the BBC his company had been brought to a standstill by the outages.

Sebagaimana diketahui, unsurprisingly, these disruptions continued to be echoed across canada and the us as millions of people have attempted to sign on. Canadian rail service Via Rail posted online that customers may not receive details of their booked trips via email, with with York’s Department of Investigation posting on X that housing evictions planned for Friday had been canceled and Arapahoe County Sheriff’s Office, in Colorado, also posting on X that a lack of email notifications means bond payments being made online were not being processed.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it's literally named 365. That implies a specific duty,” says longtime security and compliance consultant Davi Ottenheimer. “Can’t sell an empty bottle called ‘Bottle of Water. ’”.

Berdasarkan laporan, during the outage, multiple officials around the world called for countries to rely less on giant tech firms or reevaluate their relationships. “The global Microsoft outage only serves to highlight once again the lack of resilience in the UK’s digital infrastructure, and the dangers that this dependency can pose to our security, economy and public services,” Chi Onwurah, the chair of the UK parliament’s Science and Technology Committee, said in a statement.

Berdasarkan laporan, since the start of the second trump administration—with its chaos, unpredictability, and threats changing the nature of international relationships—countries across europe and other parts of the world have been starting to change their attitudes and reliance on some us-based big technology firms, such as google, microsoft, and amazon web services. Officials in France have been developing local, open source alternatives to Zoom, Teams, and other productivity software, while WIRED has documented dozens of other European efforts to ditch US big tech services.

Sebagaimana diketahui, patnekar, from indian security firm shreshta, says that while much tech infrastructure has been provided by centralized services in recent years, email seems particularly challenging to create resiliency. “Ultimately, the lesson isn't necessarily that organisations should stop relying on large technology providers,” Patnekar says. “Rather, they need to identify which services are genuinely mission-critical and ensure they have an independent fallback when those providers become unavailable. ”.

#729. OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, enabling ‘dot’ agents to make purchases

OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet, enabling ‘dot’ agents to make purchases

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/openai-launches-chatgpt-wallet-enabling-dot-agents-to-make-purchases/

Diungkapkan bahwa openai is launching chatgpt wallet, which it says is “setting a new bar for secure payments by agents. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, chatgpt wallet works with openai’s “dots” agent feature and includes a partnership with american express, mastercard, and visa. Here’s how it works.

Diungkapkan bahwa openai says chatgpt wallet is the “first wallet that lets agents pay without access to users’ actual card details and that requires a security check for every purchase, while also preserving existing card rewards and protections for eligible disputes. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we’re starting with limited availability to chatgpt pro users,” openai explains, “so we can learn from real-world use and work with businesses, banks, and payment networks to improve compatibility and reliability. ”.

The feature won’t work with websites that block agents, however, which has increasingly become an issue online.

Sebagaimana diketahui, before each purchase, the user reviews the items, total, and selected card, then approves it with a security check such as face id or a fingerprint scan. Each approval creates a clear record of the purchase the user authorized the agent to make.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after the user approves, the payment network provides a payment token—a substitute for the user’s actual card details—with a card number, security code, and expiration date. The payment is charged to their selected card without ChatGPT Wallet sharing their actual card details with the business or agent.

You can read more about ChatGPT Wallet and how it works here.

The company emphasizes that payments are secure, card info isn’t shared with your dot or merchants, and that you’re in control of purchases.

#731. Jensen Huang and the End of the Founder Fairy Tale

📅 13 Nov 2026

Jensen Huang and the End of the Founder Fairy Tale

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.wired.com/story/jensen-huang-and-the-end-of-the-founder-fairy-tale/

It was July of 2024, and Jensen Huang was punchy.

Berdasarkan laporan, i had agreed to travel to denver, colorado, to interview the nvidia ceo at siggraph, the annual confab of computer graphics phds and practitioners. Early that year I’d conducted a lengthy sit-down interview with Huang for a WIRED magazine feature, which apparently went well enough—both for WIRED and for Nvidia’s executive communications team—that I had been asked to interview Huang again at this conference. Another opportunity to grill the CEO of the modern world’s most consequential company? Yes, of course. I began preparing.

Diungkapkan bahwa what ensued was, in a word, bizarre. She was clearly intelligent, commanding respect. During the first prep call for the conference, the type of call-in which PR handlers typically try to coax specific questions out of journalists to prevent an ambush, a youngish, vaguely familiar woman took the lead. This was Madison Huang, Jensen’s daughter. She told me about the slides Jensen would be presenting on stage at SIGGRAPH and offered suggestions for key moments when I might tee him up to talk about the slides.

Slides? Tee up Jensen? What kind of “interview” was this?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i raised my concerns with both my editors and nvidia. Huang was domineering, evaded some of my questions, and, immediately after our session concluded, did an impromptu Q&A session with a much more adoring crowd than me. ) To this day, former and current Nvidia workers sometimes tell me that I “handled” the whole thing well. Let’s just say the interview didn’t go smoothly. We agreed that I would ask the questions I intended to ask him, which included questions about the environmental impact of data centers, and that Huang would also be referring to slides. (It’s on YouTube. Then I was guided offstage, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg hopped on, where he and Huang had a lovey-dovey fireside chat.

Diungkapkan bahwa as a longtime journalist i’m used to occasional adversarial interactions; i really don’t lose sleep over them. Not just wanted to; he assumed he would. Huang later agreed to meet with me again, in December 2024. This was just a CEO being a CEO. But that interview in Denver had underscored for me how much Jensen Huang wanted to control the narrative. And to a large extent he did. Until this week.

Berdasarkan laporan, narrative has always been a critical part of huang’s success. By Huang’s own telling, he was an immigrant founder, an underdog, a wife guy who chased (and eventually married) his college sweetheart, a scrappy startup guy who dined at Denny’s in the early days. A visionary who worked Sundays and who didn’t sleep well because he always heard the hoof steps of competitors. He was not just your average electrical engineering nerd who toiled away on something that would eventually find a product-market fit. A parent who brought his kids into the corporate fold. A man who loved Nvidia so much he tattooed an abstract version of the company logo on his arm.

Sebagaimana diketahui, huang built the highest-valued publicly traded company in history. It’s true. That part’s not just fairy tale. Now, it’s starting to read more like a Greek tragedy.

Diungkapkan bahwa back in january 2024, when i sat down with him for our first-ever in-person meeting, huang right off the bat talked about the importance of storytelling. Here’s an excerpt:.

Berdasarkan laporan, jensen huang: somebody who i really admire, as a leader and a person, is shantanu narayen, the ceo of adobe. He said he always wanted to be a journalist because he loved telling stories.

WIRED: It seems like an important part of building a business, being able to tell its story effectively.

Diungkapkan bahwa yes. Strategy setting is storytelling. Culture building is storytelling.

You’ve said many times you didn’t sell the idea of Nvidia based on a pitch deck.

Diungkapkan bahwa that’s right. It was really about telling the story.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, even then, huang was caught up in the crosshairs of the us–china ai war and at the mercy of regulators, as i wrote at the time. After Donald Trump’s reelection that year, Huang once again deployed his storytelling skills and lobbied the Trump administration to loosen export controls, so he could sell some of his company’s chips to China.

Berdasarkan laporan, another crucial part of the huang lore is that he ran a “flat” organization, with a few dozen top executives reporting to him. ) Huang once said the structure allowed Nvidia “to adapt a lot more quickly, which we need because our technology is moving so quickly. (This is sometimes reported as being “60” people; insiders have told me at times it’s closer to 35. ” Huang was also known to be controlling of all aspects of the business—participating in every significant meeting, seemingly aware of every moving part, and staying in the loop on sourcing, supply chains, and the company’s allocation of chips.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is where huang’s cult of leadership, and his nvidia storytelling, may have come to a stupidly disappointing final chapter. As one former employee put it, Huang can’t simultaneously have had knowledge of every element of Nvidia’s business and then potentially feign ignorance about where the chips may have fallen, both figuratively and literally. His apparent lapses in judgment have now led him to resign from the very company he coaxed into existence and have shattered the mythos of its ever-prescient founder.

It’s certainly not the narrative ending Huang would have chosen, were he still in control.

#732. Security Bite: Apple details Secure Exclaves, a glimpse at its ambient computing future

📅 13 Nov 2026

Security Bite: Apple details Secure Exclaves, a glimpse at its ambient computing future

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/13/security-bite-apple-details-secure-exclaves-a-glimpse-at-its-ambient-computing-future/

Sebagaimana diketahui, 9to5mac security bite is exclusively brought to you by mosyle, the only apple unified platform. Making Apple devices work-ready and enterprise-safe is all we do. The result is a totally automated Apple Unified Platform currently trusted by over 45,000 organizations to make millions of Apple devices work-ready with no effort and at an affordable cost. Our unique integrated approach to management and security combines state-of-the-art Apple-specific security solutions for fully automated Hardening & Compliance, Next Generation EDR, AI-powered Zero Trust, and exclusive Privilege Management with the most powerful and modern Apple MDM on the market. Request your EXTENDED TRIAL today and understand why Mosyle is everything you need to work with Apple.

Berdasarkan laporan, apple published a new security research post this week detailing secure exclaves, a new architecture built to handle what the company calls “ambient sensing. ” The latter isn’t anything new. “Hey, Siri” has been using a version of this always-on listening technology for years. The difference now (particularly on newer devices like Apple Watch Series 12 and HomeView) is new features need far more data from your surroundings, and Apple has changed where that data gets processed.

Diungkapkan bahwa today, on most apple hardware, wake-word detections run locally on-device on a smaller, low-power chip. But once it thinks it heard you say “Hey, Siri,” the main operating system gets involved to confirm and wake up the smart assistant for use. There’s nothing necessarily wrong with this process. The split second of audio is all processed locally and not sent to Apple servers.

The problem lies in Apple’s newer features that ask for a lot more from users than a wake word.

Sebagaimana diketahui, person recognition on homeview identifies who’s in the room by face and voice, and siri recap and live rewind need to keep a running sense of what’s been happening around you. That adds up to a constant stream of sensitive camera and mic data, and it needs a more secure way of being processed than anything Apple had before.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, much like the existing secure enclaves architecture for authentication, instead of passing operations to the main os, secure exclaves (notice the x) run their own tiny, separate operating system. According to Apple, that data “cannot be accessed by the main operating system, apps, or Apple. Raw data goes in and a simple “that’s Arin” or “that’s the wake word” is outputted back to the OS, everything else is thrown away. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the changes don’t stop there. In recent SB column, I mentioned how on iPhone, the green dot that appears indicating that the camera or mic is live is all software connected, not like the hardwired LED that exists on the Mac. Now on iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone Duo, and MacBook Neo, the camera and mic indicators now live inside this new exclave, meaning even a compromised OS shouldn’t be able to hide them for malicious purposes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s apparent apple is building toward this new level of ambient computing across every type of device when you read technical reports like this. Future AI-first products, like the heavily rumored AirPods Pro with inferred cameras, will most certainly built on this new Secure Exclave architecture.

Diungkapkan bahwa overall, this new technical post reads like apple laying the privacy groundwork for the always-listening, always-watching products that are here and coming in the near future. It’s the privacy-first approach we’ve come to love from Apple and further demonstrates its lead on this front. I highly recommend checking it out.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we’re halfway through november now, and i know i need some good movies to help distract me from the biting cold. Luckily, Prime Video has stocked up its increasingly compulsive library in impressive style this month. To stop you from scrolling for ages until you land on a film you fancy, I’ve handpicked three flicks I think you’ll have a grand old time with this weekend on one of the best streaming services.

Sebagaimana diketahui, first, a classic drama deservedly picked up a couple of oscars back in 1998, and for me it features the late, great robin williams' second best role (after "aladdin's" genie, naturally). Then there's a thoroughly stupid but lovable comedy that showed the world Arnie could do lolz. Finally, I’ve chosen a sci-fi thriller that gave Matthew Broderick one of his first starring roles.

So wrap up warm, break out some junk food and read on for three movies you should definitely stream on Prime Video this weekend.

Berdasarkan laporan, “how do you like them apples?” i like them mighty fine, mr. Hunting. The movie that finally won Robin Williams a richly deserved Oscar for Best Supporting Actor, “Good Will Hunting” was a passion project both Matt Damon and Ben Affleck had been working on for years before they got a Hollywood studio to bite. Damon plays the titular Will Hunting; a tough Southie kid from Boston who just so happens to be a secret mathematical genius.

Berdasarkan laporan, his absurdly high iq is discovered by professor geral lambeau (stellan skarsgård) who catches will solving an insanely challenging math problem on a chalkboard as hunting is half-assing a shift as a janitor at mit. Lambeau promptly takes Will under his wing, but it’s clear that this genius needs help. Abused from an early age and carrying a lot of rage, it’s Williams’ Dr Sean Maguire who helps Hunting find some peace.

Diungkapkan bahwa there’s also an utterly charming romance between will and fellow student skylar (a lovely minnie driver) that drives much of the movie. The only thing that ticks me off about this classic is that we never got “Good Will Hunting 2: Hunting Season” that “Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back” promised me in 2001.

Watch "Good Will Hunting" on Prime Video now.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the first movie to really show off arnie’s comedic chops. The premise of “Twins” is pretty ingenious. Although if you can’t have a giggle during “Predator’s” “stick around line” the year before this delightful comedy came out, I feel sorry for you. Thanks to a secret genetic experiment, hulking Julius Benedict (Schwarzenegger) and impish Vincent Benedict (Danny DeVito) are fraternal twins who are separated at birth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, years later, arnie’s hyper-smart, kind-hearted giant (he was raised by a professor on an isolated island) eventually tracks down devito, who has slipped into a life of crime and become a semi-sleazy crook. Once Vinnie finds himself pursued by mobsters after accidentally pilfering the prototype of a super-secret jet engine (no, really), the pair embark on a cross-country road trip that eventually reunites them with their mother, who thought they had both died at birth. “Twins” is a big-hearted ‘80s classic… though I do partially blame its existence on helping to birth 1994’s awful “Junior”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “shall we play a game?” sure, why not? oh, i’ve accidentally started the beginnings of a global thermonuclear war because i’m a high school hacker who thought it was clever to mess around with a military supercomputer. Oops. That sounds like a slightly mean synopsis of “WarGames” — a movie that I actually really like — but there’s no denying the basic plot is highly silly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, still, matthew broderick shines in one of his first big breaks. Long before he was Ferris Bueller and legendarily bunked off for the day and a decade prior to him becoming King of Pride Rock, here he plays hacker and video game enthusiast David Lightman. David basically thinks he’s playing Battleship, while over at the Pentagon, they’re in full-on DEFCON 5 mode as military brass try to stave off World War III with the Russians. Messing with an ultra-brainy computer, then accidentally entering its WOPR (War Operation Plan Response) quickly causes a national crisis. It’s silly, it’s sweet, and I wholeheartedly recommend streaming “WarGames” this weekend.

Away from tech, most of Dave’s time is taken up by walking his husky, buying new TVs at an embarrassing rate and obsessing over his beloved Arsenal.

Diungkapkan bahwa say your team is planning a customer event, and claude is on the call. You say, “Claude, start a doc for this plan. ” Claude writes up what the team has said so far, and teammates on the invite can edit the plan while you keep talking.
