When you start discussing timelines, someone asks Claude to put it on a whiteboard, and the team works on the schedule alongside the doc.

Diungkapkan bahwa claude adds a separate page for each meeting in claude. ai (opens in new tab) with the notes, transcript, and anything it built. People from your organization on the invite can see it and edit what Claude made, and it can be shared with others in your organization from the page.

Sebagaimana diketahui, by default, claude is set to stay out of calls when someone from outside your organization is invited, and to leave if someone from outside joins partway through. Diungkapkan bahwa claude uses each person’s connected tools with that person’s permission. It asks the first time, and a yes applies going forward. For now, when someone asks out loud, Claude asks each time to confirm who’s speaking. An answer posted in the call’s chat is visible to everyone on the call.

Berdasarkan laporan, when claude joins, it appears as a participant and posts a notice in the call’s chat. It saves a transcript, summary, and screen descriptions, not audio.

Before you add Claude or turn on auto-join, make sure everyone on your calls is OK with being transcribed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, claude joins when someone adds it or has auto-join on. On Enterprise plans, an admin turns it on for all or part of the organization. Support is currently available for Google Meet, with other platforms coming soon. On Team plans, inviting Claude to your meetings is available by default, and an admin can turn it off. While it’s in beta, it isn’t available to some organizations, including those with zero data retention (ZDR), HIPAA-ready configuration, or customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, during the beta, claude’s notes and transcripts are free on team and enterprise plans. #737. I Analyzed the Seven Biggest AI Chatbots to Determine How Safe They Are for Kids

📅 13 Nov 2026

I Analyzed the Seven Biggest AI Chatbots to Determine How Safe They Are for Kids

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/how-safe-are-chatbots-for-kids?utm_medium=RSS

Diungkapkan bahwa david nield is a technology journalist from manchester in the u. K. who has been writing about gadgets and apps for more than 20 years.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he has a bachelor's degree in english literature from durham university, where he also spent a term as editor of the award-winning student newspaper palatinate. More recently, he has worked as a freelancer for some of the biggest technology publications on the web, covering everything from on-the-ground reporting about product launches, to detailed explainers and how-to guides on apps, gadgets, and platforms. K. His journalism career started in print media, where he contributed to and edited several technology magazines and bookazines sold in the U. and internationally. His expertise covers broad areas of consumer tech, including smartphones, laptops, wearables, and AI.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ai safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications. At the same time, an increasing number of apps and services are becoming age-gated in a growing number of countries around the world, as governments realize that letting kids loose on AI apps, social media platforms, and the web at large might not be the best idea for their ongoing development and prosperity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the big ai apps, such as chatgpt and gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe. If you want to know what youngsters in your family may be getting exposed to, and what you can do about it, here's the rundown.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these chatgpt for teens accounts can also be linked to a parental account—but while parental consent is required for under-18s to use the service, chatgpt clearly says that teens do have the option to break the link if they want. Berdasarkan laporan, gemini is tied into everything else google does, and follows the broader rules for google accounts: no under-13s, unless you're part of a family group and using an account managed by an adult. Sebagaimana diketahui, for all under-18s (partly identified through age estimation), whether or not they're part of a managed family group, google applies some additional protections. They include preventing the AI from taking on a persona, guarding against emotional dependence on the AI, and discouraging bullying and other forms of harassment. Diungkapkan bahwa these protections for minors are applied in addition to the usual guardrails in gemini for everyone. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as with chatgpt, there's a loophole of sorts in that anyone can start chatting with gemini, for free inside a web browser, with no checks at all. These conversations can't be saved and come up against usage limits fairly quickly, but they're only protected by the general restrictions for all accounts, not the ones specific to minors.

Sebagaimana diketahui, meta ai will show up in several apps that young people and children are likely to use, including whatsapp and instagram, as well as having its own separate app on the web and on phones. #747. OpenAI’s ChatGPT Wallet lets its AI agents shop without seeing your card

📅 13 Nov 2026

OpenAI’s ChatGPT Wallet lets its AI agents shop without seeing your card

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://thenextweb.com/news/chatgpt-wallet-openai-dots-agents-payments

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a chatgpt wallet purchase awaiting approval, from openai’s launch video. Screenshot: OpenAI.

Berdasarkan laporan, openai has launched chatgpt wallet, which lets its dots ai agents buy things for users without seeing their card details. The company built it with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, it said in its announcement on Friday.

Diungkapkan bahwa users add a card once. Before each purchase, they review the items, the total and the card. They then approve it with a check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. Each approval creates a record of what the user allowed the agent to buy.

Diungkapkan bahwa after approval, the payment network issues a payment token. It stands in for the real card, with its own card number, security code and expiry date. The business and the agent never see the actual card details, OpenAI said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, users keep their card’s rewards and its protections for eligible disputes, such as a defective item. Businesses keep control of pricing, delivery, returns and customer service.

“Our goal here is to really focus on merchants and our network partners and start building out a really great foundation that’s safe and easy to use,” Chaya Nayak, who leads product for monetization and payments at OpenAI, told CNBC’s Ashley Capoot.

Berdasarkan laporan, openai is not taking a cut of purchases for now, cnbc reported. Over time, OpenAI expects users to hand purchases to their agent entirely. They would set limits on spending, categories or time periods.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, openai said some websites may block purchases by agents without meaning to. Risk systems can also flag legitimate agent purchases as fraud, which leads to declines or cancellations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to help, it published a playbook for businesses. OpenAI is also working with fraud firms Forter, Riskified, Sardine and Signifyd, and with payment providers Adyen, Checkout. It covers letting ChatGPT agents through firewalls, uploading product feeds and setting up business profiles in ChatGPT. com and Stripe.

Diungkapkan bahwa united airlines said on wednesday it will block agents from booking tickets. Amazon stops them buying on its platform, CNBC reported. Schwab and JPMorgan are blocking AI agents from moving customer money.

Sebagaimana diketahui, openai tried checkout in chatgpt before. It launched an Instant Checkout feature in autumn 2025 and quickly moved away from it, CNBC reported. They failed 42. Visa tested 22 models as shoppers this month. 8% of the time.

Luke Gebb, who heads global innovation at American Express, said the small launch is deliberate.

“It just makes sense to watch it, start it in a contained environment, and then keep rolling from there,” Gebb told CNBC.

Walmart lets agents shop through agent profiles with their own spending limits.

#748. 10 Hacks Every watchOS 27 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026

10 Hacks Every watchOS 27 User Should Know

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/hacks-every-watchos-27-user-should-know?utm_medium=RSS

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, khamosh pathak is a freelance tech journalist with over 13 years of experience writing online. An accounting graduate, he turned his interest in writing and technology into a career. He holds a specialization in user experience design from ISDI Parsons in Mumbai, where he sought to deepen his understanding of UX, consumer devices, and interplay between software and technology.

Diungkapkan bahwa khamosh has written thousands of how-tos and guides on every major platform (ios, macos, android, and windows). He got started writing how-tos and guides for Guiding Tech, where he also published several e-books. His work has also been seen at MakeUseOf, How-To Geek, and PCMag. He is truly passionate about brewing good coffee.

Diungkapkan bahwa watchos 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your apple watch supports it. That's especially true for anyone with the latest Series 12 or Ultra 4. While the newest update isn't Apple's most feature-filled, it does include a number of changes that improve the way you exercise, track your health, and locate missing items. If your Apple Watch supports watchOS 27, you should know about these 10 hacks:.

Berdasarkan laporan, with watchos 27, apple changed what double-pressing the digital crown does. Instead of opening the app switcher, it now triggers Audio Intelligence—if you have an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. If you don't have access to those features, the gesture now does nothing.

Diungkapkan bahwa it seems apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchos 27. When you're using an app while running this latest update, press and hold the bottom part of the watch's screen, and you'll trigger the app switcher. 2. You can now jump to a different app, or close an app that isn't working. Sadly, this only works when you're already in an app, and not when you're on the Home Screen, but it's certainly better than nothing.

Berdasarkan laporan, while you can load up multiple complications on your apple watch, they aren't exactly dynamic. That's why I'm a big fan of the Smart Stack widgets on the Apple Watch, which update dynamically to show contextual information. Now, with the new Siri Modular Face, you can access dynamic widgets on the Home Screen. If you've just parked your car, for example, you'll see a widget showing its location; likewise, if you have an upcoming calendar appointment, it will be front and center.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to use the siri modular watch face, tap and hold on the screen, go to the end of the list, tap the plus button, and find and add the siri modular watch face. Once you do, you'll start seeing dynamic widgets when you wake up your watch. Don't expect much personalization from this watch face, however. You can customize the colors and add three small complications, but that's it.

Berdasarkan laporan, the double-tap gesture is one of my favorite apple watch features. In watchOS 27, Apple took the gesture one step forward. By tapping your thumb and index finger together twice, you can do things like answer a call or reply to a message. You can now use the double-tap gesture to scroll through your widgets; if you perform a single tap, it then opens the highlighted widget or the shortcut. This means you can open and browse the weather app, or start a workout, without ever touching your Apple Watch's screen.

Diungkapkan bahwa your apple watch's new music recognition app has native shazam integration. What's more, Shazam will record your request even when you're offline and away from your iPhone. The moment you reconnect, the service will identify the songs, which you can see in the Shazam app on your iPhone or Apple Watch.

Diungkapkan bahwa it seems like apple has a library of songs it uses for offline recognition, because in my testing, it was able to recognize a coldplay song instantly, even when in airplane mode. To use it, you can either open the Music Recognition app, or you can add the widget for faster access. Scroll up on the Home Screen, go to the bottom of the screen, tap the Edit button, then the Plus button, and add the Music Recognition widget.

Diungkapkan bahwa apple watches have traditionally lacked a live step count widget or complication. But even still, these apps never showed live data. To find your step count, you had to go to the bottom of the Activity app, or rely on third-party apps. You’d always have to wait a couple of seconds to see the updated stats.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, now, if you own the latest apple watch series 12 or the ultra 4, you can add a live step count widget or complication to the apple watch face or the smart stack. This will show you your precise step count at all times. To use it, go to the bottom of the Smart Stack, tap the Edit button, then tap the Plus button. Here, find and add the new Step count widget.

Sebagaimana diketahui, siri is no longer a voice assistant that you use for one-off tasks. With Siri AI, you can now carry on multiple conversations with context and memory. It's not as robust as ChatGPT or Claude, but you can use Siri AI for brainstorming, researching, and jotting down ideas for later.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the siri ai app on the iphone shows all your conversations, and so does the apple watch. To use it, press the Digital Crown once, then tap the Siri app icon in the center. Tap a conversation to continue your chat on the Apple Watch. This will open up all your conversations instead of calling upon Siri. This means you can continue your Siri AI conversations and view past chats on your Apple Watch. Of course, anything you do here will be reflected in the Siri app on your iPhone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the new find my app on the apple watch shows a single map for finding people, devices, and items. This means you can now locate your family members who are sharing their location with you, as well as AirTags or other Find My items from the watchOS app.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after opening the app, you can use the digital crown to zoom in or out of the map. Use touch to pan around. The map doesn't show all items and people at once, though. Tap the Menu button at the bottom-right corner, and then switch between People, Items, or Devices. If you have multiple items, you can scroll through them using the Digital Crown.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while it's not a whoop-level feature, the apple watch now includes a readiness score. Instead of individually looking at your training load, sleep score, and vitals, you now have one number that gives you the whole picture.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the readiness score ranges from 0 to 10 and is based on your recent fitness activity, sleep data, and background health monitoring. This feature, though, is only available on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. If you have a score of 8 to 10, your Apple Watch thinks you can push yourself, or "go for it," as it says; if it's below 5, the watch thinks you should consider lighter activity. You can use the new Readiness app on your Apple Watch to see this data, but you can also access it on your iPhone in the Fitness app's new Readiness section.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, low power mode isn't your only option when it comes to extending the battery life for your apple watch. With it, your Apple Watch disables some features, like splits and alerts, and reduces the frequency of GPS and heart rate readings, in the hopes of extending your battery throughout your entire exercise. To use it, go to the Workout app and select the workout you want. watchOS 27 offers a special Max Extended Workout mode just for long workouts. Tap the Goals button in the top-right corner, and choose the Extended option. Then, switch to the Max Extended option and start your workout.

Diungkapkan bahwa the apple watch series 12 and ultra 4 come with a set of audio intelligence features that use the microphones on the apple watch, paired with ai models (both local and cloud-based), to identify sounds, music, and record conversation. Thanks to this new feature, one of the iPhone's accessibility features also makes its way to the Apple Watch.

Berdasarkan laporan, sound recognition can alert you when it hears sirens, alarms, doorbells, and more, even when your iphone isn’t around. To set this up, go to the Settings app on your iPhone and navigate to Accessibility > Sound & Name Recognition > Sound Recognition. Here, enable the sounds you want to monitor, and make sure to turn on the Detect using Apple Watch toggle.

#750. Five Hacks Every Apple Watch Series 12 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026

Five Hacks Every Apple Watch Series 12 User Should Know

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/best-apple-watch-series-12-hacks?utm_medium=RSS

Berdasarkan laporan, the latest apple watches have a lot of new features that older watches don't, so i figured it was time for a new list of hacks. While our general Apple Watch and fitness tracking hacks are still golden, Series 12 devices offer new features like native step counting, a Readiness app, an upgraded heart rate sensor, an AI-based version of Siri, and "audio intelligence" that can replay and summarize real-life conversations, within limits. Here's how to get the most out of them.

Berdasarkan laporan, the series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest apple watch models. Enjoy it! To add a step counter to your watch face, long-press on the clock screen to edit it, tap on a complication (that’s what Apple calls those little icons and numbers that appear on some watch faces), choose Activity, and then tap Steps.

Berdasarkan laporan, you don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion. Keep it off except when you have a structured conversation that you’ll want to refer to later. A button in your Apple Watch’s Control Center can turn the feature on and off. This feature is currently in beta (which you can try now if you want to), but is expected to be available to everyone later this year.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's worth turning off the default setting not just because of the creepiness factor, but also because the recaps work best when there is a single subject of conversation, with a clear start and end, and just one context. If you leave recaps running all the time, your doctor’s appointment will get mixed in with your grocery shopping, YouTube watching, and everyday chatter.

Berdasarkan laporan, to finish off a recap and make it useful, take a look at the recap shortly after the conversation, tap the three-dots menu, and hit edit. Siri won’t identify speakers and seems to shy away from including certain details, like people’s names. You’ll be able to adjust the notes and add your own important details. You can add in what it missed and also create your own bullet points so that everything gets noted down while it’s still fresh in your mind.

This one isn’t specific to the Series 12, but if you haven’t gotten on board with the pinch and wrist flick gestures yet, now is a great time.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, first, the wrist flick: if a notification is on your screen, or you’re otherwise looking at something you’d rather be done with, just flick your wrist away from you and then back toward you, as if there were a crumb on the watch face and you wanted to knock it off. This will bring you back to the watch face and close whatever you were looking at.

Diungkapkan bahwa the double pinch is another useful one, although apple calls it double tap. You don’t need to touch the watch face at all. Performing a double pinch when no notification is on screen will bring up your smart stack. The watch detects the pinch from subtle movements in your wrist, and it will open the notification. So, when you get a notification or a call, look at it on your watch, and pinch your thumb and forefinger (of the watch hand) together twice. This is confusing because you aren’t double tapping the watch, you’re tapping your thumb and forefinger together while wearing the watch. You can then use the wrist flick to close the notification. You can then double-pinch to move to the next card in the smart stack, or single-pinch to open that card and see its details.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you want to learn even more gestures, go into the watch app, and select accessibility and then hand gestures. You can remap a whole-fist “clench” to do the same thing as pressing the digital crown, for example, or to open the control center or Siri.

Berdasarkan laporan, a little rude, perhaps, but helpful: with the new ai-based siri, sometimes answers to questions can be long-winded. If Siri launches into a novel-length response and you’re not interested in hearing all that, just put your palm over the screen. You’ll instantly be transported back to your watch face, and the Siri response will stop.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you still want to see those longer responses without having siri read the whole thing to you, you can set this up on your phone, and the settings will carry over to your watch. On your iPhone, go to Settings and tap Siri, then Responses. Select Silent responses instead of Spoken responses. You can then read through her answers, or skim them, as you prefer.

Black Friday vs. Cyber Monday: Which day should you shop for the best deals?

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://mashable.com/article/black-friday-vs-cyber-monday-deals

Sebagaimana diketahui, once two distinct deal-shopping days, black friday and cyber monday have basically merged into one massive shopping extravaganza. The lines really began to blur when the world shut down in 2020, and brick-and-mortar stores hosted online sales in lieu of in-person Black Friday events. In 2026, lines outside stores are practically nonexistent. We certainly can't see them.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while major retailers will be running holiday sales throughout all of november, savvy shoppers know that black friday and cyber monday (and the few days surrounding them) still remain the absolute biggest shopping days of the year for their ability to reliably trigger record-low prices on big-ticket items (like tvs, apple devices, smartwatches, headphones, and of course, amazon's own devices). That includes discounts that beat Amazon's massively hyped October Prime Day deals.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you're debating when you should start adding big-ticket items to your cart and whether it's better to shop on black friday or cyber monday, you've come to the right place. After years of covering both sales extensively, here's our expert analysis.

Sebagaimana diketahui, way back in the age of myspace and aim — aka 2005 — the national retail federation debuted the term "cyber monday" after realizing that the monday after thanksgiving saw a flood of online sales. This was likely due to shoppers using their faster internet connections at work on Monday morning to snag deals, or at least that's what they credited it to. That, of course, and the fact that online retailers wanted some of that holiday shopping bread, too. Thus, two distinct deal-shopping days were born: Black Friday, for those who wanted to shop in stores the day after Thanksgiving, and Cyber Monday, for those who preferred shopping from the comfort of their desks.

Sebagaimana diketahui, over 20 years later, there's little — if any — real difference between the two due to the alleged "death of retail. " Everyone and everything is online, so why wouldn't Black Friday be? Based on our years of experience covering both, we can truly say neither is a "better" day to shop. It really comes down to what you're looking for and how much demand there is for it. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you see a solid deal, grab it, no matter which sale title it falls under. There's not a tremendous amount of distinction anymore in terms of discounts on particular products, as there was in previous years. However, there are still rules to follow in some product categories: TV deals tend to be more dramatic and widespread for Black Friday, with a higher likelihood of selling out before the clock even turns to Cyber Monday, while waiting for Cyber Monday to double-check that there's not a new, better laptop deal is often wise.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but with the blurred lines of cyber week, many of these deals will cross over. com, "Some TV deals will feature flashy discounts during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, but they might not have the specs you're after. As noted at BlackFriday. ".

Unofficially, it basically starts the second Black Friday ends, with retailers calling sales "Cyber Monday" deals as early as Saturday, Nov. 28. 30 in 2026. #753. If Your Google Pixel's Camera Is Suddenly Broken, Here's the Fix

📅 13 Nov 2026

If Your Google Pixel's Camera Is Suddenly Broken, Here's the Fix

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/if-your-google-pixels-camera-is-suddenly-broken-theres-a-fix?utm_medium=RSS

Diungkapkan bahwa updates are generally good for your devices. The latest Chrome update, for example, patches an actively exploited security vulnerability, while Apple's latest updates stop people from seeing iMessages they shouldn't have access to. In most cases, it's beneficial to update your tech to the latest software version whenever possible.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as google pixel users are discovering this week. As reported by Android Authority, Google's November update apparently shipped with a bug that breaks some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 cameras. Seeing as Pixels are rather famous for their shooters, this is a decidedly unfortunate glitch.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, here's the situation: following the november update, some users are opening their pixel camera apps to find an error that reads, "something went wrong. What's more, some users are reportedly saying that the issue is present on third-party camera apps, not just the Pixel Camera app. Others aren't receiving the error, but are instead running into a blank Camera viewfinder, as if the lens is totally covered. Close and open the Camera app again," with a "Learn More" link to, well, learn more. That would imply this is an issue with the camera system-wide, not just the Pixel Camera app itself.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to be clear, it doesn't seem like this is a universal issue. It's not like all Pixel users are now running with broken cameras. But based on the forum complaints Android Authority discovered, it seems reasonable to assume that this glitch isn't limited to just a handful of unlucky Pixel owners.

Berdasarkan laporan, luckily, there is an apparent workaround here, though it's not totally obvious. Some users are having no luck restarting their Pixels, while others report that a factory reset wasn't enough to restore camera functionality.

Berdasarkan laporan, what does appear to work, however, is shutting your pixel down and waiting five minutes or so. It's not clear why, but giving your Pixel a chance to "breathe" seems to shake the glitch and bring back your camera. As Android Authority reports, that fix comes from "Diamond and Gold product experts" on Google's Support forum.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if your pixel's camera is giving you grief following the november update, this workaround is definitely worth a try—especially since more drastic measures don't actually seem to do anything. As the issue does seem to be rather widespread, I wouldn't be surprised to see Google issue a patch in the coming days. But until then, turning your phone off for five minutes may be a decent compromise.

#755. 10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026

10 Privacy Hacks Every Mac User Should Know

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/privacy-hacks-every-mac-user-should-know?utm_medium=RSS

Sebagaimana diketahui, emily long is a freelance writer based in salt lake city. After graduating from Duke University, she spent several years reporting on the federal workforce for Government Executive, a publication of Atlantic Media Company, in Washington, D. C. She has nearly a decade of experience as a freelancer covering tech (including issues related to security, privacy, and streaming) as well as personal finance and travel.

Berdasarkan laporan, in addition to lifehacker, her work has been featured on wirecutter, tom’s guide, and zdnet. S. and as a content editor. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

Sebagaimana diketahui, apple has a pretty good track record on privacy. There are plenty of opt-in settings that make it even harder for anyone to snoop on your device and activity. The company bakes a number of protections into its OSes to keep your data from being shared or stolen. That said, you can make your Apple devices even more secure. These are the best privacy hacks for your Mac.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, enabling the macos firewall (which is off by default) adds a layer of protection against external devices on your wifi network, as well as unauthorized apps from initiating a connection to your device. This can interfere with certain essential activity when you're on your home network, but it's a valuable security setting when on public wifi. This makes it more difficult for hackers and malware to know your device exists, much less attack it. Turning on Stealth Mode prevents your Mac from even responding to these requests, essentially making it invisible to anything that's scanning a network you're connected to. You can leave Firewall on all the time and enable Stealth Mode only as needed. Go to Settings > Network > Firewall, flip the toggle, then hit Options to manage Stealth Mode.

Berdasarkan laporan, another hack for maintaining privacy on public networks is to enable rotating mac addresses, which randomizes the identifier your device broadcasts when scanning for and connecting to wifi. Rotating addresses are best for public, shared networks you temporarily connect to, and don't require a login via a captive portal (like hotel wifi). If you use either your real MAC address or a fixed one (random but unchanging), it's easier to track your activity on that network, including when you arrive, how long you stay, and when you leave. You can turn this on for specific networks via Settings > Wi-Fi > [Network Name] > Details and change Private Wi-Fi address to Rotating.

Sebagaimana diketahui, images and screenshots contain metadata, such as timestamps, device and hardware details, and, in the case of photos, physical location. Select the file and hit control + click to bring up an options menu, then go to Quick Actions > Convert Image. (This is also useful for quickly converting HEIC to JPEG without opening a separate app. Uncheck the box next to Preserve Metadata, then hit Convert. Much of this information is stripped automatically when you share files to social media or via encrypted messaging apps, but if you're sending them via text or email, posting to forums, or sharing over AirDrop, metadata remains intact. You can easily remove metadata from your images right on your desktop. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, apple collects information about your device for diagnostic purposes or to improve apps and services, some of which is shared with third-party app developers. This may include crash and usage data as well as recordings and transcripts of Siri interactions and iCloud analytics. You can disable sharing for some or all of these categories under Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements.

Diungkapkan bahwa you may be surprised by the number of apps and system services that use your device's location in the background. You can also turn off location permissions for some Apple apps and services if you're not using them on your device, like Weather and Maps. You should definitely disable location services for third-party apps that don't require location to function. You can find these toggles under Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services. Finally, tap System Services and disable location for any non-essential features—at the very least, disable "Mac Analytics" and "Significant Locations & routes" (which lets your Mac and other iCloud devices learn locations and routes you use often).

Berdasarkan laporan, third-party apps on your mac that need access to your device's camera and microphone have to request permission, and it's easy to grant this in the moment and then forget that you've allowed it. You should regularly audit which apps have these permissions and revoke access from those that don't need them on a day-to-day basis. Disabling them forces the app to ask again. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone or Camera to see the allowed apps and flip the toggle to disable permissions.

Berdasarkan laporan, another permission type you may have granted without much thought is local network access. While this may be useful for services like Spotify that cast to connected hardware, other utilities, media apps, and games probably don't need to be mapping your network in the background. This allows third-party apps to discover and communicate with other devices—printers, smart speakers, and IoT devices—on your home wifi. Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network to audit permissions and disable those that aren't needed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, another important permission to check concerns third-party apps that have access to your mac's full disk, which includes data from mail, messages, safari, home, time machine, and admin settings. If an app only works with files you explicitly open and save, it doesn't need full disk access. Legitimate use cases may include antivirus and malware scanners, productivity tools, or backup utilities that you trust. You can also audit which apps have access to specific files and folders. This is under Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access or Files & Folders.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you're using icloud to store photos, files, and device backups, your data is encrypted on apple's servers and in transit. Be careful, though: If you lose access to this recovery method, you will lose your data. Apple still holds the decryption key, which is useful if you somehow get locked out of your account and need help recovering it, but for sensitive data—including device backups—end-to-end encryption is the most secure way to ensure no one but you can gain access. You'll need to set up an alternative recovery method, such as your device passcode with two-factor authentication, a recovery contact, or a recovery key. You can enable Advanced Data Protection on your Mac under System Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Advanced Data Protection > Turn On. Advanced Data Protection is an opt-in setting for iCloud that encrypts your information end to end. Note that some iCloud data, including passwords and payment methods, are already end-to-end encrypted by default.

Berdasarkan laporan, you probably already know that your email isn't actually all that private, especially if you have a free account with a major service provider like gmail (google) or outlook (microsoft). But if you are sending sensitive information via email, you can minimize what can be snooped on and by whom using end-to-end encryption, which generally ensures that only the recipient can read your message. Here's what you need to know about email encryption and how to set up an extra layer of privacy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as this in-depth explainer from adaptive security describes, most emails are encrypted in transit via transport layer security (tls), which prevents anyone from reading your message as it travels from server to server. However, encryption is temporarily stripped at each server: content is received and processed in plaintext and then re-encrypted when it leaves, meaning it could be read, logged, and distributed by the server provider.

Sebagaimana diketahui, emails are also typically encrypted at rest—for example, while sitting on google's servers and in a gmail recipient's inbox. But this only prevents someone with physical access to the server hardware from reading messages, as Google still holds the encryption key and can access stored data. And, as PCMag points out, Google is scanning your messages to a degree, and it (along with other email providers) can and will hand emails over to law enforcement and government agencies in some cases.

Diungkapkan bahwa by contrast, with end-to-end encryption (e2ee), emails are readable only on the sender's and recipient's devices, and can be decrypted only with the recipient's private key. They're never translated into plaintext as they pass between and through servers to their destination, meaning that no one—including server providers, hackers, or law enforcement—can view the content. For example, metadata like subject lines and email addresses may remain in plaintext, and encrypted messages are still susceptible to phishing. It's worth noting, though, that E2EE is not impenetrable nor a total guarantee of privacy. Plus, forwarding an encrypted message breaks the encryption.

Berdasarkan laporan, still, end-to-end encryption is especially useful when sending sensitive information that may be valuable to bad actors, though if security and privacy are a high priority, you may want to consider it for all of your emails. How you deploy encryption depends on whether you are adding it to your current email or switching to a dedicated provider.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you have an account with a major email provider like gmail, outlook, or apple mail, you can add a third-party tool that layers an encryption protocol like openpgp on top of your existing account. Mailvelope is a browser add-on (and therefore a desktop-only tool) available in Chrome, Firefox, and Edge, though it can also be installed on other browsers, like Brave, that are built on the same architecture. PCMag recommends PreVeil, SecureMyEmail, and Virtru (which is limited to Gmail users in Chrome) for those who want to keep their current emails. FlowCrypt integrates with Gmail and Google Workspace on desktop and mobile.

Diungkapkan bahwa note that enterprise users of google workspace and microsoft 365 have access to true end-to-end encryption without third-party add-ons. Gmail's Confidential mode and Outlook's Encrypt feature, available to all users, are not E2EE equivalents, as Google and Microsoft, respectively, still manage the keys.

Berdasarkan laporan, for those who are willing to start fresh with a new email address (or who have a custom domain), providers like proton mail or tuta offer native end-to-end encryption. The caveat: by default, this is only between users on the same service, so from one Proton user to another. If you want to send an end-to-end encrypted email from Proton to a Gmail user, for example, you have to set up password protection (and share the password via another secure channel) or use a PGP-compatible tool like those listed above. You can also Proton's Gmail integration does allow for end-to-end encryption, but only if both Gmail parties are using the Proton integration.

Berdasarkan laporan, the bottom line here is that email wasn't designed to be a highly secure form of communication. End-to-end encryption does add a layer of privacy and security if you jump through hoops to set it up, but it's still susceptible to human error and social engineering.

Step 1: Open Calculator on iPhone.

Step 2: Tap the clock icon in the top left.

Step 3: Behold your brilliance.

Berdasarkan laporan, don't bully, just lightly roast. A gentle searing, even.

#764. Microsoft Officially Apologized for Yesterday's Outages

📅 13 Nov 2026

Microsoft Officially Apologized for Yesterday's Outages

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://lifehacker.com/tech/microsoft-officially-apologized-for-yesterdays-outages?utm_medium=RSS

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you were having trouble accessing certain services like microsoft teams or outlook, you were not alone. According to Downdetector, which tracks user reports of issues with websites and platforms, Microsoft 365, Teams, Copilot, Teams, and OneDrive were all experiencing issues. Early Thursday afternoon, many of Microsoft's biggest apps and services were experiencing downtime. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft has restored service to many users, and has officially apologized for the outages.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when i first published this article on thursday, i couldn't even load microsoft 365's status page. (I've reported on many service outages, but I can't recall a time when a service's status page was also down. ) Even as of Friday afternoon, the page still says "Service degradation on Microsoft 365 (Business or Enterprise)," and Microsoft says the following services may be affected: Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center, Microsoft 365 Education, Microsoft Copilot 365, Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Graph, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Planner, Microsoft Power Apps, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft To Do, Power BI, SharePoint Online, Universal Print, and Windows 365.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, looking specifically at outlook, microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports thursday afternoon, signaling a major issue somewhere in microsoft's pipeline. The reports did "slow down" throughout the day, but Downdetector still showed over 50,000 reports coming in every 15 minutes when I checked Thursday afternoon.

Berdasarkan laporan, while the root cause of the issue was a mystery throughout thursday's outage, microsoft confirmed the problem in an apology on friday. According to the company, "This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI [or] agents. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, microsoft says it is "deeply sorry" for the disruption to its customers and partners. The company says the fix rolled out slower than some might expect, since it wanted to restore service gradually to evaluate stability at each stage. It also says it will release a full post-incident report once it completes a review.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, during the outage, the company had confirmed that some of its infrastructure was experiencing elevated load, which it said was likely contributing to the issues. The company then thought a specific component responsible for processing server health may be the reason the system is failing health checks. Microsoft then said it was pausing all deployments and moving traffic from affected infrastructure, and that it found that a number of its servers were unexpectedly unavailable after failing health checks. Microsoft said an alternative service health check method successfully restarted some of the affected servers. The company was then actively restarting and validating affected servers to bring them back to service.

#768. Reverse engineering my Coway air purifier to ditch the cloud

📅 11 Nov 2026

Reverse engineering my Coway air purifier to ditch the cloud

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://scottjg.com/posts/2026-11-11-reverse-engineering-my-coway-air-purifier-to-ditch-the-cloud/

Sebagaimana diketahui, the year is 2017. A string of annual wildfires rocks the West Coast. The sky looks like this in the daytime:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, my home, like many in the bay area, has no insulation and isn’t really air sealed. To avoid choking on soot, a lot of people started buying air purifiers like this one:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s an overpriced box fan with a hepa filter and an air quality sensor. Also, FWIW, the device works. It has some controls for the fan speed, and it can also automatically ramp up if the air quality is bad. It’s ugly, but they’re so ubiquitous around here that I feel like no one even notices them anymore. It really does improve air quality.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this device became a staple item in our household when my wife eventually started cranking up the fan at night for white noise (a dual purpose!). Over time, I have become accustomed to it and now also require it to sleep.

Berdasarkan laporan, our home also has smart lighting, and it’s all integrated with apple home. At night, I always press the “Good Night” button, which shuts off all the lights. I really wanted to tie the fan into that. I’d press Good Night, the lights would shut off, and the fan would crank up to my wife’s preferred white noise volume.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the old airmega didn’t have wi-fi, so there was no easy way to integrate it with apple home. When it eventually broke, I bought the now-discontinued Coway Airmega IconS (for non-discontinued Wi-Fi models, check out the Airmega 250S or Airmega MightyS). It’s still just a box fan with a HEPA filter, but it’s considerably more expensive, aims to look like a piece of fancy mid-century furniture, and most importantly, can be controlled over Wi-Fi (sort of).

Berdasarkan laporan, coway’s iphone app is an absolutely classic iot affair. Thankfully, a brave soul reverse-engineered the app and wrote an integration for Home Assistant. It polls the Coway cloud service for status updates and sends commands through it to control the fan. The integration more or less pretends to be the phone app. It takes forever to load, and it asks me to change my password nearly every time I launch it. Home Assistant bridges that to Apple Home and… voilà!.

Berdasarkan laporan, the downside of this approach is that you’re still at the mercy (or lack thereof) of the coway cloud service. It seems like at least once or twice a year, it breaks.

Here are some of the reasons I have seen it break:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on top of this, it seems unlikely that coway will maintain this service forever. I suspect that eventually, like all IoT manufacturers, they’ll either charge for this service or discontinue it. My fan model is already discontinued (though there are other Wi-Fi enabled models, so… who knows).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i admit, i have been lazy. com (or whatever) and checks that the server’s SSL certificate is valid. For years, I put off trying to figure out a way to ditch the Coway cloud, because if the device was really locked down, it would be pretty tough. Presumably, when the fan starts up, it connects to coway. Most likely, I wouldn’t be able to make a fake certificate that passes that check, so the fan wouldn’t connect to my server.

Diungkapkan bahwa also, setting up a man-in-the-middle (mitm) environment is just a pain in the neck. To do that, you have to configure a bunch of routing and firewall rules to redirect traffic. The fan would have to connect to an isolated Wi-Fi network that routes all its traffic through my own server on the way out to the internet. None of this is impossible (I’ve done it before), but it’s a hassle to set up, and it’s always finicky to get right. And once you have it set up, that’s just step one.

All that said, two major things have changed.

First, there was a recent security incident (October 2026) where someone discovered that eMudhra, one of the trusted internet certificate authorities, had used a very weak parameter for some of its private keys.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for the next few days or weeks, anyone now has a root ca thanks to emudhra. Time to have some fun with MiTMing unwilling devices!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so, if the device is unpatched and it has hardcoded root certificates and it doesn’t pin the cloud service’s certificate, then… maybe that’s a way in. Admittedly, that’s a lot of ifs, but assuming the device doesn’t have any major security mistakes in its design, this could be the foothold needed to take control of it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the second thing is simply ai. An LLM can set up everything you need for a MitM environment, so you can get straight to sleuthing out how the fan works. It can do this unattended, in minutes.

Once you can sit between the fan and the internet, you can see how it communicates, which should help us understand how to get the fan to talk to us instead of the cloud.

Initially, I tried to set it up like this:.

Berdasarkan laporan, this actually didn’t work, because a raspberry pi uses a smallish pcb trace antenna that doesn’t get a ton of signal strength. With the Pi in the room with my router, the signal was too weak to reach the fan. I guess I could’ve moved the fan into the room with the router, but why do that when I can solve this with a convoluted technical solution?.

Berdasarkan laporan, the raspberry pi uses its wi-fi radio to run its own access point for the fan to connect to. It can’t easily do that while also connecting over Wi-Fi to the home network. So, I moved the Pi into the room with the fan and plugged its Ethernet port into my laptop, which bridges it to the home network over Wi-Fi:.

I’m not really making a value judgment here on whether this is a fair thing to block, but Claude will not oblige the request, not even for… uhh… testing purposes.

Luckily, ChatGPT has no such compunctions.

After a few rounds of that, here are the nftables rules it ended up with:.

Basically, the masquerade rule translates the traffic from the isolated Wi-Fi network out through our home internet, and the redirect rule forwards HTTP/HTTPS to a running instance of mitmproxy.

Also on the Pi, mitmproxy runs with its web interface, mitmweb, using a command line like this:.

Yes, off the shelf, mitmproxy has a built-in option (--emudhra-old) to automatically use the eMudhra root CA to intercept traffic.

Diungkapkan bahwa next, i used the iphone app to set up the fan on our pi-mitm-test wi-fi network. Partway through, the app reported that setup failed. Let’s glance at the mitmproxy web interface:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so, we know there was some kind of connection issue, since the app said the fan failed to connect. But it clearly got onto our isolated Wi-Fi, because it made a request.

Diungkapkan bahwa the request is very suspicious. This interface only shows connections that got far enough to make an actual HTTP request. It looks like the fan is downloading the root certificate for Amazon’s certificate authority over plain HTTP. If, for example, the fan doesn’t accept the eMudhra cert we’re using to impersonate the real servers, its HTTPS connections will fail before that point and never show up in the list.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hypothesis: the device downloads this public certificate over http so it has something to validate its later (currently unseen) https connections against. It doesn’t have any root certificates built in at all.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mitmproxy has a plugin mode where you can modify specific requests. We can use it to swap in mitmproxy’s own generated CA certificate in place of this public one. If our hypothesis is correct, the fan will trust that CA, and we can intercept the rest of its traffic.

Sure enough, the device now fully connects, and we can see some new requests:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we can intercept the traffic between the fan and the server, which means we could probably build our own server to replace the coway iocare cloud. It also turns out we don’t need the eMudhra hack at all. The fan downloads its root CA cert over plain HTTP. It was always MitM-able.

Berdasarkan laporan, the one thing missing is that none of these requests have anything to do with changing the fan speed or anything else you can do in the app. If you run tcpdump on the Pi while clicking buttons in the app, you can see encrypted traffic on port 8883, the standard port for MQTT over TLS. That’s easy to figure out, though. MQTT is a message bus protocol commonly used in IoT devices.

Going back to the POST in the request list above, here’s what that API call returned:.

So, if we control the response to this call, we control which keys the fan uses to connect to the MQTT server, and also where that MQTT server is.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for now, we can write another mitmproxy plugin that injects our own key into this response, and then use that to proxy the mqtt traffic. The plugin code gets kinda long, so I didn’t include it here, but AI generates it fairly quickly. mitmproxy doesn’t decode MQTT, but it can still show us the raw stream:.

Diungkapkan bahwa the data looks like a mix of binary and ascii gibberish, but it’s a standard mqtt protocol stream. When I adjust the fan speed in the app, you can see a new message come from the Coway server to the device. Usually, I’d load this into a traffic dissector and make a table of what gibberish comes in when I press each button in the app, but now….

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there’s enough here now to build our own web server that hands the fan its certificates and configuration during setup, plus our own mqtt server to send it commands. That completely cuts the Coway cloud out of the picture during normal operation, but we’re still using the Coway app to set the device up. We also still need a fairly annoying MitM environment to get the fan to connect to us instead of Coway.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when you use the coway app to set up the fan, it searches for the device via bluetooth. I was hoping we could figure out a way to configure the device ourselves, without the app. Plus, if we’re lucky, we might find something else useful along the way.

Diungkapkan bahwa i have reverse-engineered bluetooth devices before. My old strategy was to get the Android version of the app, decompile it, and then just pore over the code. Developers often obfuscate their apps, which makes the decompiled code harder to read. It’s not always as straightforward as it sounds. Some bytecode also doesn’t decompile cleanly back to source code, which means you end up having to read the raw bytecode.

Sebagaimana diketahui, still, in my opinion, this is usually easier than dealing with iphone apps. Android apps are usually written in Java (or Kotlin), and it’s just easier to reverse-engineer Java apps than apps compiled from Swift or Objective-C.

This time, I tried a new strategy, which was to use the built-in Android Bluetooth debug logs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, then, i connected the phone over usb and asked the ai to drive the phone via adb, look at the bluetooth logs, and reconstruct the protocol. Sure enough, the next thing it did was pull the Coway app off the phone, decompile it. The AI took a while to churn through this task. Eventually, it identified that the message carrying the Wi-Fi configuration was encrypted. Since we would ultimately need to figure out what algorithm was used for the encryption, we would probably have to look at the decompiled app. Then, it started matching up the source code with the Bluetooth logs.

After all that, we can see the provisioning works like this:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, needless to say, figuring this out end to end from the decompiled android app would have been very time consuming to do by hand. AI really comes in clutch here. It’d be at least hours of work (likely days). It took the AI about 20 minutes.

Diungkapkan bahwa the good part, though, is that all the data you need to decrypt that payload is in the bluetooth logs we captured from the phone, so we can check that our reimplementation is correct just from those. From there, the AI made quick work of reimplementing the whole setup flow in a little Python script.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i was watching the progress pretty carefully while this was going on. Two of the URLs from our capture are set right in this payload (caUrl and certSvrUrl). The AI never actually showed me the full payload, but I could see it in the intermediate output of the scripts it was writing. And that’s when I noticed something. The first tells the fan where to download the root CA cert over plain HTTP, and the second tells it where to POST over HTTPS to get its MQTT configuration.

Diungkapkan bahwa since we’re the ones sending this payload now, we can point those urls anywhere we want. Most importantly, that means we don’t have to do any MitM anymore. We just have to run our own server and plug in its URLs when we set up the fan.

Berdasarkan laporan, based on the findings in this article, i was able to build a home assistant custom integration for the fan. My Home Assistant server doesn’t have Bluetooth, and it’s pretty far away from my fan, so I opted to do the provisioning with Web Bluetooth. That way you can bring your laptop next to the fan and provision it to talk to Home Assistant directly.

After that, the device talks directly over Wi-Fi to Home Assistant.

And, more importantly, it gets bridged from Home Assistant to my Apple Home.

Sebagaimana diketahui, all in a day’s work. Now, I can finally click Good Night.

I don't post that often, so it won't be much email.

#771. After 600 experiments, here's what I discovered about JEPA world models

📅 11 Nov 2026

After 600 experiments, here's what I discovered about JEPA world models

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://haddyalchaer.com/jepa

Solving long-horizon tasks without any extra training.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there's a big debate in ai right now about what a world model should be. Most of the pixels don't matter for deciding what to do, and many of them can't be predicted at all. Most of the attention goes to generative world models, which predict the future by generating it, usually in pixels. Many scientists, including Yann LeCun, argue that this is wasted effort. [1].

Sebagaimana diketahui, the proposed alternative is jepa, the joint-embedding predictive architecture. The predictor takes that embedding plus an action and predicts the embedding of the next frame. The encoder turns each frame of observation into a learned embedding, a compact vector that describes the scene. It has three parts: an encoder, a predictor and a planner. The planner then tries hundreds of action sequences inside the predictor and picks the one whose predicted end state lands closest to the embedding of the goal. The whole loop runs in embedding space, so the model only has to learn the parts of the scene that are important for deciding actions.

Diungkapkan bahwa this year a team including lecun released lewm [2], a jepa world model whose main benchmark is push-t [3], a simulation where a robot pushes a gray t-shaped block across a table until the t sits in the green target position shown in a goal image. I've spent the last few months running 600 experiments on it.

Diungkapkan bahwa the first thing i wanted to know was how much lewm is held back by its predictions, so i started by swapping out the predictor for the simulator's perfect physics, while keeping everything else the same. The version with true physics succeeded 77%. I then gave both versions long-horizon tasks, with the goal 75 steps away, along with the same subgoals: frames from an expert demonstration, one every 25 steps. Vanilla LeWM succeeded 78% of the time. Along the kinds of paths it was trained on, LeWM's predictions are already as good as perfect physics for planning.

That means the next gains for a JEPA world model come from how the trained architecture is used, and that's where most of my 600 experiments went.

Sebagaimana diketahui, without retraining the model once, i found four new planning methods. The first two together took LeWM's success rate on long-horizon tasks from 22% to 85%, about the same as a planner that is handed the ideal subgoals from an expert demonstration. The other two methods extend LeWM to harder goals, and one of them, a single change to how the goal is scored, raised the success rate by 60 points, three times as much as swapping in perfect physics did.

Diungkapkan bahwa used exactly as published, lewm succeeds on 22% of long-horizon tasks, where the goal is 75 steps away. [2] When the goal is 25 steps away, it reaches it 89. 7% of the time, within a point of the exact-physics version at 90. 5%.

Berdasarkan laporan, so the model is accurate over 25 steps and struggles over 75. The usual explanation is that small prediction errors compound over a long plan, which would call for a better model. I tested that against the alternative on the same 250 long-horizon tasks.

250 long-horizon tasks, goal 75 steps away.

Diungkapkan bahwa exact physics added 20 points. Splitting the task into 25-step segments, each the length LeWM already handles almost perfectly, added nearly 60. LeWM's useful planning horizon is about 25 steps, so it was clear that the way to go further is to chain segments of that length together.

LeWM's planning horizon is about 25 steps.

Berdasarkan laporan, this is hierarchical planning: a high level picks subgoals and a low level reaches them. It's widely considered one of the main open problems for world models, and on Push-T it's worth three times as much as swapping in perfect physics.

Sebagaimana diketahui, extra search doesn't substitute for it. Running the planner four times and keeping the lowest-cost plan took four times the compute and added less than one point, because the four runs almost always succeeded or failed together.

Berdasarkan laporan, the subgoals in this experiment came from an expert demonstration, which a deployed robot won't have. The second method removes that dependence.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lewm was trained on expert demonstrations of the task, and its encoder can embed every frame of them, giving about 460,000 embedded states that i connected into a graph. Each state links to the states that follow it in its own demonstration, and to states in other demonstrations that are close in embedding space. To solve a long-horizon task, the planner searches this graph for a path from the current state to the goal and uses the states along that path as subgoals.

Berdasarkan laporan, this only works if distance in embedding space means something physical, and it does. Take one subgoal the robot can reach within 25 steps and one it can't, and LeWM's embedding distance ranks the reachable one as closer 87% of the time. So the embedding space doubles as a map of what the robot can reach.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the first version had a flaw. A jump between nearby states in two different demonstrations cost the same as a real step, so the search strung jumps together into paths the block could never follow (318 of 1,015 plans tried to use six or more jumps). Using nothing but LeWM's own embeddings of past demonstrations, success on the same 250 long-horizon tasks (goal 75 steps away) went from 62% to 85%, which is the same score received by the planner using expert subgoals. The fix was adding a cost on every jump between demonstrations in the graph. Can't get much better than that, right?.

Planning through a memory of demonstrations.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the caveat is that the standard test takes a demonstration, starts the robot partway through it, and sets the goal a fixed number of steps further along the same demonstration. So every test goal sits on a path that demonstrations already travel, heading for the spot they all end at. That's a reasonable design, but in Push-T every demonstration ends with the block in the same place. For 84% of the standard test's goals, the memory graph already held a nearly identical state from another demonstration.

Diungkapkan bahwa the usual sample is also small. On the official 50 episodes, LeWM succeeded 68% of the time with the goal 50 steps away. On 250 fresh episodes drawn the same way, it succeeded only 44%. Changing nothing but the planner's random seed flipped 38 of 250 episodes between success and failure.

Berdasarkan laporan, that's where i decided to build a harder test, where each task takes its start from one demonstration and its goal from another, so the robot has to travel between states that no single demonstration connects. Under these rules the memory-graph planner succeeds 75% of the time on standard tasks and 45% on the new ones. It only counts as a success if the block stays on target for the last 10 steps. The third and fourth methods I found work on that gap.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a memory graph is only as good as its coverage. When I deleted every stored state near the goal, success fell from 93% to 32%.

Berdasarkan laporan, push-t has a useful symmetry here. So when the graph has no states near a goal, it can take demonstration segments from elsewhere, transform them to fit the gap, and plan through those. The physics of pushing a block doesn't change if you shift, rotate or mirror the whole table. With these transformed segments, success came back to 85%. They also stretch a small memory a long way (a graph built from 1% of the demonstrations plus transformed copies did about as well as one built from 10%).

Filling a gap in memory with transformed demonstrations.

Block reached its target, 250 long-horizon tasks (goal 75 steps away).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the harder test, transformed segments raise success from 45% to 56%, and they help most where demonstrations are thinnest. When the goal lies in the direction the demonstrations flow, the memory-graph planner already succeeds 69% of the time. When it lies the opposite way, plain memory gets 27% and transformed memory gets 46%.

Berdasarkan laporan, i also built an interactive demo where i could place the block anywhere and pick any goal. A goal has to be an image, and an image of the scene has to show the pusher somewhere, so I placed the pusher just behind the goal. In one run, the robot pushed the block to within 14 pixels of the target, close enough to count as solved. Then it pushed the block away from the goal, and kept moving the pusher toward where the pusher was in the goal image.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the goals in the harder test are frames from expert demonstrations, so each one also shows where the expert’s pusher happened to be at that moment. A planner that compares its prediction with the whole goal image is trying to put the pusher there too.

Berdasarkan laporan, to measure how much this matters, i took the model out of the question. I ran the exact-physics planner twice on the same 50 tasks from the harder test, and the only difference was whether its cost included the pusher’s position as well as the block’s.

Diungkapkan bahwa thirty tasks went from failure to success when the pusher was left out, and none went the other way. A split like that happens by chance about twice in a billion. The physics here is from the actual simulator, not predicted, so the 4x in success comes from how the goal was created.

Diungkapkan bahwa the planner that scored the pusher did exactly what it was asked. On the 30 tasks that flipped, it got the pusher to within half a pixel of where the goal image put it, and lost the block on the way. Placing both the T and the pusher in the exact goal position is a much harder problem to solve.

Diungkapkan bahwa but lewm can’t simply be told to ignore the pusher. It compares each prediction against 16 versions of the goal image, all with the block in the same place and the pusher moved to positions taken from stored demonstrations, and keeps the closest match. It scores a plan by the distance between two embeddings, and its embedding of a goal image holds the block and the pusher together, with no part labeled “pusher”. So, as a test, I measured how far a planner gets by searching over the pusher instead. That doubled LeWM’s success on the harder test, from 11% to 23%, without retraining.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this applies to any robot because a goal should just be a set of end states, not a copy of an image. “Put the cup on the shelf” is solved wherever the robot’s arm ends up, but a goal image picks one arm position and makes the planner match it. A good goal accepts every end state that solves the task, and still includes what the task needs from the robot, like coming to rest at the end.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the good news is that large sets of demonstrations already contain many real frames of the same object in the same place, each with the robot somewhere different. Scoring a plan against the closest of those goals allows for a larger set of valid end states to plan for.

Diungkapkan bahwa none of these four discoveries change the model's weights. They apply to LeWM as published, and they should carry over to larger JEPA world models that plan the same way, at no extra training cost.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the biggest open problem remaining is generalizing to tasks that don't have perfect demonstrations. On the harder Push-T test, the best planner holds the block on target 56% of the time, and most of the remaining failures are goals that run against the direction of the data. Closing that gap needs a higher level that can propose its own subgoals beyond the demonstrations, and do it better than today's learned hierarchies like H-JEPA [4], which so far match or slightly beat flat LeWM on Push-T.

Hierarchical subgoal planner on top of LeWM.

Berdasarkan laporan, going in, i assumed lewm's predictions would be the bottleneck, but a jepa small enough to train in a few hours already predicts about as well as the simulator itself, and there are several gains that can be achieved simply by changing the way it plans. What it can't do yet is choose its own subgoals where no demonstration has been. That's what I'm currently working on, and if you want to see more, I'll post about it first on X, @haddyalchaer.

When her visions reveal that three young women, played by Sydney Sweeney, Isabela Merced, and Celeste O’Connor, are being hunted by a mysterious, spider-powered killer (Tahar Rahim), Cassie becomes their only protector. To save them, she’ll have to understand her strange new abilities, along with the secrets of her late mother’s past.

Diungkapkan bahwa why you should watch it: let’s be honest: “madame web” was a legendary box-office flop that critics tore apart on release. It's since become a hilarious watch even for fans of the character. And despite a mostly bad script and even worse acting, there are plenty of moments that will stick with you once it ends. Sebagaimana diketahui, what is it about? before denis villeneuve or david lynch took a crack at frank herbert’s “dune,” chilean-french filmmaker alejandro jodorowsky nearly made the most audacious version of all. This documentary tells the true story of that doomed 1970s production, which Jodorowsky envisioned as a mind-expanding sci-fi epic. Through interviews with the director himself, the documentary charts how he assembled a jaw-dropping team, including artists H. R. Giger and Moebius, effects wizard Dan O’Bannon, a score by Pink Floyd, and a planned cast featuring Salvador Dalí, Orson Welles, and Mick Jagger, only to watch it collapse when no studio would finance it.

Berdasarkan laporan, why you should watch it: even though his film was never made, jodorowsky’s ideas and artwork went on to shape sci-fi landmarks like “alien,” “blade runner”, and “star wars", making this a must-watch for fans. With “Dune: Part Three” on the horizon, there’s no better time to revisit the greatest “Dune” movie that never was.
