#773. Terminal borders that don't cost a cell

📅 13 Nov 2026

Terminal borders that don't cost a cell

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.joshka.net/cell-borders/

Sebagaimana diketahui, this post (and the code behind it) was written with a lot of help from ai. I'm not going to apologize for that. If that bothers you, feel free to close the tab.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i maintain ratatui, so i see a lot of the tuis people build. Many of them end up looking fairly same-ish: plain boxes on a boring background, missing a bunch of the things that good design in other mediums brings us.

Sebagaimana diketahui, borders are part of the problem. They have to take up space, so they become part of the panels people want to build. One option is to drop them and just use color, but borders are really nice for delineating and surrounding things. There are lots of ways to sort of get borders in a terminal, but none that are 100% good. I've drawn enough ┌──┐ by hand to have opinions about this.

Diungkapkan bahwa the usual way is the unicode box drawing block, which has 128 characters for lines, corners and joins. Somehow that's still not enough:.

Diungkapkan bahwa so i've been working on a terminal protocol that draws thin lines on the edges of cells instead. I've got it working as a patch to Ghostty (and an earlier version in Rio before that), and I've built demo apps for it with Ratatui. I'd like feedback from terminal and TUI authors.

Sebagaimana diketahui, every line in that screenshot is a cell border. None of them use up a row or column. The tab labels sit on the top edge of each pane, the text fields are underlined right under the text, and the buttons are one row tall and rounded.

Here's the same app in a terminal without cell borders, falling back to box-drawing characters:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, each pane loses a row and a column on every side, so the log pane shows two fewer lines and the notes wrap differently. The tab labels move inside the frame. The text fields use the underline attribute instead, and the checkbox and buttons turn into brackets.

The settings form, with cell borders and then with the box-drawing fallback:.

Diungkapkan bahwa the tabs are the same story. With cell borders they sit on the pane's top edge. With box characters they need their own row inside the frame:.

Berdasarkan laporan, lines between cells also work for charts. btop-style braille graphs fill every cell with dots, so there's nowhere to put a gridline or an average line without giving up a row. With cell borders they sit on the cell edges between the dots. Here's a monitor in that style, built with Ratatui:.

And the fallback, which has to drop the gridlines:.

Here's the tiling panes demo moving panes around, opening menus and the about dialog:.

Diungkapkan bahwa partway through, it turns on a checkerboard of the cells, which shows how everything lines up with the grid. Toggle it here:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the root of it is that box-drawing characters are text. Each line is a glyph that takes up a whole cell, and pretty much everything annoying about them falls out of that.

Berdasarkan laporan, space is the obvious one. A layout with a couple of levels of nested panels can easily spend 6 or 8 of those 50 rows on nothing but lines. On my 16" laptop with a font I can actually read, the terminal is something like 200x50 (your prefs will move that around a bit). Columns are mostly fine at that size. Rows aren't. That's a lot of screen to give up for decoration.

Berdasarkan laporan, you also can't put a line between two cells that both have something in them. Rounded corners sort of work, except the corner glyph has one background color, and when the panel's background is different from what's around it you get a little square of the wrong color in each corner. So there's no way to underline a text field right under its text, or to outline a button, without adding padding around it. And the line itself is whatever the font decides it is, weight and position included.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, then there's copy and paste. Everyone who's pasted from a TUI into Slack knows the little │ cleanup dance. Select some text inside a box and you get the box too. Sometimes you do want the box (pasting a table into a chat, say), but mostly it's junk. Cell borders aren't text, so they never get copied, which cuts both ways.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a cell border is a cell attribute, like a background color. Each segment has its own color, width, placement and style, and the terminal draws them over the cell grid. Borders are stored in the cells, so they scroll, erase, insert and reflow with the text. Each cell can carry up to twelve line segments: the two halves of each of its four edges, and four arms from its center. What happens on erase or scroll already has an answer, the same one as for colors.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the edges are split into halves so borders line up with quadrant block characters (▖▗▘▝ and friends). Yes, that still uses a character for the fill, and there might be a better way to do that part. That makes it easy to draw a shape that's a half cell in from the grid and still put a neat border around it. One problem at a time.

The same idea could stretch to sextants and octants, or to quarter and eighth widths, if designs need them.

Diungkapkan bahwa lines can be solid, double, dashed or dotted. Each corner and center of a cell can be square or rounded, with a configurable radius and anti-aliased arcs. A rounded corner can name an outside color, so the area outside the arc is painted correctly when the panel's background differs from what's behind it.

Diungkapkan bahwa when two neighboring cells both put a line on their shared edge, they merge into one line. The stroke with the higher priority wins, then the wider one, then the one to the right or below. That way a focused pane can raise its priority and keep its whole outline, whatever order its neighbors were drawn in. My first try was "right/bottom always wins", which lasted until the focused pane lost half its outline to its neighbor.

Everything is one DCS string with a namespace:.

Diungkapkan bahwa the common path is a pen, held in the cursor like the current background color. Set it, print some text, and the printed cells get the borders:.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are also rectangle commands that set or clear borders on existing cells without touching the pen, and a capability query. An app sends the query followed by DA1. If the DA1 reply arrives without a cell-border reply first, the terminal doesn't support it, so the app falls back to box characters and reserves the space they need. Terminals that don't understand the DCS ignore it, the same as any unknown DCS.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the minimum a terminal needs is the pen, the rectangle commands and solid strokes. I've tried to keep that first cut small, because there's always one more ". and this" to add, and that's a slippery slope.

Diungkapkan bahwa line styles, rounded joints, priority and outside colors are extension fields listed in the capability reply, and unknown fields are ignored, so they can be added later. I'd rather the early decisions be two way doors where possible.

Diungkapkan bahwa the spec calls itself version 1 (it's the 1 in dcs 1 + b). That's v1 in the old sense, before we all got bogged down in semver. It doesn't mean done or stable, it means it's the first one I was willing to write down. Read it as v0. 1, or a draft, or whatever you prefer.

Diungkapkan bahwa what none of these give you is a line with its own color and width on each edge. The rationale document covers the prior art in more detail and explains each choice in the protocol.

Sebagaimana diketahui, my own first prototype was in rio (raphamorim/rio#1947), with an earlier version of the spec that used apc instead of dcs. Feedback pointed out that APC isn't safe to reuse: Kermit 95 has run APC payloads as Kermit commands since the 90s. DCS is where structured terminal commands already live, and terminals ignore DCS strings they don't recognize, so I switched to that.

Diungkapkan bahwa when i first showed this around, most of the questions were about these. The spec goes into all of them properly, but here's roughly where I landed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, multiplexers were the first thing people asked about. A multiplexer that doesn't know about the protocol should drop them and answer DA1 itself, and then apps running inside it fall back to box characters like they would anywhere else. tmux and friends redraw panes from their own idea of the cell grid, so passing these sequences through would just put borders in the wrong place. One that does know about it can store borders like any other attribute and redraw them.

Conflicting lines on a shared edge are settled when the terminal renders, using the priority rule above, so it doesn't matter what order the app wrote the cells in.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, erase, insert and delete all work the way they do for background colors. Erased cells pick up the current pen, and lines that get inserted or deleted take their borders along. Scrollback, the alternate screen and reflow mostly come for free, because the border lives in the cell.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on cost: the ghostty change is about 1,650 lines, and a fair chunk of that is tests. Each cell gets a 16-bit border ID, which fits in padding that was already there, so cells don't get any bigger and a screen with no borders costs nothing extra. The IDs point into a table of distinct border sets (about 100 bytes each) that's shared by the whole terminal. A typical TUI only uses a handful of distinct sets, but the table is never freed, so in the worst case (all 65,535 IDs in use) it's somewhere around 10-15 MB.

Berdasarkan laporan, rendering only does extra work for cells that have borders. Each one looks at its four neighbors to resolve shared edges, so changing a row also rebuilds the rows either side of it. Rounded corners cost more, because the anti-aliased arc is drawn as rows of small quads, roughly one per edge pixel. Straight lines are a few solid quads per cell. I haven't benchmarked any of this properly yet, and it's the part I'd most like another set of eyes on.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the spec and rationale are on my ghostty fork. I've only built and run it on macOS so far, so the GTK and OpenGL builds are untested. To build and run it (you'll need Zig 0. The Ghostty branch implements all of version 1. 17 and Xcode):.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, inside that ghostty, the gallery script on the same branch draws the style gallery above. It detects support first, so it's also a quick check for another terminal's implementation:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, once it's running you can flip between views with keys: p placement, c colors, h blocks, j junctions, e halves, s styles and l live. w cycles the stroke width, b turns borders off so you can compare, and q quits. Each view also has a matching flag (--placement, --styles and so on) if you want to start on it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the tiling panes demo is on the ratatui branch. It falls back to box-drawing characters when the terminal doesn't support cell borders, which is how I made the comparison shots above:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, drag panes around with the mouse to retile them. n and v split, x closes, and right click opens a pane menu. Press b to switch between cell borders and box drawing, or g to shade alternate cells and see where the edges are.

Diungkapkan bahwa the btop-style monitor from the chart screenshots is in the same branch. Given how much of it an AI wrote, I did briefly consider calling it bslop:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's a real system monitor (it reads your actual cpu, memory, network and processes), so it's a better test of how this looks on a busy screen than the panes demo. It needs a newer Rust (1. 1 to 4 show and hide the boxes, b and g work the same as in the panes demo, and h or ? lists the rest of the keys. 95) than the rest of Ratatui because of the sysinfo dependency.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i'm not attached to this being the exact solution, but i think it's a problem worth solving, and i'd like it to be more than one terminal's feature (and more than one weekend's worth of yak shaving). If you work on a terminal, would you implement this, and which parts look expensive? If you work on a TUI library or app, which of your widgets would use it, and what would they need that isn't here? Comments are welcome on the Ghostty discussion.

A trio of new Hulu shows to unwind with now that the week is nearly done.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Berdasarkan laporan, we’re well into november now, and as the nights darken and become ever more bitter, i need the comforting warmth of the best streaming services like hulu to get me through this chilly time of year. The three shows I’ve picked out for your streaming pleasure will hopefully keep the winter blues at bay.

Berdasarkan laporan, my first choice is a new reality show. If you’ve ever wondered what “The Traitors” would look like if Janice Soprano was trying to whack everyone as a pretend mob boss as her wannabe celeb gangsters all vie for $250,000, that’s your weekend plans sorted.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, next up is the new korean melodrama. Two very different students tentatively start a relationship, with the killer twist being that most of the action is set in a robotics lab. I don't normally go in for this genre, but the hook is too good to resist here. Who says love can’t bloom when you’re building the next T-1000?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lastly, there’s the second season of the brilliant “the lowdown”. Ethan Hawke’s bumbling journalist returns to unravel a conspiracy theory regarding Tulsa’s prison system. The big new addition this year? That would be Tommy Lee Jones playing Hawke’s charismatic conman poppa.

Diungkapkan bahwa here are three new shows you should definitely add to your hulu watchlist this weekend. Just don’t forget to turn the heating on.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what is it about? a high-stakes reality show that’s basically “the traitors”. With the celebs placed in a luxurious Italian villa, they vye for $250,000 by taking part in games lifted straight from mob movies. Anyhoo, the premise is still fun. y’know, if you swapped out Claudia Winkleman’s iconic fringe for a bunch of ‘celebs’ who are tasked to act like wiseguys. Honestly, I’ve not seen a single one of these ‘famous’ folk in my life before, except host Parker Posey and The Sopranos’ Aida Turturro. A new Don gets picked every week, and it’s up to them if their fellow gangster wannabes get paid or get slayed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sign up to the weekly tom's streaming guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Berdasarkan laporan, why you should watch it: it’s basically a trashy version of “the traitors” with a lot more pasta and mob movie-inspired tasks. Turn off your brain, mentally rewatch “Goodfellas” if you’re getting bored and just enjoy all that gorgeous Italian scenery. If nothing else, it’s great to see Janet Soprano back on TV.

Diungkapkan bahwa what is it about? you know what more romantic dramas really need? robots, baby! set in a university robotics lab, love starts to spark between troubled phd candidate min-jae (choo young woo) and free spirit you-jin (kim so-hyun), who has just transferred in from a clothing and textiles course. That’s quite the career change. Why is Min-Jae so down in the dumps? Before becoming a student of science, he was a professional swimmer whose career ended when he lost his leg. From pro paddler to making robots. Anyway, You-jin eventually gets Min-Jae to open up in this classy Korean melodrama.

Sebagaimana diketahui, why you should watch it: i’m not usually one for melodramas, but the hook of “between steps” is so damn sweet. A couple meets while making things that are basically going to become Terminators in the next few years. Before Arnie destroys their entire lab, just enjoy this sweet drama that really is beautifully shot.

Diungkapkan bahwa why you should watch it: your favorite tulsa-based ‘truthstorian’ is back in season two of this excellent neo-noir comedy crime drama. Traumatized from the events of the first season, where he exposed the crooked Washbergs, Lee ends up making an inebriated speech while receiving a journalistic award, quickly disgracing himself. All should be well for our freelance journalist Lee Raybon (Ethan Hawke), but the poor guy just can’t seem to get out of his own way. Despite his tattered reputation, Raybon ends up getting drawn into a conspiracy theory centering around local penal corruption. Oh, and his estranged dad also turns up out of the blue.

Sebagaimana diketahui, why you should watch it: the script is once again excellent in this left-field crime-centric comedy. Hawke is in his usual stellar form, while the addition of his pop Lee Raybon Snr (Tommy Lee Jones) adds a lot. Playing a former Vietnam vet/turned conman with dementia, the pair’s scenes are must-watch.

#786. Live-migration support in FreeBSD and bhyve coming

📅 13 Nov 2026

Live-migration support in FreeBSD and bhyve coming

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://gyptazy.com/blog/freebsd-bhyve-live-migration-support-rfc/

Diungkapkan bahwa this project presents a first working state for live migration of bhyve guests on freebsd 15. A running amd64 guest can move between two hosts over TCP while continuing to run; it is paused only for the final stop-and-copy phase. 1. The work builds on bhyve's experimental snapshot support and adds dirty-page tracking in the vmm kernel module together with a migration protocol in bhyve and bhyvectl.

I previously discussed the state of bhyve live migration, its historical development, existing limitations, and why it matters for the future of FreeBSD virtualization in my article bhyve on FreeBSD and VM Live Migration – Quo vadis?.

Berdasarkan laporan, the goal is deliberately practical: make it possible to test, discuss, and improve a real implementation rather than discuss live migration only in the abstract. The current code and test tooling are being published as a WIP RFC so that the next steps can be shaped in the open. A more detailed demonstration of a VM being live migrated can be watched on my YouTube channel.

Diungkapkan bahwa live migration is an important building block for enterprise virtualisation. It is also central to the Sylve project, which aims to offer a Proxmox-like virtualisation solution for FreeBSD. It enables host maintenance, hardware replacement, load balancing, and failure-domain management with far less disruption to workloads. Migration is not an optional convenience in that kind of platform; it is one of the capabilities that makes clustered operations practical.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it is equally important for boxybsd, where i offer free bsd-based vps instances to individuals. Without a credible migration path, routine host work can require a guest outage. That makes live migration a current show stopper for the project, and is why this work is being pushed toward a testable, reviewable state.

Diungkapkan bahwa the source starts with a pre-copy phase. Once the remaining dirty set fits the configured downtime target, stops shrinking, or reaches the configured round limit, bhyve pauses the guest and its devices. It sends populated guest memory, then repeatedly obtains a bitmap of pages changed since the previous scan and sends only those pages. It then sends the final dirty pages and the existing snapshot state for the vCPUs, kernel state, and emulated devices.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the destination validates the basic vm geometry, receives memory and state, restores it, and reports that it is ready. The destination does not start the guest if it does not receive that commit message. Before GO, a failed migration can resume the source guest. Only then does the source send GO, the commit point. A warm, stop-and-copy mode is available too, which is useful both as a fallback and as a comparison baseline.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the current two-host test environment, repeated live migrations, memory-rewrite workloads, and fsync-heavy disk workloads have completed successfully. For a slowly dirtying 512 MiB guest, observed downtime has been roughly 138–171 ms. A rapidly dirtying guest may not converge during pre-copy, but still falls back to a correct stop-and-copy completion with a longer pause. These are encouraging engineering results, not a production support promise or a complete correctness proof.

Berdasarkan laporan, the following are neutral engineering requirements, not criticism of the value of the prototype. They need to be addressed first before further upstreaming into FreeBSD can be evaluated responsibly.

Berdasarkan laporan, we have already had deeper discussions about these questions in the sylve discord. Publishing this current state is intended to make those discussions more concrete, bring in wider FreeBSD and bhyve feedback, and turn the prototype into a clear roadmap. The immediate focus is correctness, compatibility validation, transport safety, and repeatable tests—not adding performance features first. Currently, some peopel already have access to it and it's planned ot publish this at least as a proposal on my git and GitHub at:.

Diungkapkan bahwa compression, zero-page elision, broader device coverage, richer orchestration, and performance tuning can follow once the foundation is sound. If you operate bhyve, work on FreeBSD virtualisation, or are interested in Sylve or BoxyBSD, testing the RFC and contributing design feedback would be especially valuable.

Diungkapkan bahwa status: wip rfc for a first working bhyve live-migration implementation on freebsd 15. 1.

Berdasarkan laporan, when it comes to cleaning tasks, i’ve always relied on my trusted white vinegar to come to the rescue. Be it cleaning surface stains or giving my windows a streak-free finish, there are so many uses for white vinegar around the home.

But why exactly are people spraying vinegar on their front doors this season? While your first thought might be to simply clean the surface thoroughly, you’ll be mistaken.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to a university of minnesota extension study, diluted white vinegar can deter pests like ants and spiders from taking refuge in your home. So all of a sudden, layering it on your front door makes sense. Here’s why.

Berdasarkan laporan, it seems like white vinegar can do so much more than cleaning and limescale removal; it also makes a great natural ant and pest repellent. Not only do ants have a highly sensitive sense of smell and can be overwhelmed by the strong vinegar odor, but it can also clean up ant pheromone paths — disrupting them from guiding others toward food and moisture sources.

Sebagaimana diketahui, essentially, spraying white vinegar eliminates the chemical scent trails ants leave behind, helping to prevent an infestation in your home. Which is why it’s a good idea to target potential entryways such as around the front door frame, baseboards, and cracks.

Essentially, spraying white vinegar eliminates the chemical scent trails ants leave behind, helping to prevent an infestation in your home.

Bear in mind that using vinegar is only a short-term fix rather than a long-term deterrent.

Diungkapkan bahwa and this isn’t guaranteed to banish a persistent pest problem or a full infestation. In that case, it’s always best to call a professional local pest control service to handle it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, simply mix equal parts white vinegar and water in a spray bottle to create a mild solution. Then, spray this mixture around your front door, making sure to target any small gaps or crevices where ants might enter. This process helps erase chemical trails left by ants and temporarily interrupts their activity. What’s more, it’s cheap, chemical-free, and only takes seconds to do.

Also, since white vinegar has a high acidity level, take care to protect nearby plants and sensitive surfaces from potential damage.

Diungkapkan bahwa alternatively, experts advise soaking cotton wool balls in peppermint essential oil before putting them around door frames. The strong fragrance will be too overpowering for such pests and will prevent them from entering.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this pure peppermint oil is paraben free, and provides a fresh scent. Versatile to use in aromatherapy, or in an oil or reed diffuser. And while the fragrance is pleasant to our senses, it is also known to be a natural pest repellent.

For more pest tips, be sure to clear this one thing in their yard to prevent rats this fall.

NOTE: Do NOT use peppermint oil if you have pets as this is toxic when inhaled or ingested.

#792. A technical vision for the Haskell ecosystem

📅 13 Nov 2026

A technical vision for the Haskell ecosystem

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://discourse.haskell.org/t/a-technical-vision-for-the-haskell-ecosystem/15078

the technical leadership committee of the Haskell Foundation has been successfully bootstrapped!.

We have spent the last few weeks discussing our vision and strategy and are now fully operational.

Berdasarkan laporan, we’re going to actively develop initiatives and proposals that we believe need funding and execution. For that we need companies, contractors and volunteers to help. Everyone can participate, whether it’s by dropping ideas informally, writing a concrete proposal themselves or finding entities that could support or fund initiatives.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we tried to keep the community proposal process as light as possible. However, we believe that fairness and participation are vital, especially when funding is involved, so anyone who writes a proposal should be aware that we will open the floor for the community to comment or even deliver counter-proposals. The process may evolve as we make experiences and get feedback.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, below is our vision. Feel free to get in touch with us!.

We believe that Haskell is awesome and that it can provide unique value to everyone, because it sits at an interesting intersection between human craftsmanship and machine automation:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there may be better languages for formal verification or for vibecoding, but there’s no better language for “human in the loop”. Haskell is where we maintain control of our work, build institutional knowledge and ship responsibly.

We’re driven to improve Haskell for everyone:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, imagine haskell had the iteration speed of golang, the debugging capabilities of c# and the onboarding experience of rust. And all that while providing stronger guarantees and better performance!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, modern workflows require fast iteration times: compilation, interactive repl, remote dependency caching, ci and test integration. All of this affects both human and machine workflows.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while haskell scales well in terms of code complexity… it doesn’t scale well in terms of build times. As an example, GHC’s own CI has turnaround times of 6 hours. We want to bring them down to 2.

Instead of helplessly dumping logs and binaries into LLM chats, we envision deterministic tools that allow precise and ergonomic enquiries:.

And all of that in your editor/IDE as well as through powerful CLI and scripting interfaces, the latter enabling power users as well as LLM-driven debugging (natively, without requiring any custom adapters like MCP).

Berdasarkan laporan, debugging must be fun again, without littering debug. Trace. trace all over your codebase.

Documentation and interactive exploration will assist newcomers in understanding all caveats of laziness and GHC and should clearly explain how to leverage these tools.

In these times of low frustration tolerance, we are going to build the best onboarding experience in the programming language ecosystem, because it is the ultimate benchmark for developer experience as a whole.

This can only be done if we commit to unix principles, which we summarize as:.

Documentation should be a joy to read, written by humans, for humans.

Berdasarkan laporan, security and trust don’t get established by accident. Once trust is lost, it’s often irrecoverably lost.

To protect our community assets and reputation, we need to:.

Berdasarkan laporan, we should further support attempts to utilize or extend the strengths of the haskell language to boost practical applications of secure design and architecture, such as information flow control or mandatory access control. We’re also monitoring the efforts of dependent types and liquidhaskell.

What if we could compile Haskell software that’s 10 years old with the latest GHC, without any source code changes?.

While this might seem like an impossible goal to achieve… embarking on that journey is going to get us closer to a robust, stable and predictable ecosystem anyway.

The questions we need to answer along the way are:.

Not only requires this investment in GHC and core tooling, but also potentially support community efforts to maintain stable package sets or coordinate ecosystem upgrades, make cabal more ergonomic for complex use cases, spearhead and support stability policies and gather data about what parts of the ecosystem cause churn.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we want haskell to not only be a choice for fast moving startups, but also for large or conservative companies that do not want their workflows or software stacks disrupted. Stability will benefit both of these types of users, reduce cost and friction and build a reputation for Haskell as a modern language with a predictable ecosystem.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, all of the above is an attempt to support the haskell open source ecosystem that we love. We are committed to open source, its values and the social aspect of it. Collaboration is how we engage with and inspire each other.

We want to enable all the maintainers and volunteers who keep this ecosystem alive, many of them unknown, doing their part on a Saturday evening at the other end of the world.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we code because we love to ship products. But we also code, because we want to socialize, meet people and have a good time. We’re committed to both of these values.

Berdasarkan laporan, thank you @hasufell and the tlc for writing this up; it’s very inspiring to see these goals. I think this ambitious agenda will provide us with a lot of fun and profit.

That’s really great to see I’ll be doing my part and see if I can submit a proposal for some unglamorous work I’ve been meaning to do.

Woah, this is so inspiring and motivating! I have multiple features I want to add to HLS!.

Is Haskell Team finally focusing on “Adoption” ?.

Berdasarkan laporan, the kitchenaid artisan plus design series luminaire stand mixer is a special edition stand mixer, and boy does it look like one. The delectable textured blue/gray/beige finish and the crystalline glass bowl are enough to get it in a Taschen coffee table book, and I’m not mad about it. Four attachments, including double-edge flex beater.

Berdasarkan laporan, why you can trust tom's guide our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Berdasarkan laporan, there’s a reason why kitchenaid stand mixers are iconic. Utter the name around a group of bakers, and you’ll elicit a chorus of reverent gasps. Without a shadow of a doubt, the KitchenAid Artisan Tilt-Head stand mixer is the best stand mixer in the world.

But what about the new-for-2026 KitchenAid Artisan Plus Design Series Luminaire stand mixer? Sure it’ll win the award for longest, most superfluous-adjective-d name, but is it also worthy of the best stand mixer crown?.

Diungkapkan bahwa at $699/£899, the luminaire is a pricey, “special edition” stand mixer. Every year, KitchenAid releases a design-forward version of its iconic Artisan Plus, and this year, that’s in the form of the crystalline-glass-bowl, breige (that’s blue, gray, beige) spackled Luminaire. Oh, and it’s got a little light so you can see what you’re mixing (see what you’re missing? No? Just me?). Could this new special edition KitchenAid be the perfect one for you? Find out in this KitchenAid Artisan Plus Design Series Luminaire Stand Mixer review.

Double-edge flex beater, dough hook, whisk, flat beater.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the kitchenaid artisan plus design series luminaire stand mixer is $699 from williams sonoma and £899 from john lewis in the u. K.

Sebagaimana diketahui, to save my fingers, i will henceforth refer to this product as “kitchenaid luminaire”. If you’re wondering why the name is so long, I’ll help break it down for you.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “artisan plus” is how kitchenaid refers to its “artisan plus” line of stand mixers — this includes the iconic kitchenaid artisan plus ($599). This is not the same as the “Artisan” line, which lacks precision speed control, ½ step speed, and an illuminated bowl. “Artisan” models are your standard tilt-head mixers, usually around $499.

Diungkapkan bahwa “design series” is kind of like a special edition. Each year, KitchenAid christens a “Design Series” model — 2022 saw this gorgeous sage-and-copper mixer ($699); 2025 was the “outdoor” theme with a forest-green finish and wooden bowl ($699). 2026 is all about the blue peppercorn/velvet finish (KitchenAid’s words, not mine), and the illuminated bowl.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Sebagaimana diketahui, other artisan plus models rock the same illuminated bowl, but just look at how gorgeous the light is, streaming through the textured glass. It’s almost ecclesiastical.

Berdasarkan laporan, naturally, the design series machines are pricier than the standard artisan plus models ($599). These are special editions, like buying a book with sprayed edges or gold foil, or a supercar in British Racing Green. You’re paying extra for the design aspect. I’m not going to tell you if the elevated design is worth your extra $100 — only you can decide that.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even so, this doesn’t explain or excuse why the luminaire is so outrageously priced in the u. £899 is $1,200. K. K. ? It makes no sense. Why is the mixer double the price in the U. I’d be interested to hear KitchenAid’s explanation.

Diungkapkan bahwa the clue’s in the name, but the kitchenaid luminaire is a design marvel. It’s breathtakingly beautiful. The light refracting through the glass bowl and dappling my countertops is one of the most gorgeous sights I’ve ever seen in my kitchen (the winner being the homemade kimchi I labored over for hours and promptly devoured in ten days).

Sebagaimana diketahui, available in peppercorn blue, the luminaire isn’t glossy like other kitchenaid stand mixers. I thought it would be harder to clean, but I was wrong — more on that in the “Storage & maintenance” section below, though. That’s the whole point of them. While it’s a little frustrating you can’t get this specific model in another shade, this is par for the course for Design Series models. It’s got a spackled, textured finish. They come in one “Design”.

Diungkapkan bahwa there are four attachments: the double-edge flex beater, normal beater, whisk, and dough hook. Each attachment does what it says on the tin — now I’ve used the silicone-lined flex beater, I don’t think I can go back to the standard. Not having to pause mixing to scrape down the sides is a game-changer.

Diungkapkan bahwa like other kitchenaid stand mixers, the attachments click in with a gentle twist and remove just as easily. I washed mine by hand.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, unlike other kitchenaid stand mixers, the luminaire comes with a glass mixing bowl only. Actually, I’m in awe of it. This is obviously to show off the gorgeous light refractions, and I’m not mad about it at all. It’s beautiful.

I have nothing bad to say about the design quality here: it’s a “Design Series” model, and boy, it doesn’t let you forget that.

Berdasarkan laporan, i tested each attachment multiple times, so i’ll go through them one-by-one here. In short, the KitchenAid Luminaire is a premium stand mixer, and it sure as heck performs like one. The speeds range from 20 to 260 RPM, and unlike the standard “Artisan” line, it features stepless adjustment for seamless speed changes.

Berdasarkan laporan, the double-edge flex beater is the best thing to happen to my home baking setup since the sourhouse doughbed. As the name — kind of — suggests, it’s a normal beater attachment with a silicone “flexible” edge. During mixing, these silicone edges scrape down the sides of the bowl without needing to stop and manually scrape.

Berdasarkan laporan, as you can see, there’s an almost windscreen-wiper-like pattern on the bowl. This is where the beater has already scraped down cake batter. Obviously, as the beater moves, it scrapes the remaining batter, and so on and so forth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, now that i've used this attachment, i’m not sure i can go back to the regular beater on my kitchenaid artisan 5qt ($499). The double-edge flex beater is intended for sticky batters, like chocolate cake, banana bread, etcetera.

Berdasarkan laporan, the beater is the standard rounded-triangle-shaped attachment without silicone edges. This can be used for cake batters, muffin mixtures, whipped dips, or even shredding meat. I made some whipped feta dip — using KitchenAid’s recipe — and shredded chicken.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i was a little frustrated when i had to stop mixing and scrape down the edges multiple times, but this is expected with the standard beater attachment. I like that this attachment can be a little gentler than the double-edge version, particularly helpful when I shredded a whole chicken. The resulting texture was a touch too mushy for my preferences, but it turned an entire chicken into small shreds in about thirty seconds.

Diungkapkan bahwa as you can see, the egg texture is even and glossy, with an airy, thick texture. I baked this mixture in my air fryer (as my oven is garbage), which I think was the problem — but, again, this is my fault, not the Luminaire’s.

The mixer can be adjusted from slow to 260RPM seamlessly, ideal for technical bakes like meringue, where you need to change the speed while adding sugar.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i made kitchenaid’s “everyday bread” recipe to test the dough hook. You shouldn’t mix yeasted doughs faster than speed 2, as it can overwork the yeast and cause a flat loaf.

Berdasarkan laporan, as you can see, the dough hook took everything i threw at it. It blended the dough perfectly and kneaded it gently, saving my forearms. I have no issues with this at all — the dough hook is the ideal baker's assistant.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the u. S. Yep, I’m grimacing, too. , the KitchenAid Luminaire boasts a 5-year warranty and 15-year repairability; in the U. $699 for a one-year warranty is pretty bad. K. , this decreases to just one year. KitchenAid, what’s going on across the pond?.

Diungkapkan bahwa disappointing warranty aside, the kitchenaid luminaire is easy to clean and maintain. It’s just as big and heavy as other KitchenAid stand mixers, which means it’s made of real metals and holds a high-quality motor, but if you’re only as strong as a sick Victorian child (like me), you’ll need help getting it out and putting it away.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i found cleaning the glass mixing bowl just as easy as cleaning any other bowl — ditto with the mixing attachments. Top marks all around here (well, U. S. warranty aside… yeesh!) Maybe that U. K. warranty is what you’re paying for? (£899 is $1,200…).

Sebagaimana diketahui, would i buy the kitchenaid luminaire? no. I’m sorry, but I can barely afford to heat my house. K. I live in the U. , where it’s an abhorrent £899. I’m not going to drop almost a grand on a stand mixer.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, should you buy the kitchenaid luminaire? if you’ve got enough money, yes. Without a doubt. And that light? Monumentally helpful. It performs admirably at every task you throw at it, whether that’s shredding chicken or making ten-tiered cakes. Oh, and don’t get me started on the mesmerizing lace-like patterns stretching across my kitchen countertops… we’d be here all day.

Berdasarkan laporan, for baking enthusiasts, this is a no-brainer. The KitchenAid Luminaire will not let you down. I’ll be watching from afar with my face pushed up against the glass, a wistful tear trickling down my cheek.

#795. Minnesota guitarist's "palmfrets" invention strikes a new chord

📅 12 Nov 2026

Minnesota guitarist's "palmfrets" invention strikes a new chord

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.echopress.com/business/minnesota-guitarists-invention-strikes-a-new-chord

Berdasarkan laporan, fergus falls — the back room of stella’s restaurant in fergus falls filled with people on oct. 28, all there to see musician Ben Ranson play.

Berdasarkan laporan, ranson, who grew up in sebeka, minnesota, and currently lives in sandstone, is a regular performer at venues across the region, including in fergus falls. But Oct. 28 was no ordinary gig. That night, Ranson revealed something he’d been working on for years.

Berdasarkan laporan, it wasn’t a new song or a clever guitar lick, it was an invention called “palmfrets” — something ranson believes could change the way guitarists use their instrument. It allows players to play new bass lines or melodies using their palm, a special set of frets called palmfrets and a technique called palmfretting.

The idea for palmfrets came to Ranson over five years ago.

Ranson had already been doing musical experiments — even constructing organ-like foot pedals and learning the seven string guitar — all in a quest to get more notes out of the guitar, specifically more bass notes.

Diungkapkan bahwa he said the reason behind the invention, initially, was entirely artistic. He wasn’t thinking much about developing a commercial product.

Berdasarkan laporan, “that was not on my mind at all,” ranson said. “And it wasn’t really until I made one that really worked that it sort of dawned on me like, oh, this is something that people are really going to want. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, ranson made an early-stage version of the invention in his garage, and said that, at first, he didn't recognize the importance of what he had created. He set it aside and left it in a corner for awhile — years, even.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eventually, he returned to his forgotten creation. It was then that he began to hear the music.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he drafted his ideas and designs on paper, and enlisted the help of engineers. Together, they created new prototypes made from 3D printed plastic and laser-cut metal parts.

It was during that time when Ranson said something shifted.

Berdasarkan laporan, ranson knew the plastic and metal version was not practical, and only lasted a matter of weeks. But it worked, and from there, Ranson said the engineering became more serious.

Diungkapkan bahwa serious enough that ranson applied for a patent, which he received on oct. 6, 2026.

Ranson had an inkling that this was something special, and recalled the first time he started playing the guitar with a solid prototype.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i was like, ‘i’m doing things that chet atkins never did,’” he joked. “I just had this sort of realization, like, other people are going to want to do this. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, fast forward to oct. 28 in Fergus Falls, and Ranson’s invention is now in the hands of other guitar players.

Berdasarkan laporan, using the pisiform bone — a small, pea-shaped bone in the wrist, near the bottom of the palm — players depress a string on the palmfret, an extra fret or set of frets near the wrist of the picking hand. The player can then use the thumb of their picking hand to pluck the string fretted by the pisiform bone.

This frees up the fretting hand — the hand which frets strings on the neck of the guitar — meaning the player can move up and down the fret board more freely, and fret other strings because the pisiform bone is doing some of the hard work.

“So if you want to, you can move (the fretting hand) anywhere you want, play any other notes that you want to play,” said Ranson.

Essentially, guitarists could play a bass line with their pisiform bone and play other melodies or chords that would have otherwise been, literally, out of reach.

Ranson had some rules when designing palmfrets.

“One of the basic principles in inventing it has been: if it interferes with the normal way that you would play the guitar, it’s no good,” he said.

Diungkapkan bahwa “so the basic principle is you have to keep all of the function of the guitar as people know it,” he explained. “It has to add, but it can’t take away. That’s the basic principle. ”.

Still, adding another element to the guitar introduces a learning curve, even for players as skilled as Ranson.

He gave proof of the learning curve by showing a callus on his pisofone bone — a callus reminiscent of the ones beginning guitarists get on their fingers when first learning to play — and compared his skill-level with the palmfrets to being a teenager playing in their first band and only knowing six songs.

Diungkapkan bahwa “that is the stage i am at now, frankly. ”.

During the reveal, other guitar players tested out the palmfrets, taking turns passing around acoustic guitars, electric, and even the bass.

Sebagaimana diketahui, darren quam, a musician from battle lake, who was in attendance on oct. 28, tried his hand — or palm — at the new invention.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “at first, you know, it took me a second to kind of understand how you could use it,” quam said. “But then — especially when Ben had us come up and try it — then, you know, trying it with my own hands, I was like, okay, I see how this could be very useful in certain situations. ”.

Quam also commented on the learning curve.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it’s not a whole new instrument, but it’s a whole new way of playing. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, despite the new way of playing, during the reveal show, quam seemed to catch on quickly, with ranson joking “we’re going to have to take this away from you. ”.

From a practical standpoint as a gigging musician, Quam thought the invention would be useful for solo players.

“I think it really is probably the most useful in like a solo situation where you’re playing and you can accompany yourself, especially with those lower notes where you can fret with your palm hand and change the root note or the chords, and still be able to have the freedom to play on the higher strings as if there was someone else accompanying you, you know, like a bass player.

Diungkapkan bahwa “so it’s kind of like you’ve got a bass player on your palm all of a sudden. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and speaking of bass players, ranson believes the bass guitar, as it now is, could become “obsolete. ”.

“But for a great reason, as far as bassists are concerned,” he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with the palmfrets, a bass player could play a bass line beneath a bass line, or play chords while playing a bass line. Meaning a bass player could accompany themselves, or add chords when playing with a group.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “as a guitarist, you might want to play some jazz song, or whatever song you want — it’s got a clear melody, but you just need to have chords underneath it so that people can understand what that melody is. ”.

With palmfrets, the bass player can play the chord and the bass line, rooting the listener, while allowing the lead guitarist to focus on the melody.

Diungkapkan bahwa ranson explained that he expects the invention to make the bass into a very powerful instrument, “kind of like a piano. ”.

For Ranson, thinking about how the invention will be used in the future is all speculation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “but i think it’s going to be really interesting. I mean, I can’t wait,” said Ranson.

The true potential of the invention, according to Ranson, might not be revealed for many years.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “let’s say 15 years from now, there’s going to be some kid who got one of these as a teenager. Then you’ll know what it can do. ”.

AI unlocks Gödel's notebooks, said to contain hundreds of proved theorems

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/nov/13/kurt-godel-notebooks-ai-helps-unlock-hidden-discoveries-man-who-transformed-maths

Kurt Gödel left 1,009 pages of densely written text – much of it in an obsolete shorthand – which is now said to contain hundreds of proved theorems.

Berdasarkan laporan, the austrian logician kurt gödel was one of the most original thinkers of the 20th century. His two incompleteness theorems, published in 1931, transformed mathematics and paved the way for the digital age.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after his seminal results of the 1930s, gödel published only a few papers. His unpublished work, however, runs to tens of thousands of pages, and is of great interest to historians of science.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, since 2017, the finnish logician jan von plato has led a project at helsinki university to understand the contents of 16 notebooks that gödel wrote in the early 1940s. This material – the “workbooks” – is 1,009 pages of densely written text about maths and logic. Much of it is written in a German shorthand, Gabelsberger, that was obsolete even when Gödel was using it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, progress in the mathematical understanding of the text was painfully slow – about a page a week – until september, when von plato enlisted the help of the ai model claude. Within a couple of days, Claude had provided a comprehensive digest of the entire material, revealing Gödel had proved hundreds of theorems that no one knew about.

The most famous logician of modern times had, in fact, discovered significantly more than anyone had thought.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i was flabbergasted,” said von plato. Gödel was far ahead of his time. “The workbooks not only contain dozens of anticipations of results not known until the 70s and 80s, but they also contain 14 themes in logic that have not been pursued. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, gödel changed the course of logic because he revealed the limits of mathematical knowledge. His incompleteness theorems show that in all mathematical systems there are true statements that can neither be proved or disproved. Yet while this result was a blow to previous generations of logicians, who had hoped that all truths were verifiable, Gödel’s work pushed the field in new directions, inspiring Alan Turing to write his 1936 paper that began the theory of modern computation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 1940, gödel fled austria under the nazis. He settled in Princeton, New Jersey, and became a close friend of Albert Einstein at the Institute of Advanced Study. Increasingly paranoid in his later years, he refused to eat food that was not cooked by his wife, and died of starvation in 1978.

Berdasarkan laporan, von plato said he had started his gödel project in 2017 because he was facing mandatory retirement from helsinki university. 5m (£2. “What should I do to make myself indispensable? Oh yes, I’ll start reading Gödel’s enigmatic shorthand pages!” He received a €2. 1m) grant from the European Research Council, taught himself Gabelsberger shorthand – “I am one of only six people who can read it in the world” – and assembled a small team.

Berdasarkan laporan, in august, at a conference in france about ai and theorem proving, von plato met computer scientists who suggested that he co-opt the help of claude in trying to make sense of the workbooks. On his return to Helsinki he began the process, showing Claude his transcriptions of the workbooks, as well as six books he had previously written on Gödel and other secondary scientific literature.

Diungkapkan bahwa “in a couple of days, i got to see a 650-page explanation of the workbooks. It had to be controlled page for page, but it’s basically a work that is impossible to do for human beings,” he said. “Humans read one page at a time and we tend to forget things. It takes us a year to read about 50 pages. We just are not able to keep in mind all the different parts.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the ai can connect all the pieces in a thousand pages. It can see all of Gödel’s writings as one piece. ”.

The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment.

Berdasarkan laporan, gödel’s incompleteness theorems revealed the existence of statements whose truths were independent of the system they were written in: that is, they could not be proved or disproved within the system. In 1966, the American mathematician Paul Cohen won the Fields medal, the highest honour in maths, for showing the independence of two well-known mathematical statements: the continuum hypothesis and the axiom of choice.

Diungkapkan bahwa gödel reacted to cohen’s fields medal by saying that he had already proved the result in the 1940s. Yet when pushed for a proof by his peers, Gödel was unable to reconstruct one from his notes.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first task von plato set claude was to discover if gödel’s workbooks had a proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, which would reveal that gödel had been telling the truth in 1966. “He was just one step away,” said von Plato. For me, the architecture of his proof is just wonderful. The answer came back: yes, almost. “There’s one definition that Gödel got wrong, but he had the right definition two years earlier, and so the thought is that he would have arrived at the right definition anyway if he had just continued for a few months. It makes all of these results of set theory follow a uniform pattern.

Diungkapkan bahwa “what strikes me especially is that he starts from ideas. Step after step he goes ahead and he manages to fulfil the aims that he has in this formal work. He has very, very clear ideas, and then he’s methodical. He’s not like someone who plays with formulas and hopes to arrive somewhere. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa von plato said that when claude presented him with the reconstructed proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, he ran it through the proof assistant coq, a program that verifies the validity of mathematical proofs, and it passed. Von Plato believes that had Gödel published his work on the axiom of choice, he would have won the 1940 Fields medal. “Maybe he felt that when Cohen got the medal, that that was something he sort of missed. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in further discussions with claude, von plato asked the ai model to extract all theorems in the workbooks for which gödel either had a proof, had sketched a proof or had an idea for a proof. When these results were put into Coq: “About 400 were verified as stated, about 200 were repaired, meaning that perhaps the statement of the theorem had to be made more precise, or some assumption had to be added. Gödel himself, when rereading his notes, would occasionally add a marginal remark: falsch! [incorrect] or schlecht! [bad]. About 50 were false, and this is no wonder. Claude found 663. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, von plato added: “i am sure that the continued study of gödel’s manuscripts will reveal further treasures. The workbooks contain, Claude says, more than a dozen themes in logic and foundations of mathematics that have not been found in the 80-plus years since they were written down. So this is one thing to explore. But there are many others. His physics and cosmology notebooks are an unknown territory I plan to start exploring once I am finished with my present logic projects. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, joel david hamkins, a professor of logic at the university of notre dame, indiana, has not seen claude’s reconstruction of gödel’s proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, but said that if it stood up “it is remarkable and historically interesting. Although how much is Claude and how much is Gödel is a job for the historians. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, hamkins said: “the fact that there are things in there that resemble [cohen’s proof] does not mean he had it. But Gödel had so many ground-breaking ideas that it is maybe not surprising that his notebooks are full of exciting things. You don’t get credit for work you don’t tell anyone about. It shows he was on the path. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, lonewolf is still pre-1. 0 and runs as a single node. Full XMPP compliance and clustering are on the roadmap.

Diungkapkan bahwa your users can now exchange messages, presence, iqs, and roster subscriptions with people on other xmpp servers. If a host has a certificate and a public DNS name, federation is on by default, with nothing extra to configure.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lonewolf authenticates peers by certificate only. The other server needs a trusted certificate and SASL EXTERNAL support. We don't support Server Dialback.

Diungkapkan bahwa when the other server supports it, both directions share a single connection (xep-0288). Servers also tell each other their stanza size and idle limits up front (XEP-0478).

Berdasarkan laporan, federation checks certificate revocation lists published by the ca, fetched over plain http. tls. fetch_crls = false, or point s2s. tls. If a CRL can't be downloaded, the connection goes ahead anyway. You can turn downloads off with s2s. crls_path at a local file to use only that.

Sebagaimana diketahui, clients and servers can now connect with tls from the first byte (xep-0368), using new dedicated listeners. Outbound federation discovers both STARTTLS and direct TLS endpoints.

Sebagaimana diketahui, use letsencrypt. certificate_profile to pick one of the profiles your CA advertises, including short-lived certificates. If you change the profile, Lonewolf renews early so the new one takes effect right away.

Berdasarkan laporan, you can now enable scram-sha-512 and scram-sha-512-plus. Be aware that they come from an expired Internet-Draft, not an RFC, and aren't registered with IANA.

Berdasarkan laporan, even if you leave sha-512 login disabled, new accounts and password changes now store credentials that v0. 2. 0 can't read, so rolling back isn't straightforward.

#802. No AI Slop: A Manifesto

No AI Slop: A Manifesto

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slopmanifesto.com/

Written by the speakers and attendees of AIE Code Summit 2026.

In 2001, 17 software engineers and leaders got together at a ski lodge in Snowbird, Utah to understand the biggest challenge of their time: heavyweight, documentation-driven software development processes.

Out of this we got the Agile Manifesto, four values and twelve principles that changed how most of the industry builds software.

Today we convene to build our own manifesto - the No AI Slop manifesto.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ai increasingly helps us write our code, docs, plans, and messages. We've all been on the receiving end of slop, and most of us have sent some too. Through this work, we have come to value:.

Our own thinking over a model's first draft.

Improving the system over patching the output.

The world moves especially fast these days, but the goal of these resolutions is to embrace our important human role in harnessing AI safely, responsibly, in a way that creates value for everyone, and that will be relevant for years to come.

Again, the world moves especially fast these days, but the goal of these resolutions is to embrace our important human role in harnessing AI safely, responsibly, in a way that creates value for everyone, and that will be relevant for years to come.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we look forward to working with the community to evolve these beliefs as the world changes. Comments and feedback on this document are welcome. What is slop? Why does slop happen? Why is slop worth fighting? How do we fight slop?.

Diungkapkan bahwa cern’s large hadron collider (lhc) uses extremely strong magnets to collide particles at nearly the speed of light, breaking them up into smaller components for study. (The phrase “high luminosity” refers to the increased number of particle collisions. ) CERN’s goal is to achieve between 140 and 200 particle collisions 40 million times per second in each experiment in order to increase their chances of observing rare particles or phenomena. They are currently working on upgrading the LHC for upcoming experiments scheduled to begin after 2030. The new iteration of the particle collider, called the High-Luminosity LHC, will slam more particles together than before. To succeed, the collider will need extremely compact and high-quality magnets.

In a study published 24 September in IEEE Transactions on Applied Superconductivity, researchers outline their journey to manufacture these next-generation magnets for the LHC, which require new materials and manufacturing techniques.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the collider’s current dipole magnets contain coils made of niobium and titanium (nbti) and can achieve strengths of 8. 3 tesla. That is about 166,000 times as strong as Earth’s magnetic field. However, this magnetic force is the upper limit of what NbTi coils can achieve. For the LHC’s new quadrupole magnets, scientists are creating coils made of niobium and tin (Nb₃Sn), which will yield just under 12 T.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, susana izquierdo bermúdez, a magnet engineer at cern who leads a team of about 60 people, has been involved in the development of these magnets since 2012. Over the years, she has contributed to many different aspects of the project, including early winding tests, electromagnetic design, mechanical design, manufacturing, and testing.

Diungkapkan bahwa izquierdo bermúdez notes that while nbti is ductile and can be wound after the superconducting compound has been formed, nb₃sn is brittle and cannot tolerate the large strains involved in coil winding. For this reason, the magnets are produced using a process known as wind-and-react: The cable is first wound into its final coil geometry, and the Nb₃Sn superconducting phase is formed only afterwards through a high-temperature heat treatment.

Berdasarkan laporan, to start, the team takes a 760-meter-long cable composed of strands of niobium and tin and wraps it around a center pole to form a coil about 7. 2 meters long with a 150 millimeter aperture.

Berdasarkan laporan, once wound, the coil undergoes a controlled heat treatment in an inert atmosphere. The temperature is increased over time, plateauing at about 210 °C and then 400 °C before peaking at about 650 °C. During this process, which takes several days, the niobium and tin in the strands react to form the brittle Nb₃Sn superconducting phase.

“After reaction, the coil must be handled very carefully because excessive deformation could damage the brittle superconducting material,” Izquierdo Bermúdez explains.

The coils are then smoothed over with a liquid epoxy resin, which fills any internal voids, cracks, or gaps, and finally is cured into a rigid polymer.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in their study, izquierdo bermúdez and her colleagues outline their efforts to manufacture more than 120 coils for 4. 2-meter-long magnets for the LHC. 5-meter-long magnets and more than 70 coils for 7. Four coils are incorporated into each quadrupole magnet.

Berdasarkan laporan, in total, the team produced 250 coils, 25 of which failed either due to human error or challenges in the manufacturing process that left the coils with subpar electrical or mechanical properties. Izquierdo Bermúdez says that even the smallest imperfection can compromise a coil. In one instance, a coil had to be discarded because a single metal particle trapped between the coil and one of its protective components was suspected of interfering with its performance.

Diungkapkan bahwa in september, izquierdo bermúdez’s team finished running quality control tests on the 7. 3 T. 2-meter magnets for CERN, confirming they reached peak magnetic forces of 11. The magnets are functioning well, and the team is now working to manufacture back-ups.

Sebagaimana diketahui, izquierdo bermúdez says that it is a great honor and responsibility to be a part of this work, which has been a large team effort. “It has taken many years of work by a large international team, from conductor and magnet development through manufacturing, testing and final integration. Seeing the technology reach this stage is something we can all be very proud of,” she says.

This story was updated on 10 November 2026 to correct the total number of particle collisions in each experiment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, michelle hampson is a freelance writer based in halifax. She frequently contributes to Spectrum's Journal Watch coverage, which highlights newsworthy studies published in IEEE journals.

That's some really painstaking manufacturing! I wonder what other experiments and, eventually, commercial uses we'll find for magnetic coils so precise and powerful.

Sebagaimana diketahui, openai has disbanded its stand-alone robotics team, moving its researchers onto other teams. The company confirmed the reorganization when asked about it by Fortune. The change came recently enough that OpenAI had already registered a booth at CoRL, a top academic robotics conference in Austin, this week. A company spokesperson said that robotics remains a core part of OpenAI’s long-term vision and portrayed the reorganization as a sign of the company’s commitment to robotics, rather than a retreat from it. OpenAI said it has reassigned its robotics research team to the company’s main research team, reporting to Chief Research Officer Mark Chen, while the applied robotics and hardware teams have been reassigned to the company’s larger Applied organization, which reports to OpenAI President Greg Brockman. Though the conference app and floor plan marked OpenAI’s spot, when Fortune visited booth #208, it sat empty with OpenAI’s logo nowhere to be seen.

Diungkapkan bahwa openai had a robotics team in its early days but wound it down in 2020, with cofounder wojciech zaremba later citing limited robot data and a more efficient path toward artificial general intelligence (agi)—the human-like ai that has been openai’s goal since its founding—through other methods. OpenAI seemed to confirm this view in its response to Fortune. It said that at the start of the year, the company’s researchers assumed the best way to make progress on robotics was to build on its work on AI models such as Sora, a video generation model that, in order to create realistic videos, had to have some implicit understanding of how the physical world works. The company spokesperson said that despite the reorganization, OpenAI remains committed to bringing general-purpose robots into the world. OpenAI rebuilt a stand alone robotics team in 2024, announcing a partnership with the startup Figure to develop AI models for humanoid robots. This discovery is what motivated OpenAI to disband the stand alone robotics team and move the affiliated researchers onto teams working on more general AI models. Last year, Altman told the company that it needed to abandon “side quests,” and the company has jettisoned some efforts—including Sora—in order to reallocate computing resources to more core and potentially-profitable endeavors. The reorganization also comes at a time when OpenAI is under pressure to rein in its costs and show that it is more focused on a few, core products. The company is under pressure to stanch its heavy operating losses—which reportedly totaled $10. OpenAI has said it is currently developing its own humanoid robot, with CEO Sam Altman targeting a first public demonstration in 2027. But since then, the company spokesperson said, the company’s general-purpose frontier models, including GPT-6 Astra, have shown that can be directly applied to robotics. This would obviate the need to have separate robotics teams building specialized AI models just to be the digital “brains” for robots. ” Instead, he said, they likely see robotics as a challenge that can be addressed as a downstream application of general intelligence—similar to the way the same underlying frontier AI models now power specialized coding tools, or tools for legal or financial work. That partnership ended in February 2025, when Figure said it would develop its own robot AI. Guanya Shi, an assistant professor at Carnegie Mellon University’s Robotics Institute, reacted to the change at OpenAI, telling Fortune that he would interpret the move as a signal that OpenAI sees robotics as “no longer a special problem. This is the approach that eventually yielded the company’s breakthrough product ChatGPT in late 2022. In particular, OpenAI became increasingly devoted to training ultra-large language models on vast datasets of human-written text. The reorganization reflects a bet that is gaining traction across the AI industry: that general-purpose models built for language, code, and vision can also be used for “embodied AI”—where AI models control devices that can act in the physical world, such as robots, driverless cars, or drones. Researchers have seen surprising performance when connecting GPT-6 Astra to robots, directly using the general-purpose AI model to perform some robotic tasks. 9 billion in the most recent quarter—as it seeks to close a new funding round and prepares for a possible IPO in early 2027.

This line of thinking—that general AI models can be applied directly to controlling robots without the need to create specialized models with “spatial intelligence”—would seem to challenge the assumptions underpinning many of today’s robotics startups, which have raised billions on the premise that robots need brains of their own.

Diungkapkan bahwa but russ tedrake, an mit professor and cofounder and ceo of walden robotics, said robotics companies still have an advantage the ai labs don’t: their robots are already gaining work experience in real places, such as on factory floors. Such “deployment” experience—and the data these robots gather—helps robots adapt to specific workplaces and tasks. Better foundational models make that site-specific data more valuable because robots can learn from it faster, Tedrake said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, recent experiments have tested how much work a general-purpose model can do without specialized training on robotic data. Researchers gave Astra camera images, robot information and a control interface that allowed the model to command the robot to take certain actions. In an Nvidia study, an Astra-powered agent achieved a 74. 8% success rate on a simulated manipulation benchmark—where the model commands a simulated robot in a digital simulation, as opposed to a real robot—compared with 51. 0% reported by the best specialized robotic models on this leaderboard.

Sebagaimana diketahui, shi said advances in general models’ spatial and reasoning capabilities already let them handle tasks that previously required dedicated training. They can cope when a bottle is in a different position or the lighting changes, and reason about the sequence of a task or which step went wrong, he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, meanwhile, large language models are powerful but slow and need to be hosted in the cloud, meaning the robot or device needs a constant network connection. Shi still sees a need for smaller, specialized models that can run on a robot’s onboard computer without needing a constant internet connection.

Diungkapkan bahwa “there may be different starting points for how to grow intelligence,” pete florence, cofounder of generalist, a startup training general-purpose ai models for robots, told fortune. He said it was unclear that any existing model would be the one that dominates robotics in the long-run. For its part, OpenAI said it was reassigning its robotics researchers to other teams because it now believes this is the best way to accelerate progress towards building general-purpose robots.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, back at booth #208 at corl, a few former members of the once-unified, stand-alone openai robotics team milled about. They still drew a crowd, despite having no display or demo. After all, one of the conference’s hottest questions was how much robotics expertise would remain valuable as general-purpose models grew more capable—and the experience of those former OpenAI robotics researchers, now dispatched to other teams, offered one answer. Wen Shao is a reporting fellow at Fortune covering AI, with a focus on the companies, economics, and infrastructure shaping the industry.

Concurrent Shell Command Queues

Tanggal: 06 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://emmer.dev/blog/concurrent-shell-command-queues/

How to run shell commands in parallel while limiting their concurrency.

Berdasarkan laporan, i had a use case recently where i wanted to speed up some bash processing that i was doing, but still keep concurrency constrained. So I wondered: is there a straightforward way to create thread pools in Bash? The answer is: yes, but it takes some work to be semi-resilient and portable.

Berdasarkan laporan, you may ask: why do this in bash at all? it seems silly to use a language with poor concurrency controls. You'd be right to ask this question, and my answer is: because I have a fondness for Bash, and I wanted the challenge. But you're still probably better off using another language, such as Python.

Berdasarkan laporan, here is code that creates a command queue that accepts shell commands to execute. You do not need to know all the commands that you want executed up-front, you can submit commands to it over time.

Diungkapkan bahwa queue_start initializes the queue (managed by mkfifo) and starts the executor (concurrency managed by xargs -p), queue_submit submits commands to the queue, and queue_wait waits for the queue to drain before cleaning up. Calling queue_wait is optional, command processing will start as soon as you queue it with queue_submit.

Berdasarkan laporan, you can copy and paste this code into a script, or it's also safe to put in your dotfiles, as it only sets some of the exit traps for interactive shells. It works in Bash and Zsh, and it has as much defensive programming as I know how to add, but I'm confident it has failure modes that are difficult to predict or avoid.

My original use case had to do with making a large number of web requests, so here's an example using Postman Echo :.

A more deterministic scenario demonstrating that concurrency is respected, only starting command three after command two has completed:.

Command queues are inherited by subshells:.

Different subshells can have their own command queue:.

Queueing each line of a command's output as a command to execute:.

Queueing each line of a file as a command:.

Here are some reasons why you might just want a different programming language:.

Berdasarkan laporan, the amount of additional code needed to support multiple is complicated and likely isn't needed in most cases. Subshells can still have their own queues.

Command output is intentionally not streamed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this prevents interleaving the output of most commands. Output larger than PIPE_BUF may still get interleaved.

Diungkapkan bahwa queue_wait doesn't return a value indicating any job failure. **.

This would require a temporary file or a second file descriptor and some complicated code.

queue_wait has to wait for running processes started after queue_start.

Processes started after queue_start will inherit the queue write file descriptor (which is what allows subshells to work), and xargs won't see the end of the queue until every copy of the write descriptor is closed.

_queue_stop indiscriminately terminates descendants.

Any other backgrounded jobs will be terminated, including ones started before queue_start.

Microsoft 365 services are slowly recovering from a prolonged outage that has handed critics of single-vendor dependence a particularly unwelcome case study.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ever wondered what it would be like if your it supplier abruptly pulled the plug? perhaps the result of a mood swing by an unpredictable political leader? for affected microsoft customers, the disruption has offered an unwelcome preview. Email? Gone. Messaging with Teams? Iffy. Collaboration? Nope.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the list of problems in what microsoft delicately called a "service degradation" is breathtaking. Copilot threw a wobbly. The company put the incident's start at 1826 GMT on November 12. Viewing recently used files in the Microsoft 365 application was problematic. Exchange Online fell over. Microsoft 365 Education was affected (unfortunate, considering the changes the company has made), and so on.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at 1401 gmt on november 13, microsoft reported: "we're continuing to see improvements in service availability," but the damage has surely been done. If the outage halted work at your organization, then questions will have to be asked.

Even Microsoft's rivals had some sympathy for the engineers and administrators dealing with the problems.

Sebagaimana diketahui, jos poortvliet, co-founder of nextcloud, told the register: "mistakes happen in the it industry. This holds true for companies of all sizes, including us. Our heart goes out to all the admins today.

Berdasarkan laporan, "this incident shows how dependent organizations are on a single ecosystem. Especially in critical infrastructure, monopolies are increasing the risk of stalling businesses globally if an incident occurs.

Diungkapkan bahwa "when everything is hanging on a single vendor, companies can't switch providers quickly to get back up and running, or have a second setup as backup, or pull the plug when under attack and keep working air-gapped. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, similarly, civo ceo mark boost noted that it whoopsies were a way of life. "The real concern isn't that Microsoft has suffered an outage. It's that we've allowed so much of our critical infrastructure to become concentrated in the hands of so few companies, creating enormous single points of failure. "Every technology provider will experience failures," he said. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, dame chi onwurah, chair of the commons science and technology committee, also commented: "the global microsoft outage only serves to highlight once again the lack of resilience in the uk's digital infrastructure, and the dangers that this dependency can pose to our security, economy and public services. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, this week, microsoft warned users to treat its unsupported exchange server 2016 and 2019 as "permanently vulnerable.
