This happens often with information that’s puzzling or offensive, and which, if published, would upset the subject and his admirers. Easy. “He’s as good as it gets,” he told Charlie Rose. He loved Bellow, “but I grew up on Roth,” whose books “meant and mean everything to me. (“If that had been available to us…we would have published it straight through. ”) In an interview, Remnick was asked for his dessert island author: Roth, Bellow, or Updike. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2013, remnick attended roth’s 80th birthday celebration at the newark museum. ” After tributes by Edna O’Brien and Jonathan Lethem, the elderly Roth read confidently from Sabbath’s Theater. The following day, he recalled “the most astonishing literary performance I’ve ever witnessed. (“These were not his last words—please, not that!”) It was, for Remnick, an iconic moment—“a triumphal lope around the bases, like Ted Williams did on his last day in a Red Sox uniform. Remnick was transfixed. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, after the evening ended with birthday cake and champagne toast, remnick rushed home to write. “I saw and heard something remarkable just a few hours ago, something I’m not likely to forget until all the mechanisms of remembering are shot and I’m tucked away for good. Appearing on newyorker. com the next day, his article had the zest and lyricism of deadline writing mixed with teenage wonder. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa five years later, roth was tucked away for good, felled by heart disease. “But whom would he talk to up there? He had never found a goy yet who could talk fast enough for him. ” A serious problem, given how long eternity could last. Eventually, Roth chose Bard College’s cemetery, where he had Hannah Arendt for company, and chose to be buried next to the eventual grave-site of his very-much-alive friend, the Romanian writer Norman Manea, so that he and Norman could “continue their conversations. He had prolonged his life through swimming, an abstemious diet, and numerous cardiac stents, but the end came swiftly. In Sabbath’s Theater, the rowdy hero considers burial in the quiet country. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa at roth’s funeral, a close circle of friends, including remnick, watched his coffin lowered into the ground. “Where was the rawness and the mess? Where was the embarrassment and the shame?” A few places, actually, but not newyorker. Later that week, Roth received a hero’s farewell in the New Yorker. Remnick was struck by the austere, secular service (“no Kaddish, no God, no speeches”). In The Counterlife, Roth mocked pious, fulsome eulogies. com, where nearly a dozen grateful tributes appeared.

Sebagaimana diketahui, remnick added his own eulogy. Here again was Roth as literary ascetic, “living alone in the woods,” shunning modern blandishments. In the literary pantheon, he ranked with Hemingway, Bellow, and Melville—“but he was funnier, more spontaneous, than any of them. The Roth he remembered was indomitable (“Roth’s vitality never dwindled, particularly on the page”). ” In Remnick’s eulogy, Roth acquired a purity, a saintliness. He was a survivor who, after illness and divorce, “redoubled his sense of discipline and set himself free. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, roth’s life had ended, but his afterlife was just beginning. (“I didn’t think the friendship would survive,” Thurman said. According to Remnick, “Roth long resisted the idea of a biography,” then finally “relented. “And I didn’t think I would survive. ” In fact, Roth courted biographers, seeking a loyal, sympathetic Boswell, but every candidate, including Judith Thurman, had demurred. ”) Later, Roth enlisted Ross Miller, his closest friend, but after two failed attempts, Roth gave up.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, around 2010, with time scarce, roth made his final, fateful selection. “He doesn’t judge his protagonist,” Roth said after reading Bailey’s biography of John Cheever. Could he understand Jewishness? Or working class Newark? Roth didn’t much care. To many, Blake Bailey seemed a strange choice: a midwest Gentile with a slick, to-the-manor-born mien. “That is the kind of moral latitude I need in a biography. ” It was that approach, and his just-us-guys bonhomie, that won Roth’s favor.

Berdasarkan laporan, biography has several tasks. In so doing, it often complicates our feelings toward our heroes. In chronicling a life, it locates patterns, teases out meanings, and reveals someone’s layers, their human flaws. Such was the fate awaiting Roth’s readers when Philip Roth: The Biography arrived.

Diungkapkan bahwa how would roth’s admirers react? bailey, to his credit, didn’t ignore roth’s darker side. He gives us Roth’s lechery (“I was forty and she was nineteen. Perfect”) and general selfishness with women. ) To balance the moral scales, Bailey emphasized Roth’s generosity and loyalty. (“A mature woman wouldn’t take your shit,” Roth’s therapist says. In short, we get all of it: Roth’s anger, selfishness, and compulsive womanizing, but also his warmth, generosity, and menschlicheit.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, remnick’s review, which ran that april, and read like a mini-biography, struck a similar balance. It didn’t attempt to untangle Roth’s contradictions, but instead sketched a brilliant but confounding figure who can’t seem to separate from his problems, particularly those that fueled his writing. Though suspicious by nature, he seems unable to sever bonds of trust and dependence, even after profound betrayals.

Diungkapkan bahwa though written gracefully, with characteristic ease, the review has its awkward notes. At times, a protective note creeps in. In Remnick’s words, the young Roth was “determined to live unfettered. ” As for Roth’s biographer, “Bailey is industrious, rigorous, and uncowed. ” In simple English, Roth slept with his students. We’re reminded of Roth’s “remarkable service” to writers and his “many close and enduring friendships with women. ” Translation: he shunned marriage and monogamy. As a middle-aged professor, Roth “availed himself of what he viewed as the perquisites. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, not everyone found bailey “uncowed. ” In the book, Roth’s first wife is branded “a bitter, impoverished, sexually undesirable divorcée. ” The critic Laura Marsh called him an “adoring wingman” and a misogynist. The New York Times noted Bailey’s “complicity” and found his book “a sprawling apologia for Roth’s treatment of women. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, before long, remnick’s endorsement would seem like one of the great critical misjudgments of the year. “Mein gott,” Remnick wrote Cynthia Ozick. He seemed shocked by Bailey’s undoing. “I don’t know what David was thinking,” an acquaintance of his (and Roth’s) told me. But he also feared Roth’s. In short order, Bailey was disgraced, his book withdrawn, following sexual assault charges. His chief concern, “in the unreal and unfortunate world of ‘one thing equals any other thing,’” was that Roth’s reputation might suffer.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he was right to worry. By 2021, a variety of factors, from #metoo to a broad reappraisal of the “great male narcissists” (as David Foster Wallace branded them), had tarnished Roth. Roth’s reputation was declining. In college courses, Roth went unassigned. But it wasn’t the defamation-by-association that Remnick feared. (At Yale University, Roth, Bellow, and Malamud had practically vanished from the syllabus. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, and yet, roth wasn’t cancelled—far from it. As of 2023, nearly all his novels remained in print. The academic journal Philip Roth Studies kept chugging along. Roth’s good name was still good enough for the New Jersey Performing Arts Center, which hosted “Philip Roth Unbound,” a three-day festival of panels and performances.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, indeed, roth’s place in literary history was fixed, as it had been since the 1970s. The New Yorker, on the other hand, had both prestige and a readership above a million. Why, then, had he needed the New Yorker? Despite his fame, Roth’s sales were generally modest; of his 32 books, very few were bestsellers. Indeed, it’s likely that more readers encountered Roth’s writing through the New Yorker than through his books.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but there was something roth needed more than readers and prizes. “He values complicity very highly,” his friend Judith Thurman once said. As time passed, Roth felt increasingly embattled—betrayed by friends, besieged by critics, brought low by illness. He was, said Thurman, “the greatest seeker of complicity as a friend. More and more, he sought allies, supporters, defenders. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa indeed, that’s what his literary allies provided: sympathy, at the deepest level; good company; unconditional loyalty. Their admiration was sincere. They sought favors and jacket blurbs. Yet many operated shrewdly. They exploited Roth’s connections, and eventually published memoirs quoting private letters and conversations. To accuse them of mere opportunism would be cynical. For decades, Roth suffered the curse of fame: everyone wanted something from him, if only proximity, a chance to bask in his celebrity.

Diungkapkan bahwa then there were the journalists. In return, he received access—the reporter’s holy grail—and Roth’s writing, a greater bounty of words than any other magazine. Remnick offered praise and the huge readership of the New Yorker. Both sides win—and lose—to varying degrees. In their strange pas de deus, journalists seduce subjects, who seduce them back. All the while, Remnick promoted “a literary genius” who managed to “portray Jews in all their human variety. With Roth and Remnick, there were only winners. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that sounds flattering, but in a curious way, it diminishes roth. After all, Roth didn’t merely “portray” Jewish Americans. ” We likely wouldn’t care about such a writer. Nor did he render anything so vague as their “humanity. In book after book, Roth probed, provoked, and pushed Jewish-America’s pressure points. He was a dangerous writer, his fiction fed by strong, dark emotions, chiefly anger—his lifelong muse and tormentor.

Diungkapkan bahwa even as remnick flattered and lionized roth, some part of him surely knew better. “He had lost, if only for a moment, his instinct for skepticism, his bullshit meter. Back in 1995, he faulted Ben Bradlee, his former boss at the Washington Post, for a lapse in judgement. ” Many years later, Remnick criticized Bradlee’s closeness to presidents and politicians.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i learned something from that,” remnick said, referring to journalists who befriend their famous subjects: “ultimately, they come and bite you in the ass. They can dull your judgement. They can compromise you. I’m very wary of it,” he added.

Sebagaimana diketahui, our report used open source research, freedom of information requests, and server infrastructure mapping to identify webloc customers in the us, el salvador, and hungary.
